title: fix(auth): collapse a repeated `iss` in the client redirect
body:
## Why

`build_client_redirect` promises "exactly one `iss`", but a registered redirect_uri can supply the parameter more than once. `replace_query_param` rewrites only the first match and leaves the rest, so `?iss=a&iss=b` came out as `iss=<issuer>&iss=b` -- two copies of a response parameter, which RFC 6749 §3.1 forbids.

```python
build_client_redirect(
    "https://client.example/cb?iss=a&iss=b",
    {"code": "abc", "state": "xyz"},
    iss="https://issuer.example/",
)
# before: ...?iss=https%3A%2F%2Fissuer.example%2F&iss=b&code=abc&state=xyz
# after : ...?iss=https%3A%2F%2Fissuer.example%2F&code=abc&state=xyz
```

## What changed

- `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/auth/redirect_validation.py`: new private `_drop_repeated_query_param()` keeps only the first occurrence of a key, and `build_client_redirect` applies it after `replace_query_param` -- so every call site gets the invariant the docstring already claimed. It is byte-preserving like its siblings: only the duplicate segments are removed, everything else passes through verbatim.
- `tests/server/auth/test_redirect_validation.py`: two tests -- the reported `?iss=a&iss=b` case, and one asserting a valueless `flag` plus a non-UTF-8 `sig` survive untouched while the duplicate goes.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/server/auth/test_redirect_validation.py`: 62 passed.
- Both new tests fail with the source hunk stashed and pass with it applied (verified, not assumed).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both touched files.

Fixes #6297

title: fix(auth): preserve empty authority on custom-scheme redirect URIs
body:
## Description

When a native OAuth client registers a custom-scheme `redirect_uri` with an empty authority (such as `myapp://` or `myapp:///callback`), `add_query_params()` and `replace_query_param()` in `fastmcp/server/auth/redirect_validation.py` re-serialize the parsed URL using `urllib.parse.urlunparse()`. Because custom native-app schemes are not registered in `urllib.parse.uses_netloc`, `urlunparse()` strips the empty `//` authority when `netloc == ""`, turning `myapp://` into `myapp:?code=...` and `myapp:///callback` into `myapp:/callback?code=...`.

This PR adds a `_set_query()` helper that restores the empty `//` authority when `not parsed.netloc` and the input URI started with `<scheme>://`, while leaving scheme-only URIs (`com.example.app:/callback`) and host-bearing URIs (`myapp://callback`) unchanged.

Closes #6296

title: Send {} for required OpenAPI object bodies with no fields
body:
`FastMCP.from_openapi` drops a required `application/json` object body when every property is optional and the caller supplies none. The request goes out as empty bytes with no `Content-Type`, and APIs that require a JSON body reject that otherwise valid call.

The request director now sends that omitted object as `{}` with `application/json`. An optional body is still left off the request, and a call that sets a property still sends that object.

```python
await client.call_tool("search", {})
# before: b"" with no Content-Type
# after:  b"{}" with application/json
```

title: fix(auth): accept private-use scheme redirect URIs in CIMD documents
body:
## Description

`CIMDDocument` requires every `redirect_uris` entry to have a host, with `urn:` as the only exemption. RFC 8252 §7.1 private-use schemes such as `com.example.app:/oauth` have no host, so one of them makes the whole document invalid. The proxy then logs "CIMD fetch failed", the client resolves as not registered, and `/authorize` fails even though the server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported`. Raycast's client document lists `com.raycast:/oauth`, so any `OAuthProxy` with CIMD enabled (the default) rejects it. The `application_type="native"` docs already list `com.example.app:/callback` as an allowed redirect.

The host requirement now applies only to `http` and `https`. Matching at authorization is unchanged, and `matches_allowed_pattern` still refuses unsafe schemes such as `javascript:`.

```python
CIMDDocument(
    client_id="https://example.com/client.json",
    redirect_uris=["com.example.app:/oauth"],  # previously: "must have a host"
)
```

Fixes #6336

Written with AI assistance (Claude).

title: fix: versionless fallback lookup must not see a mounted server's list middleware
body:
Fixes #6301

## Summary

When the highest version of a component is disabled, a versionless lookup (`get_tool` / `get_resource` / `get_resource_template` / `get_prompt` with no explicit version) falls back to enumerating the remaining versions. That enumeration went through the **normal list path**, which for a mounted server runs the mounted server's middleware. A middleware that filters listings (e.g. an `on_list_prompts` hook returning `[]`, as AuthMiddleware does) therefore emptied the fallback's candidate list, and the lookup failed with `Unknown prompt` / `Unknown tool` instead of serving the next-highest enabled version promised by the `get_*` docstrings.

## Changes

Adds a fallback enumeration channel `list_*_all_versions` on `Provider` (tools, resources, resource templates, prompts):

- **Default implementation**: forwards to the regular list path — no behavior change for any existing provider.
- **`AggregateProvider`**: forwards the channel to each child provider.
- **`FastMCPProvider`** (a mounted server): enumerates the nested server with `run_middleware=False`, so list-filtering middleware on the child cannot hide versions from a lookup. The nested server's core listing logic still applies disabled filtering and component-level auth; the parent's own transforms (including the parent's visibility/disable rules) still run on the enumeration result.
- **`server.py`**: the four fallback call sites now enumerate via the new channel.

Regular listings are unchanged: a mounted server's list middleware still applies when the parent serves `prompts/list`, `tools/list`, etc. (the existing `test_list_skips_failing_mount_by_default` coverage confirms the middleware still runs on the list path).

## Testing

Reproduced the issue scenario on `main`: `prompts/get greet` → `Unknown prompt: 'greet'`.

After the fix, the issue's script prints:

- `prompts/get greet -> hello from v1` (v2 disabled by the parent, v1 served)
- connecting directly to the child still serves v2

Test suites run locally: `tests/server/mount/test_mount.py` + `tests/server/middleware/test_middleware_nested.py` → 44 passed, 2 failed pre-existing on baseline (verified by stashing: same 2 failures without this change); `tests/server/versioning/` + `tests/server/providers/test_fastmcp_provider.py` + `test_base_provider.py` → **145 passed**.

title: fix(elicitation): add items.type=string to multi-select list shorthand
body:
Fixes #6300

## Summary

The `[["a", "b"]]` shorthand for multi-select elicitation sends the property schema `{"type": "array", "items": {"enum": [...]}}` — missing the required `"type": "string"` inside `items`. The MCP 2025-11-25 protocol schema defines the multi-select enum schema's `items` as `{ type: "string"; enum: string[] }` with `type` required, so strict clients (official TypeScript SDK, MCP Inspector) reject the request with a zod `invalid_union` error before it ever reaches the handler (what #3731 saw).

The `list[Literal[...]]` form already sends `"items": {"type": "string", "enum": [...]}`. This PR makes the nested-list shorthand produce the same schema.

## Changes

- `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/elicitation.py` (`_parse_list_syntax`): the `[["a", "b"]]` branch now emits `"items": {"type": "string", "enum": [...]}`.
- The titled multi-select path (`[{"low": {...}}]` → `anyOf`) is unchanged: SEP-1330 requires the anyOf pattern there, and the 2025-11-25 multi-select *group* schema has no `items.type` requirement.

## Testing

Reproduced both paths on `main` with a real legacy `Client` (matching the issue's example): `[[...]]` sent `{'enum': [...]}` (invalid per the 2025-11-25 model), `list[Literal[...]]` sent `{'enum': [...], 'type': 'string'}`.

After the fix, verified on this branch:

- `[["red", "blue"]]` → `{'type': 'string', 'enum': ['red', 'blue']}` — identical to the `list[Literal[...]]` output
- titled path unchanged: `{'anyOf': [{'const': 'low', 'title': 'Low'}]}`
- `pytest tests/client/test_elicitation_enums.py tests/client/test_elicitation.py`: **66 passed**, 2 failed pre-existing on baseline due to a local env issue (`No module named 'jsonref'`, unrelated to this change — verified by stashing and re-running).

title: fix(client): keep the response cache inert on legacy connections (#6298)
body:
## Description

Closes #6298.

On a `mode="legacy"` connection, a `CacheConfig` that sets `default_ttl_ms` made the response cache active, so a second `list_tools()` was answered from the cache and a tool registered in between never appeared. The docs say the opposite ("a cache is inert on a legacy connection"), and `cache=None`, `cache=True`, and the same `CacheConfig` in the default mode all behave correctly.

The cause: `Client._call_with_cache` gated the cache on whether a `CacheConfig` was passed, not on the negotiated protocol version. `CacheConfig` carries both a TTL and a top-level enabled flag, so constructing one with only `default_ttl_ms` left the legacy connection with a live, writable cache.

The fix is two lines in `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/client.py` (lines 1357-1358), inside `_call_with_cache`, right after the closed-client guard and before the cursor continuation-page branch:

```python
if self.protocol_version not in MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS:
    return await send()
```

Legacy connections now skip both the cache read and the cache write on every list path. `MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` is already imported at line 57 and used for the same kind of gating at lines 461 and 1557.

`tests/client/client/test_response_cache.py` (lines 164-194) adds `TestEraGating::test_legacy_with_default_ttl_cache_is_inert`: it asserts that nothing is written into the cache after a `list_tools()` on a legacy connection, and that a manually populated cache is ignored - the wire request still happens and the server answer wins. The second assertion is independent of the first, so the test still fails if only one half of the gate is fixed.

title: Normalize raw-string redirect URIs through AnyUrl before validation
body:
Fixes #6295

## User-visible change

A plain-string redirect URI validated differently than the same URI passed as `AnyUrl`. `AnyUrl` applies WHATWG-style normalization (backslash in the authority becomes a path separator, `..` segments are resolved, IPv4 shorthand like `127.1` is expanded, trailing C0 characters are stripped), while raw strings went straight to `urlparse`. An attacker-controlled spelling such as `https://evil.com\.example.com/cb` therefore matched the allowlist pattern `https://*.example.com/*` in its raw form but not its parsed form -- and the raw form is the one emitted in the redirect. The same divergence affected `https://127.1/cb` ("web" clients) and `http://evil.com\.localhost/cb` ("native" clients) through `is_redirect_uri_allowed_for_application_type`.

Raw strings are now re-parsed through `AnyUrl` in `matches_allowed_pattern` and `is_redirect_uri_allowed_for_application_type` (with a pass-through fallback for schemes pydantic cannot express, so custom schemes like `com.example.app:/callback` and `urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob` keep their existing classification). The built-in OAuthProxy DCR/authorize paths already pass `AnyUrl` and are unchanged.

## Dot-segment rejection preserved

`AnyUrl` normalization resolves `.` and `..` segments away, so a normalized-only check would turn a rejected traversal spelling into an ordinary matching path. `matches_allowed_pattern` now applies `_has_dot_segments` to both the raw and the normalized path; all existing `TestDotSegmentBypass` cases still pass.

## Testing

- Reproduced the issue's five examples against unchanged code: raw form accepted, `AnyUrl` form rejected; after the fix both forms are rejected.
- Added `TestRawStringNormalization` (10 cases): issue examples for all three public helpers, custom-scheme pass-through, and a guard that dot-segment rejection survives normalization.
- Full upstream `tests/server/auth/test_redirect_validation.py`: 68/68 pass, verified under pydantic 2.13.4 and 2.14.2.
- `ruff format` clean; `ruff check` (E4/E7/E9/F) clean on the changed file.

Full-suite CI is the final gate.

## Note

This PR was written by an AI agent (WorkBuddy) operating on behalf of @uhhgxg. Per the contributing guide's gate: not yet assigned to #6295, so this PR may be closed by the require-issue-link workflow until a maintainer assigns -- it will reopen on assignment, and I'll update it in place rather than opening a duplicate.

title: fix(agentic): suppress equivalent public triage feedback
body:
#6075 received four substantively equivalent triage reviews as the target baseline advanced and main was merged into the PR. Keep fresh head/baseline verification and independent review, but separate that evidence from public feedback identity: an explicit outcome and stable finding identities determine whether the latest intact bot review already says the same thing. New, resolved or materially changed findings still produce feedback; ambiguous, legacy, dismissed and edited reviews cannot authorize suppression.

Suppressed delivery retains `unchanged_feedback` with `verified_head_sha` and `verified_baseline_sha`, plus a separate historical `previous_review` receipt. It does not count the old review as a publication on the new revision. title: Fix version fallback through mounted servers with list-filtering middleware
body:
Fixes #6301

**Problem**

When a parent server mounts a child that has list-filtering middleware (a middleware whose `on_list_*` hooks hide components from listings — `AuthMiddleware` filters lists the same way), versionless lookups through the mount fail instead of falling back: with v2 disabled on the parent, `client.get_prompt("greet")` returns `Unknown prompt: 'greet'` and `parent.get_prompt("greet")` returns `None`, even though v1 is enabled. Tools, resources, and resource templates behave the same way. Without the child middleware, v1 is served as documented.

**Root cause**

The version fallback in `FastMCP.get_tool` / `get_prompt` / `get_resource` / `get_resource_template` enumerated its candidates by listing (`super().list_*()`). Through a mount, that listing runs the child server's list middleware, so a lookup silently depended on listing output — and list middleware is allowed to hide components that lookups must still resolve.

**Change**

The four fallback paths now probe successively lower versions with get calls (`VersionSpec(lt=…)`), applying the same session transforms, enabled check, and component-auth check per candidate as before (including the hashed-lookup identity restriction for tools). When the server-level get withholds the highest matching version for component auth, the probe learns that version from the raw aggregate result and continues below it, so unauthorized versions are skipped rather than terminal. A rejected-version set guarantees the probe terminates even if a provider's get does not narrow by spec. Listing behavior is unchanged — a mounted child's list middleware still filters the parent's listings exactly as before.

**Tests**

- New regression class `TestFallbackThroughMountWithListFilteringMiddleware` in `tests/server/versioning/test_visibility_version_fallback.py`: through-mount fallback for prompts, tools (including `call_tool` end-to-end), resources, and resource templates with a child middleware that empties every listing, plus a test pinning that listings through the mount remain filtered. The four fallback tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- `tests/server/versioning` (incl. the existing visibility-fallback and auth-fallback contracts), `tests/server/mount`, `tests/server/middleware`, `tests/server/transforms`, and `tests/server/providers/test_catalog_tool_names.py` pass. (The proxy/HTTP and auth suites show pre-existing, environment-dependent failures in my sandbox that are identical on unmodified `main`.)

**Compatibility**

Only versionless lookups whose highest version is rejected change resolution strategy; listings, explicit-version lookups, and execution are untouched. One disclosed corner: per version step the probe evaluates the aggregate's chosen representative, so duplicate components sharing both name and version across providers with divergent visibility are no longer distinguished the way full enumeration distinguished them.

Co-authored-by: Alperen Keleş <19610315+alpaylan@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Accept structured skill metadata and allowed-tools lists
body:
Right now a lot of popular skills quietly vanish from `skills/list` because their frontmatter doesn't pass our checks on `metadata` and `allowed-tools`. The only trace is a warning in the server log.

A few examples:

- Vercel's `vercel-plugin` uses `metadata` for real config: `priority: 5`, plus lists of file patterns its hooks match on. 38 of its 55 skills get dropped.
- Stripe's and Salesforce's Codex plugins, and Anthropic's own Discord/Telegram/iMessage plugins, write `allowed-tools` as a YAML list instead of one string.

To be fair, the Agent Skills spec does say both should be strings. But skills-ref (the spec's own reference validator) doesn't reject either one, and Claude Code and Codex load these skills just fine. So we end up stricter than basically everyone else.

This PR lets `metadata` values be any JSON and lets `allowed-tools` be a string or a list of strings. We pass them through untouched rather than converting them to strings, since SEP-2640 has hosts check that the frontmatter we serve matches the actual `SKILL.md`.

When a skill does either of these, we log it at info level when its `SKILL.md` is read, so there's still a trail without blocking anything.

Everything else stays strict (name, description, license, compatibility, and `metadata` still has to be a mapping). One heads-up: the `.metadata` and `.allowed_tools` properties now return the wider types.

title: fix(search): include tool identity in BM25 catalog hash to detect renames (#6284)
body:
### Summary
Closes #6284

When a tool was renamed in a way that preserved its combined searchable text (e.g. `foo` with description `bar` renamed to `foo bar` with no description), `_catalog_hash` produced an identical SHA256 hash because it hashed only `sorted(_extract_searchable_text(t) for t in tools)`. As a result, `BM25SearchTransform` skipped rebuilding its index and kept stale `_indexed_names`, causing subsequent queries to raise `KeyError: 'foo'` when resolving matching document indices against `tools_by_name`.

This PR:
1. Updates `_catalog_hash` to include tool name, version, and searchable text: `sorted((t.name, getattr(t, "version", None), _extract_searchable_text(t)) for t in tools)`. Any tool rename or version change produces a new hash, forcing an index rebuild.
2. Resolves tools in `_search` defensively using `tools_by_name.get(self._indexed_names[i])` to guard against missing names.
3. Adds regression tests verifying that catalog hash differentiates tools after a rename preserving searchable text, and that `_search` correctly resolves renamed tools without `KeyError`.

### Tests
- Unit test: `test_hash_differs_when_tool_renamed_preserving_searchable_text`
- Unit test: `test_search_after_rename_preserving_searchable_text`
- Full test suite: 192/192 transform tests passing.

title: fix(client): preserve class identity for mutually recursive schemas in result.data (fixes #6135)
body:
Fixes #6135. Reported by @alpaylan.

When a tool returns mutually recursive Pydantic models (e.g. `Person.pet: Pet | None` and `Pet.owner: Person | None`), FastMCP's schema generation inlines the root model into `output_schema` and compresses it with `prune_titles=True`, leaving mutually referenced models in `$defs` without explicit `title` attributes. This caused nested models to fall back to generic `"Root"` class names, collide, and fail to hydrate correctly in `result.data`.

This PR extracts definition names from `$ref` pointer paths when `title` is missing, matches root schema properties against `$defs` to identify recursive candidates, propagates resolved names during schema hydration, and manages class registration in module globals with LRU cache eviction cleanup.

title: fix(tools): keep hidden parameter factories out of visible defaults
body:
Fixes #6285

## Summary

`TransformedTool.run` fills missing arguments from the schema defaults and gives any `ArgTransform.default_factory` precedence. But `default_factory` requires `hide=True` (enforced in `ArgTransform.__post_init__`), and hidden parameters never appear in the transformed schema, so the factory branch can only fire when a hidden parameter is renamed to a visible sibling's name — which the conflict check explicitly skips.

In that case the visible parameter silently receives the hidden one's factory value instead of its documented schema default:

```python
@Tool.from_function
def base(x: str = "x-default", y: str = "y-default") -> str:
    return f"{x}|{y}"

tool = Tool.from_tool(base, transform_args={
    "x": ArgTransform(name="y", hide=True, default_factory=lambda: "factory"),
})
await tool.run({})  # -> "factory|factory"; the schema promised y == "y-default"
```

The fix skips hidden transforms in the default-fill loop. Hidden factories are already applied under their original name when forwarding to the parent (`hidden_defaults` in `_create_forwarding_transform`), so no behavior is lost.

## Test plan

- New regression test `test_hidden_rename_does_not_leak_factory_into_visible_sibling`: asserts `tool.run({})` returns `"factory|y-default"` — fails without the fix (`"factory|factory"`), passes with it
- `pytest tests/tools/tool_transform/test_args.py`: 28 passed
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: the touched files are clean (one pre-existing RUF036 elsewhere in `tool_transform.py`, unrelated to this change)

title: fix(search): rebuild the BM25 index when the tool name set changes
body:
Fixes #6284

## Summary

`_catalog_hash` only hashed the searchable text multiset, while `_indexed_names` caches tool names. A rename that leaves the searchable text unchanged — e.g. tool `"foo"` with description `"bar"` becomes a tool named `"foo bar"` — keeps the hash identical, so the index is not rebuilt and the stale name list survives. The next search then resolves a cached name against the new catalog:

```
tools_by_name[self._indexed_names[i]]  # KeyError: 'foo'
```

and the `search_tools` call fails with an internal error. Dynamic providers that regenerate or rename tools between searches can hit this.

The fix includes the tool names in the hash input (`sorted((t.name, text) ...)`), so any name-set change forces a rebuild.

title: fix(provider): isolate component construction failures in FileSystemProvider (fixes #6209)
body:
### Summary
Closes #6209.

When standalone decorators are converted into components via `extract_components(module)`, signature inspection or type validation errors (such as an unsupported `*args` signature on `@tool` or prompt) raised unhandled exceptions outside `discover_and_import()`.

In `FileSystemProvider`, this caused:
1. Constructor crashes at startup when an invalid file was present in the scanned directory.
2. Healthy tools to disappear on reload when introducing an invalid file, while leaving `provider.failed_files` empty because the exception escaped before `result.failed_files` could be populated.

### Changes
1. **Per-file component conversion isolation**: Wrapped `extract_components(module)` in `try...except Exception as e:` inside `discover_and_import()`, recording any failure in `result.failed_files[file_path]` and allowing discovery to continue for remaining healthy files.
2. **Safe reload clearing**: In `FileSystemProvider._load_components()`, deferred clearing `self._components` until after `discover_and_import()` returns so component state is not wiped prematurely.
3. **Regression tests**:
   - Added `test_discover_and_import_skips_component_construction_failures` in `tests/fs/test_discovery.py`.
   - Added `test_provider_isolates_component_construction_failures` in `tests/fs/test_provider.py` verifying that invalid files do not hide healthy tools on reload and are properly tracked in `provider.failed_files`.

This adds `SkillsDirectoryProvider(roots, *, reload=False)` to `fastmcp.skills.provider`, a thin `SkillCatalogProvider` that loads every skill folder below its roots with `Skill.from_directory` and serves them at their relative paths.

from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.skills.provider import SkillsDirectoryProvider

mcp = FastMCP("Skills", providers=[SkillsDirectoryProvider(Path.home() / ".claude" / "skills")])

#   to 'pdf-tools' and start SKILL.md with '---\nname: pdf-tools\ndescription: <...>\n---'

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WM1d5rTFoBi2Hm3niULv61Y)_

## Description

FastMCP has two skills stacks: the resource-only one from 3.x and 4.1 (`fastmcp.server.providers.skills`, `fastmcp.utilities.skills`) and the skills-extension one in `fastmcp.skills`. The new one was bolted onto the old through `experimental_skills=True`, so every skills bug had two homes. This makes the new stack the only real implementation and puts the old one on a one-minor deprecation clock. The old API shipped in stable releases, so in 4.2 it keeps its 4.1 behavior and warns; it goes in 4.3. Only things introduced in the 4.2 alphas, plus the documented-as-changeable `experimental_skills`, change without a warning.

The new `SkillsDirectoryProvider(roots, *, reload=False)` in `fastmcp.skills.provider` stops the server at startup if any folder isn't a valid [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/specification), with one fix per folder. Each old directory provider's warning runs the same check, so a user (or their agent) sees exactly what to rename before switching:

```text
FastMCPDeprecationWarning: `ClaudeSkillsProvider` is deprecated and will be removed in FastMCP 4.3.
Replace it with `from fastmcp.skills.provider import SkillsDirectoryProvider` and
`SkillsDirectoryProvider(['/home/me/.claude/skills'])`. ... Fix these folders first:
- /home/me/.claude/skills/pdf_tools: SKILL.md must begin with YAML frontmatter. Fix: rename the
  folder to 'pdf-tools' and start SKILL.md with '---\nname: pdf-tools\ndescription: <...>\n---'
```

<details><summary>What changes, by when it shipped</summary>

Stable since 3.0, warn in 4.2, removed in 4.3, behavior unchanged: `SkillsDirectoryProvider`, `SkillProvider` and the eight vendor presets from `fastmcp.server.providers.skills` (and the names re-exported from `fastmcp.server.providers`), and `list_skills`, `get_skill_manifest`, `download_skill`, `sync_skills` from `fastmcp.utilities.skills`.

Experimental since 4.1.2, documented as changeable: `SkillsDirectoryProvider(..., experimental_skills=True)` now returns the new provider with a warning, so invalid folders fail at startup instead of being skipped.

4.2 alpha only, changed freely: `list_skill_summaries` is gone, `fastmcp.skills` internals were trimmed, and the new provider is strict.

</details>

<details><summary>Who this reaches</summary>

GitHub code search finds roughly 100 to 140 repos importing the old modules, mostly small. Upgrading to 4.2 breaks none of them; they get a warning. Of the 15 with reach we checked, 6 (OpenBB, PyWry, xknx-editor, evergreen, openbridge, calibremcp) have folders the new provider would refuse, so they need the listed renames or frontmatter before 4.3. The downstream smoke consumers (agno, Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents) don't use skills.

</details>

`ClientGroup` dropped its tool routes on the last context exit, so a tool resolved inside the group couldn't be called later with only its own client connected: `call_tool()` fell back to discovery and required every member. Known routes now survive the exit, and the catalog is marked for lazy rediscovery, so an unknown name after a reconnect still reloads it.

```python
async with group:
    route = await group.resolve_tool("calc_add")

async with route.client:
    await group.call_tool("calc_add", {"a": 1, "b": 2})  # previously: 'greet' is not connected
```

Keeping the routes but not the loaded flag means a new tool added between sessions is still found without an explicit `list_tools()`, which matches the old reconnect behavior. A tool removed between sessions now fails at the server rather than locally until `list_tools()` refreshes the catalog, the same as a removal within one session. Tests cover the MRE (fails on main), lazy rediscovery after reconnect, and discovery still requiring every client. Thanks to @YingzuoLiu for the root-cause analysis on the issue.

title: Accept alternate OpenAPI JSON success responses
body:
An OpenAPI POST can return a declared `202` job identifier after executing successfully, but FastMCP advertises only its primary `200` schema. MCP clients then reject the successful result. Include the other declared JSON 2xx responses in an `anyOf` output schema, keeping error and `default` responses out. Preserve bodiless-success handling and each response's local references.

The primary response keeps its existing wire format, and `validate_output=False` keeps its previous behavior. For operations with distinct object response schemas, FastMCP's inferred `.data` becomes a dictionary instead of the primary response's dataclass: use `result.data["report_id"]` rather than `result.data.report_id`. Single or identical response schemas are unchanged; the documentation describes mixed object/non-object wrapping as well.

Fixes #6265

title: fix(client): keep shared keep_alive=False stdio subprocess until the last client exits
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

This carries #5226 forward with maintainer finishing touches, keeping the original commits and authorship. Closes #5179.

A `keep_alive=False` stdio transport stops its subprocess whenever any session on it exits, even with other clients still connected. That is reachable through `create_proxy(StdioTransport(..., keep_alive=False))`, which opens a fresh client on the transport for each request, so one request finishing closes the subprocess under every request still in flight. #5180 fixed this by taking the connect lock during session cleanup, and #5219 reverted it because cleanup that runs during cancellation or garbage collection must not wait on a lock. The fix here takes no lock: the last session out signals stop synchronously, a new `connect()` that sees the stop signal waits for shutdown under the lock it already holds, and a late `disconnect()` resets only the connection it waited for, so it can't clear a replacement.

```python
transport = PythonStdioTransport("server.py", keep_alive=False)
async with Client(transport) as first:
    async with Client(transport) as second:
        pid = (await second.call_tool("pid")).data
    await first.call_tool("pid")  # same pid; before: MCPError("Connection closed")
# the subprocess exits here, after the last client
```

On top of #5226, the tests cover each #5219 regression with a real subprocess. The new tests are a cancelled scope exiting every shared session, a proxy request finishing beside a connected backend client, and an abandoned `Client` garbage-collected with its session task still pending, which must not wedge later Clients or `create_proxy` calls. On today's main, #5223 releases a cancelled `Client`'s hold in its own task, so the collected-client test is the one that still catches #5180's lock-based cleanup. It fails against both #5180 and #5180 plus #5215, and #5219's original wedge test no longer does. The transport docs no longer claim that `keep_alive=False` isolates connections, and the stdio `keep_alive` docstrings describe last-client-out shutdown.

_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

`dereference_refs` treated every `$ref` key in a schema as a reference, including the ones inside instance data. A tool whose default is `{"$ref": "https://example.com/customer.json"}` advertised `{}` because the remote-ref stripping recursed into `default`. A literal local value such as `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Text"}` was worse: jsonref replaced it with the definition. In both cases the advertised `default`, `const`, `enum`, or `examples` value no longer matched what the tool actually uses.

Values under those keywords are now copied unchanged. Before the jsonref pass they are wrapped in an opaque holder that jsonref passes through untouched, then unwrapped before the post-inline size check, so the expansion limits still count them. Properties named `default` or `enum` are still treated as sub-schemas, and remote references in schema positions are still stripped before anything is resolved.

```python
@server.tool
def describe_schema(
    config: Annotated[dict[str, Any], Field(default={"$ref": "https://example.com/customer.json"})],
) -> dict[str, Any]: ...

# advertised default before: {}
# advertised default after:  {"$ref": "https://example.com/customer.json"}
```

Closes #5644.

title: fix(client): report a lost connection instead of 'Client is not connected'
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

When an HTTP server goes away, the client's session runner clears its session as soon as the transport cancels it, then keeps unwinding while the transport tries its termination request. A call started in that window, still inside `async with client`, hit the `session` property's "Client is not connected. Use the 'async with client:' context manager first." error, which points at a mistake the caller never made. `ping()`, which reads `session` before session monitoring sees the dead runner, got that error even after the runner had finished.

The `session` property now tells the two cases apart: when a context is still held and the session task exists, a missing session means the connection was lost. It raises the transport's own failure once the runner has finished (what `_await_with_session_monitoring` already raises for other calls), and the SDK's `MCPError` "Connection closed" while it is still unwinding, the same error the in-flight call receives. Outside a context the old "not connected" message is unchanged.

```python
async with Client(url) as client:
    ...  # server dies
    await client.call_tool("echo", {"text": "b"})
    # before: RuntimeError: Client is not connected. Use the 'async with client:' ...
    # after:  MCPError: Connection closed
```

Closes #6162.

title: fix(server): run lifespan teardown on SIGTERM for HTTP servers
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

`mcp.run(transport="http")` holds the FastMCP lifespan open around `uvicorn.Server.serve()`, so user teardown only ran once `serve()` returned. When a signal stops the server, Uvicorn finishes its own shutdown and then replays the signal before `serve()` returns. For SIGTERM, which Docker, Kubernetes and Cloud Run all send, the default action kills the process right there, so lifespan teardown never ran even though Uvicorn had logged "Application shutdown complete". SIGINT fared only a little better: the replayed `KeyboardInterrupt` cut async teardown short.

Lifespan teardown now runs as the last step of Uvicorn's shutdown, after connections drain and the ASGI lifespan has exited, and before the signal is replayed. The outer lifespan entry still owns startup, so a failing lifespan raises its own exception before the port binds, and cancelling the serving task still tears down through the same block. This covers HTTP and SSE; stdio has no Uvicorn shutdown and is not changed here.

```python
@lifespan
async def app_lifespan(server):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        yield {"http_client": client}  # now closed on `docker stop`, not just Ctrl+C

mcp = FastMCP("My server", lifespan=app_lifespan)
mcp.run(transport="http")
```

Closes #4927.

Co-authored-by: Aztec03hub <19616323+Aztec03hub@users.noreply.github.com>

title: fix(middleware): map exception subclasses in ErrorHandlingMiddleware
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

With `ErrorHandlingMiddleware` installed, a tool call with bad arguments comes back as `-32603 Internal error`. The tool layer raises `fastmcp.exceptions.ValidationError` chained from pydantic's `ValidationError`, the middleware classifies by that cause, and it compared types with `in (ValueError, TypeError, ...)`. Pydantic's `ValidationError` is a `ValueError` subclass, not `ValueError` itself, so it fell through to the internal-error branch. The client is told the server broke when the client sent bad input.

Classification now uses `issubclass` for every mapped family, so a subclass gets the same code as its base. Argument validation failures report `-32602 Invalid params`. Other subclasses that were landing on `-32603` move to their family's code as well, for example `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`) and `ResourceSecurityError` (a `NotFoundError`).

```python
mcp = FastMCP(middleware=[ErrorHandlingMiddleware()])

@mcp.tool
def concat(a: str, b: str) -> str: ...

await client.call_tool("concat", {"wrong": "x"})
# before: MCPError -32603 "Internal error: 3 validation errors for call[concat] ..."
# after:  MCPError -32602 "Invalid params: 3 validation errors for call[concat] ..."
```

Closes #1606.

title: fix(openapi): keep both values when a query object property matches another parameter
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

A `form`/`explode=true` object query parameter puts its properties into the query string as bare keys, so a property can share a name with another declared parameter. The serializer wrote every value into one dict keyed by query name. That meant `filter={"q": 1}` together with `q=false` sent only whichever value was processed last, and the result depended on argument order. OpenAPI treats a route's form parameters as one RFC 6570 variable list (`{?filter*,q}`), so both values belong on the wire.

Every serializer branch now goes through a single `add` step that repeats the key when a name is already taken, instead of overwriting it. This covers exploded and non-exploded arrays and objects as well as plain values, so no branch can still drop a value depending on order. Serialization without collisions is unchanged.

```python
await client.call_tool("list_items", {"filter": {"q": 1}, "q": False})
# before: ?q=false
# after:  ?q=1&q=false
```

Closes #6149.

title: docs(settings): explain what FASTMCP_DEBUG actually does
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

The settings page described `FASTMCP_DEBUG` as "Enable debug mode", which reads as FastMCP debugging. All it does is pass `debug=True` to the Starlette app behind the Streamable HTTP and SSE transports, so unhandled HTTP-layer errors return tracebacks. It does nothing on stdio and doesn't touch the log level. The row now says that, points to `FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` for debug logs, and warns against using it in production.

The issue also asked how to wire a `--debug` flag into a custom entry point without calling `configure_logging()` again. The Logging section now shows `mcp.run(log_level="DEBUG")`, which applies on every transport. Renaming or redefining the setting, as the closed #2908 draft tried, is a separate enhancement; this PR only documents current behavior.

Closes #2860.

title: fix(client): identify as fastmcp in clientInfo by default
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

A FastMCP `Client` that isn't given `client_info` falls through to the SDK's placeholder, so every server it talks to sees `{"name": "mcp", "version": "0.1.0"}`. That identity tells a server nothing: it isn't FastMCP, and the version never moves. The server side already reports `fastmcp.__version__` in its own `serverInfo`, so the client should do the same.

The client now defaults `client_info` to `Implementation(name="fastmcp", version=fastmcp.__version__)` on both the legacy handshake and modern discovery paths. An explicit `client_info` still wins, and the client docs now say what's sent and how to override it.

```python
async with Client("https://example.com/mcp") as client:
    ...
# server sees: before {"name": "mcp", "version": "0.1.0"}
#              after  {"name": "fastmcp", "version": "4.2.0"}
```

Closes #1367.

title: fix(openapi): serialize label and matrix path parameter styles
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

The OpenAPI request director serialized every path parameter in the `simple` style, ignoring the `style` it parsed from the spec. A route declaring `style: label` or `style: matrix` therefore got `/items/blue` instead of `/items/.blue` or `/items/;color=blue`, so servers that route on those prefixes never matched. Path serialization now follows the declared style for scalars, arrays, and objects, with and without `explode`, per the OAS style table. `simple` output is unchanged.

Each item is still encoded separately, so the style delimiters (`.`, `;`, `,`, `=`) stay literal while the same characters inside values are percent-encoded. A `label` value that would serialize to a bare `.` (an empty string or empty array) is rejected, because a server would normalize it away as a dot segment.

```python
# parameters: [{"name": "color", "in": "path", "style": "matrix", "explode": True, ...}]
await client.call_tool("get_items", {"color": ["blue", "black"]})
# before: GET /items/blue,black
# after:  GET /items/;color=blue;color=black
```

Closes #5856.

title: fix(telemetry): record mounted and nested server spans as INTERNAL
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

A tool call through a mounted server produced two `SERVER` spans, one for the parent and one for the child, so backends that count `SERVER` spans as requests (App Insights, Azure Monitor) counted every mounted call twice. The same happened when a tool called `ctx.fastmcp.call_tool`. Now `server_span` marks the request once it has enriched the seam span or opened the `SERVER` span, and any `server_span` nested in that request opens an `INTERNAL` span under the current one. `seam_span` clears the mark, so an in-process `ProxyClient` backend still gets its own `SERVER` span, since that really is a new inbound request.

This also stops a nested call from re-enriching the still-active seam span (a parent `tools/list` used to come out tagged with the child's `fastmcp.server.name`), and parents the nested span on the `delegate` span instead of the remote caller's `_meta` traceparent. Anyone filtering on `kind == SERVER` to find a mounted child's span should filter on `fastmcp.server.name` or the span name instead; the telemetry docs diagram is updated to match.

```
tools/call sub_hello (SERVER, parent)
  └── delegate hello (INTERNAL)
        └── tools/call hello (INTERNAL, sub)   ← was SERVER
```

This carries forward #5279, which was closed without merging.

Closes #5268.

Co-authored-by: sonmaximum <13666301+sonmaximum@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Add the gofastmcp.com homepage and move the docs under /docs
body:
## Summary

gofastmcp.com today is the Mintlify docs at the domain root. This adds a homepage for the project and moves the docs under `/docs`, so the domain can grow other pages the way nextjs.org does.

- **`website/`**: a small Next.js app that owns the domain root and proxies the Mintlify docs from `fastmcp.mintlify.site/docs/*`, the same arrangement prefect.io uses for its docs. It follows the Prefect design system (Articulat CF loaded from prefect.io so the licensed font is not committed here, DM Mono, the Night palette and website type ramp) and leads with the open source project: install line, the README server, live GitHub and PyPI numbers, eight docs-linked capability cards, the three pillars, a section on building with coding agents (llms.txt, the docs MCP server, the `fastmcp-server` skill, and the agent setup guide on prefect.io), a Get Started grid of docs guides, community links and recent MCP posts from the Prefect blog. FastMCP Gateway appears in the nav Deploy button, the Deploy lane and the closing CTA.
- **Docs move** (separate commit): every docs section that lived at the root 308s to its `/docs` counterpart, section by section rather than as a catch-all so future root pages are never shadowed. Agent-facing files keep their root URLs (`/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, `/mcp`, `/.well-known/mcp*`, `/skill.md`, `/.well-known/skills/*`) through rewrites, since MCP clients do not reliably follow redirects. The docs logo links back to the homepage.
- **Telemetry** (separate commit): the same `@amplitude/analytics-browser` setup as prefect.io and `docs/fastmcp-analytics.js`, reporting to the shared Prefect project through a same-origin `/api/t` proxy. Page views, CTA clicks, docs link clicks and outbound clicks, each stamped with its section; links to Prefect domains carry the device id. Off in `next dev` and for GPC/DNT visitors.
- `pyproject.toml`: codespell skips `website/bun.lock`, which is full of third-party package names.

## Cutover (outside this PR)

The code is ready before the domain moves. `website/README.md` has the checklist:

1. Vercel project for this repo with Root Directory `website`.
2. Mintlify dashboard: Custom domain, enable **Host at**, domain `gofastmcp.com`, base path `docs`.
3. Point `gofastmcp.com` at the Vercel project.
4. Smoke test `/`, `/docs`, an old path such as `/getting-started/quickstart` (expect 308), `/llms.txt`, `/mcp` (405 on GET) and `/.well-known/mcp.json`.

Until step 2 is done, `/docs` links on a local build 404 because the Mintlify origin has no `/docs` base path yet. The page itself renders regardless.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check-types` in `website/`
- [x] `prek` hooks on the changed files (gitleaks skipped locally, binary not installed)
- [x] Desktop and mobile layouts checked in a browser, no horizontal overflow, mobile menu works
- [x] Redirects verified against the dev server (`/getting-started/quickstart` -> 308 `/docs/getting-started/quickstart`)
- [x] Amplitude proxy verified end to end with a placeholder key (Amplitude's own 400 comes back through `/api/t`)
- [ ] Preview deployment on Vercel
- [ ] Cutover steps above

Draft until a maintainer confirms the approach and the Vercel/Mintlify steps; the external-PR issue check will need an issue link before this is marked ready.

title: Cull expired OAuth state from the default OAuthProxy file store
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WWcAmyaiGhDd2X39BAZceKx)_

The default `FileTreeStore` behind OAuthProxy never deletes expired entries, so long-running servers slowly fill the disk with stale transaction and token files. @nosmile99's change reaps them with `FileTreeStore.cull()` (py-key-value-aio 0.4.6). Since servers are long-running, a one-time startup cull isn't enough, so the cull now runs in the background on the OAuth write paths (authorize, code exchange, refresh), at most once an hour. The first flow after a restart clears what earlier runs left behind, construction stays side-effect free, and there's no new public API. Custom `client_storage` is never touched.

This carries #5735 forward with maintainer finishing touches, keeping the original commits and authorship. Closes #5718.

title: Fix and quiet the triage alerts from 2026-11-02
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WPFm3DJARss4o8sCcd76TzX)_

## Description

Most triage alerts on 2026-11-02 were noise or came from fixable bugs, and the alert text didn't say what to do. Each cause below comes from the actual Prefect Cloud runs.

**`issues/8203` 404.** Renovate escapes upstream refs as `[#​25533](...)`, and the PR-body issue regex allowed `&` before `#`. So every Renovate PR event, and this PR's own event, made the intake look up issue 8203 and crash. Now `&` is excluded.

**Merged mid-run (#6190, #6096, #6199).** The fix PRs merged while their issues were in triage. The delivery gate correctly refused to post, but the run was marked Degraded and paged twice per issue. Gate refusals caused by a change underneath the run now raise `EvidenceChanged`. The controller records the delivery as `superseded`, and the intake no longer alerts on `stale` or `baseline_changed` items. `settle` already requeues those, and a new push fires its own triage event, which cancels the old batch through the issue claim. A merged PR's issue closes and drops out of inventory. Nothing reruns.

**#6236 "needs operational attention".** The title-keyword PR search for a generic title ("Add configuration for _meta.fastmcp data") returned more than six unrelated PRs, so the context hard-failed before any model ran. Now only linked PRs count toward the bound. The newest keyword matches fill the remaining slots, and the omitted numbers are recorded.

**#6199 "Review differs from retained independent evidence".** The stored records match exactly, so this check hid which of its three conditions failed. Now each condition has its own message.

The alert now reads "triage skipped some issues" and shows each issue's actual detail, plus a note that skipped issues retry for up to 3 tries. Failures read "triage failed before finishing".

## Contribution type

- [x] Bug fix (simple, well-scoped fix for a clearly broken behavior)
- [ ] Documentation improvement
- [ ] Enhancement (maintainers typically implement enhancements — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md))

- [x] I have run `uv run prek run --all-files` and all checks pass (agentic ruff, ty, and pytest; the 2 `real_base_head_execution` tests need the CI docker sandbox and fail identically on main locally)
- [x] I have self-reviewed my changes

### [`v0.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0170)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/compare/0.16.10...0.17.0)

Released on 2026-10-09.

The executables in our macOS and Windows release archives and `ruff` wheels are now code-signed.
macOS executables are signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple. Windows
executables have timestamped Authenticode signatures from Azure Artifact Signing. This enables
verification of the release publisher and binary integrity, supports publisher-based allowlisting,
and should reduce security warnings and antivirus false positives.

##### Breaking changes

- Update the default and latest Python versions for 3.15 ([#​28792](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28792))

  Ruff now defaults to Python 3.11 instead of 3.10 when no Python version is configured through
  [`target-version`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#target-version) or
  [`requires-python`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/#inferring-the-python-version). When
  checking for syntax errors without a configured Python version, Ruff now defaults to Python 3.15
  instead of 3.14.

- Update the default rule set ([#​28786](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28786))

  Several of the `flake8-datetimez` rules
  ([`DTZ001`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-without-tzinfo/),
  [`DTZ005`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-now-without-tzinfo/),
  [`DTZ006`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-fromtimestamp/),
  [`DTZ007`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-datetime-strptime-without-zone/),
  [`DTZ011`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-date-today/),
  [`DTZ012`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/call-date-fromtimestamp/), and
  [`DTZ901`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/datetime-min-max/)) are no longer enabled by default,
  while [`undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/undefined-local-with-nested-import-star-usage/)
  (`F406`), which corresponds to a syntax error, is now enabled by default.

- Update Rust crate quick-junit to 0.8.0 ([#​27295](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27295))

  JUnit output now uses a `skipped` attribute instead of `disabled` on `<testsuite>` elements and
  includes a `skipped` attribute on the root `<testsuites>` element.

- \[`flake8-import-conventions`] Add `datetime as dt` as a conventional alias (`ICN001`) ([#​28790](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28790))

- Support Unicode dummy variable names ([#​28722](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28722))

  The default [`lint.dummy-variable-rgx`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#lint_dummy-variable-rgx)
  now recognizes underscore-prefixed Unicode names, such as `_次`, as dummy variables.

- Update to Unicode 17 ([#​21229](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/21229), [#​28784](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28784))

  Ruff now uses Unicode 17 data for identifier normalization and named character escapes (`"\N{...}"`).

- Always show unsafe and display-only fixes in the CLI ([#​27810](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27810))

  The default `full` output format now shows unsafe fixes and suggestions requiring manual review,
  regardless of the [`unsafe-fixes`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#unsafe-fixes) setting.
  Actually applying unsafe fixes still requires explicit opt-in.

- Remove the Python dependency from conda-forge builds ([conda-forge/ruff-feedstock#361](https://redirect.github.com/conda-forge/ruff-feedstock/pull/361))

  The conda-forge build no longer depends on Python, now supports linux-riscv64, win-arm64, and
  linux-ppc64le platforms, and now includes shell completions. However, no longer depending on
  Python means that `python -m ruff` and `import ruff` will no longer work. Use `ruff` directly from
  `PATH` instead. PyPI installations and those from the standalone installer are unaffected.

- Remove support for ruff-lsp ([#​28750](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28750))

  Support for `ruff-lsp`, the legacy Python language server [deprecated in Ruff
  v0.9.5](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/releases/tag/0.9.5), has been removed. The Ruff VS Code
  extension now always uses the native language server; `ruff.nativeServer` is deprecated and
  ignored. See the [migration guide](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/editors/migration/).

##### Stabilization

The following rules have been stabilized and are no longer in preview:

- [`lazy-import-mismatch`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/lazy-import-mismatch) (`TID254`)
- [`lazy-import-immediately-resolved`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/lazy-import-immediately-resolved)
  (`TID255`)
- [`os-path-commonprefix`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/os-path-commonprefix) (`RUF071`)

The following behaviors have been stabilized:

- The formatter, [`unsorted-imports`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/unsorted-imports/) (`I001`),
  [`line-too-long`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/line-too-long/) (`E501`), and
  [`doc-line-too-long`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/doc-line-too-long/) (`W505`) now
  consistently ignore trailing pragma comments when computing line length. This resolved several
  bugs involving interactions between these rules
  ([#​27313](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/27313)) but may also cause existing imports to be
  reformatted and was thus classified as a breaking change.

title: Let private triage sweeps run without the Sol reviewer
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WQHKcG9f9KSPKrT1zMxbw41)_

## Description

Running triage over the 130 gated PRs costs mostly the Sol `triage_review`, about 70% of tokens in a 10-issue pilot. That review exists to gate public output, and a private sweep (`publish_reviews` off) posts nothing. This allows a native-triage runtime without `triage_review` only when publishing is off. In that case the controller retains each outcome with `adversarial_review: None` and doesn't call Sol. Anything later proposed for a public action gets its own Sol review. A publishing runtime still has to include the reviewer, so the live automations are unchanged.

```python
Runtime(plans={"assess": ..., "reproduce": ...}, triage_plan=..., ...)            # private sweep: ok
Runtime(plans={"assess": ..., "reproduce": ...}, publish_reviews=True, ...)       # still rejected
```

title: Add a Client-level keep_alive option for stdio transports
body:
## Description

Fixes #644

`keep_alive` is a stdio-only option, so you can only set it by building the transport yourself. A client created from a script path, such as `Client(Path("server.py"))`, infers a `PythonStdioTransport` and offers nowhere to turn session persistence off. To do that you have to drop down to `PythonStdioTransport(script_path=..., keep_alive=False)`.

The issue's open question was how a client-level option should default when stdio defaults to `True` and the other transports have no such option. As noted in the issue thread, `keep_alive` exists only on `StdioTransport` and its subclasses, so a client-level option can only ever affect stdio. `Client` now accepts `keep_alive: bool | None = None`. `None` leaves the transport's own setting alone, so the stdio default is still `True` and nothing changes for existing code. An explicit value is set on the stdio transport, overriding whatever the transport was created with. With any other transport it raises `ValueError`, the same way `Client(..., verify=...)` rejects non-HTTP transports.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from fastmcp import Client

client = Client(Path("server.py"), keep_alive=False)

async with client:
    await client.call_tool("process_data", {"file": "data.csv"})
# the subprocess exits here instead of staying alive for reuse
```

One decision to confirm: an `MCPConfig` also raises, even a single-server config whose one entry is stdio. Each `StdioMCPServer` entry already has its own `keep_alive` field, and a multi-server config builds its backends at connect time, so applying a client-wide value there would need a separate design. If you'd rather a single-stdio-server config accept it, that's a small follow-up.

title: Let clients with different timeouts share a kept-alive stdio session
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WFuLUk1Tdcd9FkR8jax7BPQ)_

## Description

#6156 fixed kept-alive stdio transports ignoring a later client's timeout (#6155), but it made a client nested inside another one on the same transport fail to connect when the two timeouts differed. 4.1.x let that work, so it's a regression on main. Now the nested client shares the live session and its default timeout, as in 4.1.x, and FastMCP logs a warning naming both timeouts; per-call `timeout` still applies. Sequential clients keep #6156's behavior: an idle session is rebuilt when the timeout changes. Different transport options still raise.

```python
transport = PythonStdioTransport("server.py")
async with Client(transport) as first:
    async with Client(transport, timeout=5) as second:  # RuntimeError on main
        await second.call_tool("sleep", {"seconds": 3}, timeout=5)
```

title: fix(client): omit None prompt arguments instead of sending the string "null"
body:
Fixes #6025

`Client.get_prompt()` turned every non-string argument into JSON text, so `{"audience": None}` reached the server as the string `"null"`. The server validated it as an ordinary `str` and rendered `audience='null'` instead of using the parameter default.

MCP prompt arguments are `dict[str, str]`, so `None` has no wire form. The client now leaves `None` values out, which makes `{"topic": "x", "audience": None}` behave exactly like `{"topic": "x"}`.

```python
@mcp.prompt
def greet(topic: str, audience: str | None = None) -> str:
    return f"topic={topic!r} audience={audience!r}"

await client.get_prompt("greet", {"topic": "x", "audience": None})
# before: topic='x' audience='null'
# after:  topic='x' audience=None
```

Other non-string values (lists, dicts, numbers, booleans) are serialized as before. A `None` that is a real value inside a list or dict is also unchanged, because only top-level `None` arguments are skipped.

## Testing

- New test `test_client_omits_none_arguments` in `tests/client/client/test_client.py`. It fails without the change (the server log shows it received `'audience': 'null'`) and passes with it.
- `tests/client/client/test_client.py` and `tests/client/client/test_error_handling.py`: 81 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_client_new_preserves_internal_task_extension`, which needs the `docket` package that is not installed in my environment; it does not touch this change.
- `ruff format --check` is clean on both files. `ruff check` reports one existing `BLE001` at `tests/client/client/test_client.py:778`, which is also present without my change.
- Not run: the full suite, `prek`, and the docs checks.

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) to help find the cause and draft the change and test. I reviewed the diff myself.

I am not assigned to the issue yet; I opened this so the change is ready for review if a maintainer wants it.

title: fix(config): apply tool transforms before tag filters on single servers
body:
## Problem

In a single-server `MCPConfig`, tags added through the server's `tools` transforms are invisible to `include_tags`/`exclude_tags` — fixes #6196.

`_to_server_and_underlying_transport` (the transforming single-server path) registered the tag filters **before** adding the `ToolTransform`, while the multi-server composite path (`_build_composite`) applies transforms first with a comment explaining why: transforms may add or modify the tags the filters then match. With the filter-first order, `include_tags: ["keep"]` plus `tools: {add: {tags: ["keep"]}}` lists no tools, and the matching `exclude_tags` case lists everything — both correct on two-server configs.

## Fix

Reorder the single-server path to transforms-then-filters, mirroring `_build_composite` (comment included).

## Tests

- `test_single_server_transform_added_tags_filtering_in_memory` — new; reproduces #6196 fully in-memory (patches the backend transport with an in-process FastMCP), so it runs on every platform. Fails on `main` (`ffccd32`: the tool set comes back empty) and passes with this change.
- `test_single_server_config_transform_added_tags_filtering` — subprocess variant mirroring the issue end to end (skips on Windows like the other stdio-subprocess tests; runs on CI).
- Full `tests/test_mcp_config.py`: 39 passed, 12 skipped (pre-existing Windows subprocess skips).

title: Gate 3.x PyPI publishing behind an environment
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W5hwJDHfbenKkGLgqLLbXim)_

Publishing a GitHub release currently goes straight to PyPI with nothing in between, and `/marvin` agents run with `Bash(*)` and an unscoped Marvin App token, which per this repo's own workflow comments includes `contents: write` and `actions: write`. An agent like that, or an injected issue body it's reading, is one `gh release create` or `gh workflow run` away from a publish.

On `release/3.x`, this puts the `fastmcp-slim` publish job behind a `pypi` environment. That job is the only one that needs the gate, because remote and fastmcp already refuse to publish unless a matching `fastmcp-slim` version is on PyPI. A release or a dispatch now waits for an approval, once per release. Comment-triggered workflows run from `main`, so the `/marvin` token scoping only lives in the main PR.

```yaml
  pypi-publish:
    name: Upload fastmcp-slim to PyPI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: pypi
```

The `pypi` environment and its reviewer have to exist before this merges. Otherwise GitHub auto-creates an unprotected one.

title: Drop client context holds left by finished tasks
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7W?thread=cmsg_01EkwKAptPX4vtXECnAMud7WUXK4jjhmHkBWJUk8o66CXh)_

## Description

#6018 records which session each `async with client` entered, keyed by the entering task, so a stale context can't release a newer session. Nothing removes that record when the context is released by `close()` or exited from another task. A reused client keeps one entry, plus its finished task and session task, for every such cycle.

```python
client = Client(server)
for _ in range(50):
    await asyncio.create_task(client.__aenter__())
    await client.close()
# main: 50 entries retained; this branch: 1, pruned on the next entry
```

A finished task can never run its own exit, so its holds are dead, and the next entry now prunes them. An earlier version of this branch used weak keys. That turned out to let GC of an orphaned, still-pending task run its `__aexit__` under another task and release that task's hold, so pruning only finished tasks avoids depending on collection timing.

title: fix(cli): preserve explicit null in generated tool commands
body:
Fixes #6190. Generated tool commands currently decode JSON `null` into `None` and then discard it as an omitted option. A nullable required parameter consequently fails validation, while an optional one can silently fall back to its default. For a tool accepting `profile: dict[str, str] | None`, this command should send null to clear the profile:

```bash
python cli.py call-tool set_profile --profile null
```

Filter omitted optional arguments before decoding JSON, then forward the decoded arguments unchanged. Preserve defaults and empty collections, avoid collisions with parameter names, and document explicit null handling for JSON-encoded parameters.

title: fix(cli): escape CR and CRLF in generate-cli descriptions
body:
Fixes #6074

## Problem

`generate-cli` embedded parameter descriptions into the generated script with only `\`, `"` and LF escaped. A description containing Windows-style CRLF — or a lone CR — kept its raw carriage return inside the single-quoted `cyclopts.Parameter(help="...")` string, and running any generated command raised `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`. The tool docstring path never escaped newlines at all.

## Fix (`fastmcp/cli/generate.py`)

- **Help text**: normalize CRLF → LF and CR → LF before the existing escapes, so both become the escaped-`\n` form inside the double-quoted help string.
- **Docstring**: normalize CRLF/CR to plain LF (valid inside triple quotes) alongside the existing `\` and `'` escapes, so no carriage return lands in the generated source.

Descriptions with any line-ending style now generate importable scripts, with no change to the server's metadata.

## Tests

`tests/cli/test_generate_cli.py::TestToolFunctionSourceNewlines`:
- parametrized CRLF and lone-CR parameter descriptions → generated source parses (`ast.parse`) and contains no `\r`;
- a tool description mixing CRLF and CR → same.

All three fail on `main`; the full `test_generate_cli.py` suite (89 tests) passes with the fix.

title: fix(openapi): make resource templates for non-identifier path parameters readable
body:
Fixes #6150

## Problem

OpenAPI legally allows path parameters whose names are not Python identifiers — `{$top}`, `x.y`, `1id`. `build_regex()` built regex group names with only a hyphen-to-underscore swap, so such names produced invalid group names (`(?P<$top>...)`), `re.compile` raised, and the function returned `None` — silently disabling the whole template. `from_openapi` still listed it, but every read failed with "Resource not found".

## Fix

- **`fastmcp/resources/template.py`**: new `template_param_key()` — every character a legal template variable may carry that a Python identifier cannot (`$`, `.`, leading digits, …) becomes `_` (`{$top}` → `_top`, `{x.y}` → `x_y`, `{1id}` → `_1id`, hyphenated names unchanged). `build_regex()` now uses it for both simple and wildcard groups, so these templates compile and match instead of returning `None`.
- **`server/providers/openapi/components.py`**: `OpenAPIResourceTemplate.create_resource()` maps matched params back onto route parameters through the same helper (previously only hyphens were normalized, so `_top` wouldn't have reached a `$top` route parameter).

Templates that previously disabled themselves now match; `build_regex` still returns `None` for genuinely ambiguous templates (duplicate group names after sanitization).

## Tests

- **End-to-end** (`test_openapi_features.py::TestNonIdentifierPathParameterNames`): the issue's exact scenario — four routes with `top`, `$top`, `x.y`, `1id` path params mapped to resource templates; all four are listed and all four read successfully through `MockTransport`. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- **Unit** (`test_resource_template.py::TestNonIdentifierTemplateVariableNames`): `match_uri_template` returns sanitized keys for `$`/dot/leading-digit/hyphen/identifier names, `build_regex` compiles the `$` case, and wildcard `{$top*}` spans segments.
- **Updated two tests that pinned the old behavior** (`TestMalformedURITemplates`): leading-digit templates now assert the sanitized-match expectation instead of "returns None". Duplicate-group templates still return `None`.

Full sweep: `tests/resources/`, `tests/server/providers/openapi/`, `tests/server/providers/proxy/`, `tests/utilities/openapi/` — **1483 passed**, ruff check/format clean.

title: fix(json-schema): keep tools/list working when a root $ref resolves to a boolean schema
body:
Fixes #6125

## Problem

`dereference_refs()` asserted the final result is a `dict`, but a root `$ref` can resolve to a **boolean schema** — `true` and `false` are valid JSON Schemas. With `{"type": "object", "$ref": "#/$defs/Any", "$defs": {"Any": true}}`, jsonref replaces the whole root schema with the boolean (dropping the root's own keywords along the way), the assertion fires, and one such tool fails `tools/list` for the **entire server**. The same crash reaches `create_proxy` backends, since that path dereferences through the same function.

## Fix

Replace the assertion with the same fallback every other "can't fully inline" case already uses (circular refs, oversized expansions, `JsonRefError`):

```python
if not isinstance(dereferenced, dict):
    return resolve_root_ref(schema)
```

`resolve_root_ref` already handles non-dict targets safely (`if not isinstance(target, dict) ... return schema`), so the tool keeps its original schema — `$ref` and `$defs` intact, valid per spec, `type: object` at root per MCP requirements — and the rest of the server's tools stay visible.

I considered fully inlining the boolean case (e.g. returning the root's keywords for `true`), but siblings can themselves contain `$ref`s that jsonref already resolved in the discarded tree, so rebuilding them would re-introduce dangling refs. Falling back keeps the fix consistent with the existing partial-resolution paths and side-effect-free.

## Tests

`tests/utilities/test_json_schema.py` (unit):
- `test_falls_back_for_root_ref_to_boolean_schema` — the issue's exact schema returns unchanged instead of raising
- `test_falls_back_for_root_ref_to_false_schema_without_siblings` — `false` target, no siblings
- `test_falls_back_for_root_ref_to_non_schema_json_value` — a `$defs` entry can be any JSON value (e.g. a list), so the guard covers all non-dict targets
- `test_nested_ref_to_boolean_schema_is_inlined_as_is` — pins the already-working nested case (property node becomes the boolean itself)

`tests/server/middleware/test_dereference.py` (end-to-end):
- `test_root_ref_to_boolean_schema_does_not_fail_listing` — the issue's repro as a server: both tools are listed, the boolean-schema tool keeps its original schema

All 84 tests in the two touched suites pass, plus 113 in the neighboring suites that share this code (`test_json_schema_expansion`, `openapi/test_schemas`, `tool_transform/test_schemas`, `test_json_schema_generation`). Static checks (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `ty`, `codespell`) pass on the changed files.

title: fix(json-schema): decode RFC 6901 escapes when extracting $defs names
body:
Fixes #6034

## Problem

`compress_schema()` decided which `` are referenced by reading the raw pointer text of each `` (`ref.split("/")[-1]` in `_single_pass_optimize`). A definition referenced through a properly encoded JSON Pointer therefore looked unused and was pruned, leaving dangling ``s in the returned schema:

- RFC 6901 escapes: `#/$defs/a~1b` (definition `a/b`), `#/$defs/c~0d` (definition `c~d`)
- percent-encoding: `#/$defs/Alias%20One` (definition `Alias One`)
- sub-pointers into a definition: `#/$defs/Container/properties/value` — the raw last segment is `properties`, not `Container`

The same raw-text extraction is used in two OpenAPI paths, with the same effect: `OpenAPIParser._extract_schema_dependencies` (collecting component schemas by name) and the request-body `` pruner inside `_combine_schemas_and_map_params`. A component schema named `a/b`, referenced as `#/components/schemas/a~1b`, was never collected and its rewritten `` dangled.

## Fix

Add `ref_target_name()` to `fastmcp.utilities.json_schema`. It returns the first pointer segment after a definition root (`` by default, `components/schemas` for raw OpenAPI documents), decoded the same way `_resolve_local_ref` decodes pointers: percent-decode the fragment, then unescape `~1`/`~0` per RFC 6901. Matching the resolver's own convention keeps the collectors consistent with what actually resolves — anything `_resolve_local_ref` can resolve is never treated as unused. A pointer may continue past the name, so a sub-pointer names the container definition.

The helper is used at all three extraction sites:

- `_single_pass_optimize` (`compress_schema` `` pruning)
- `OpenAPIParser._extract_schema_dependencies`
- `_combine_schemas_and_map_params` request-body `` pruning

Raw `` values are untouched everywhere; only the used/unused decision changes.

## Tests

- `TestRefTargetName`: the decoder itself — escapes, `~01` not re-decoded, percent-encoding, sub-pointers, non-definition pointers, alternate roots
- `TestCompressSchemaEscapedRefNames`: the issue's schema keeps all four referenced definitions; def→def escaped references keep both definitions; unused escaped definitions are still pruned
- `TestEscapedSchemaNameReferences` (OpenAPI): schemas named `a/b` and `Alias One` are collected from the document and survive `_combine_schemas_and_map_params` with their references intact

The `compress_schema` regression fails on `main` for the reported reason (all four referenced definitions pruned, so `result.get("$defs")` is `None`) and passes with this change.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/utilities/ -n 0` — 1312 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run pytest tests/tools tests/resources tests/prompts -n 0` — 893 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run prek run --files <changed files>` — ruff check/format, prettier, codespell, loq passed; `ty check` passes on all changed files when run directly (the prek runner hit a transient allocator OOM on ty, not a type error); gitleaks was skipped locally because the binary is not installed

title: Keep posted review receipts on partial delivery and reject differing reviews
body:
## Description

Codex flagged two delivery gaps on #6116, and both were already present in the deployed goldfish.

The first is partial delivery. When an outcome verifies several PRs and delivery fails after the first review is posted, the controller replaced the result with a bare failure. `published_reviews` came back empty, so a review that was already public dropped out of the queue and out of freshness normalization.

The second is in `post_review`, which adopted any existing review with the same revision marker. If two issue workers reviewed the same PR head with different feedback, the second review was reported as `already_posted` and never delivered.

Delivery now raises `PartialReviewDelivery`, which carries the receipts it already holds, and the controller keeps them under `posted`. An existing review is adopted only when its body matches, apart from line endings. A differing review fails with "A different review already exists for this revision" and lands in the operational bin instead of passing as published. Separately, `agentic_stack.sh validate` now wraps each plan as `{"plan": ...}`, which the current `/execution-plans/validate` endpoint requires; it was returning 422.

```python
try:
    deliver_reviews(...)  # #7 posted, #8 fails freshness
except PartialReviewDelivery as error:
    error.posted  # [receipt for #7], still reported as published
```
