title: Record verification selections outside the route instead of failing
body:
## Description

Existing-contribution verification for #5474 kept failing with "Selected contribution evidence is missing". The route admitted only #5487, but the assessor selected #5230, whose body now closes #6166. #5230 was in the collected evidence but outside `route.pull_requests`, so the check raised a misleading error and burned retries. #5812 hits the same mismatch.

This keeps the admission boundary as it is. Only admitted selections are executed. Anything selected outside the route is recorded as `verification_selection_outside_route`, with a next step that names the PRs. The assess plan prompt now also tells the assessor to select only from `context.route.pull_requests` and to mention other relevant work in `reason`.

```python
item = {
    "route": {"pull_requests": [{"number": 5487}]},
    "assessment": {"verification_prs": [5230, 5487]},
    ...
}
[s.pr_number for s in verification_specs(group, item, {})]  # [5487], was ValueError
```

title: Post Marvin's dedupe and too-long comments from workflow steps
body:
The dedupe and triage workflows let the model post comments itself: dedupe through `gh issue comment`, and triage through the GitHub MCP `add_issue_comment` tool. Both comments have a fixed format, so the model does not need a comment tool.

Dedupe now returns duplicate issue numbers through `--json-schema`. A workflow step keeps the numbers that are existing issues other than this one, builds the comment from the same template with titles from the API, posts it on the triggering issue, and adds `potential-duplicate`. The model's token is read-only. The comment and label use a separate token created after the model exits. The job also drops `id-token: write`, which no step used.

Triage no longer has `add_issue_comment`. When the model applies `too-long`, a workflow step posts the same contributing-guidelines comment, once per issue or PR.

This also fixes single-duplicate issues never closing. With one duplicate, the comment says "possible duplicate issue". The label step, `auto_close_duplicates.py`, and the agentic intake matched only "possible duplicate issues", so those issues were never labeled or closed. They now get `potential-duplicate`, and `auto_close_duplicates.py` closes them after 3 days like any other duplicate.

## Rollout caveats

- `watch: the first Marvin Issue Dedupe runs after merge. A run that finds duplicates but posts no comment means structured_output did not arrive.`
- `no-op: open single-duplicate issues from before this change have no potential-duplicate label, so auto-close does not touch them.`

title: Mask the Docket backend password in the worker banner
body:
Fixes #6112

The worker startup banner prints the Docket backend URL verbatim, so a Redis URL carrying a password in the userinfo (`redis://user:secret@host`) or in a `password`/`sentinel_password` query parameter leaks the secret into terminals and CI logs.

```python
'redis://default:***@localhost:6390/0'
```

title: perf(schema): skip unnecessary reference sibling restoration
body:
Large tool catalogs spend time rebuilding expanded schemas even when there are no reference sibling keywords to restore. This skips that extra walk for ordinary `#/$defs/` references without siblings. In a local 965-tool catalog with 50-tool pages, median `Client.list_tools()` latency falls from 32.192 to 20.396 seconds, 36.6 percent lower. The returned schemas match; the measurement covers local ASGI discovery.

Other pointer forms and URI spellings normalized by jsonref keep the existing restoration path. The existing discriminator traversal also copies literal data on the optimized path, so editing one expanded default, const, example or enum does not change another reference's value.

```python
from fastmcp.utilities.json_schema import dereference_refs

schema = {
    "properties": {"name": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Name"}},
    "$defs": {"Name": {"type": "string"}},
}
expanded = dereference_refs(schema)
# expanded["properties"]["name"] is {"type": "string"}
```

Fixes #6160.

title: Use renamed argument names in transformed tool validation errors
body:
## Description

Renaming an argument with `ArgTransform(name=...)` only changes the transformed tool's schema.
`_forward` maps the call back to the parent's argument names, so the parent's validation errors name arguments the client never saw (`n` instead of `max_results`, `f.limit` instead of `filters.limit`).

`_forward` now catches the parent's `ValidationError` and rebuilds it with the transformed names, keeping nested paths, error types and messages.
Chained transforms report the outermost name, and transforms that don't rename anything are left as is.
The rebuilt errors are custom pydantic errors, since pydantic can only re-create its built-in error types by name, so they drop the `For further information visit ...` line.

```python
def search(q: str, n: Annotated[int, Field(le=10)] = 5) -> str: ...


find = Tool.from_tool(
    Tool.from_function(search),
    name="find",
    transform_args={"n": ArgTransform(name="max_results")},
)
# call "find" with {"q": "x", "max_results": 50}
```

```diff
 1 validation error for call[search]
-n
+max_results
   Input should be less than or equal to 10 [type=less_than_equal, input_value=50, input_type=int]
-    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/less_than_equal
```

Closes #6157

title: Fix kept-alive stdio transports ignoring client timeouts
body:
A shared `keep_alive=True` stdio transport silently reuses the first client's request timeout: a later client asking for five seconds can time out after one, while a one-second limit can be ignored. Fixes #6155, reported by @BlueX888.

Include `read_timeout_seconds` in the existing reuse guard: rebuild an idle session when the timeout changes, and reject an incompatible connection while the previous session is in use. Matching timeouts preserve session reuse, including proxy clients that rebind callbacks per request. This change is limited to request timeouts; callback configuration keeps its existing behavior. Per-call timeout overrides remain supported.

```python
from fastmcp import Client
from fastmcp.client.transports import PythonStdioTransport

transport = PythonStdioTransport("server.py", keep_alive=True)
async with Client(transport, timeout=1) as first:
    await first.list_tools()
async with Client(transport, timeout=5) as second:
    await second.call_tool("sleep", {"seconds": 3})  # Uses the five-second timeout
```

title: Preserve overlapping OpenAPI query parameter values
body:
OpenAPI `form`/`explode=true` object parameters serialize their properties as bare query keys. When one of those keys matches a separately declared query parameter, the serializer previously overwrote one value, with the surviving value depending on argument order. For example, `filter={"q": 1}` together with `q=false` now sends both values as `q=1&q=false` (in either argument order). Fixes #6149.

title: Stop FastMCP callable caches from retaining dropped tools
body:
FastMCP's process-wide callable caches retained tool closures after their servers were dropped, including the captured per-user data. Store wrapper and adapter metadata on the function or bound instance instead, so references between a callable and its cached values can be collected together. Callables that cannot own this metadata run uncached; ordinary type adapters keep the existing bounded cache. Runtime cache entries are discarded when a tool function is pickled for a task.

This fixes the FastMCP-owned retention in #6115. The independent signature and parameter caches in `uncalled-for` still retain functions until released there; that remaining dependency issue is tracked in https://github.com/chrisguidry/uncalled-for/issues/21. The lifecycle regression isolates those third-party caches and does not claim that a full application using the current dependency has no remaining retention.

Fixes #6115

title: fix(json-schema): handle boolean schemas from root $ref dereferencing
body:
Fixes #6125.

A tool whose parameters hold a root `$ref` to a boolean schema (for example `{"type": "object", "$ref": "#/$defs/Any", "$defs": {"Any": true}}`, where `true` is a perfectly valid JSON Schema) took down `tools/list` for the whole server: `dereference_refs` inlined the reference to the boolean `True`, then hit `assert isinstance(merged, dict)` and the middleware turned that into an Internal server error for every tool, not just the offending one. The fix teaches `dereference_refs` the boolean case at the root: `true` conjoins with the root's sibling keywords, so the siblings alone describe the result, and `false` becomes its dict form `{"not": {}}`. Nested boolean references already passed through untouched, so the change is root-only.

```python
mcp.add_tool(AnyArgs(name="anything", parameters={
    "type": "object", "$ref": "#/$defs/Any", "$defs": {"Any": True},
}))
# tools/list now returns ["anything", "ping"] instead of Internal server error
```

Credit to @alpaylan for the precise repro in #6125.

title: Preserve incompatible schema defaults during dataclass hydration
body:
A missing, non-required field should not make an otherwise valid tool result fail to hydrate just because its schema default doesn't match the field type. The dataclass path currently inserts that default before validation, so a tool returning `{}` can leave `result.data` as `None`.

```python
from fastmcp.utilities.json_schema_type import json_schema_to_type

schema = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"name": {"type": "string", "default": None}},
}
TypeAdapter(json_schema_to_type(schema)).validate_python({})
# Root(name=None), instead of a ValidationError
```

Tool results can lose their parsed data when an omitted field has a default that does not satisfy its own type, such as `"name": {"type": "string", "default": null}`. The dataclass conversion path injects the default into the input and validates it as an explicit value, while the `additionalProperties: true` path already preserves that default

Let dataclass fields apply their own defaults, hydrating valid defaults and preserving invalid ones. Check recursive defaults once their generated types can be resolved. Keep parent object default merging and validation of explicitly supplied values

Fixes #6123

title: fix(schema): preserve additionalProperties on object schemas without explicit type (fixes #6124)
body:
Resolves #6124

### Summary of Changes

An object schema with `properties` but no explicit `"type": "object"` (valid in JSON Schema) previously bypassed `_object_schema_to_type` in `_convert_normalized` and called `_create_dataclass` directly in `_convert_schema`. Because `@dataclass` does not permit extra fields, schemas specifying `"additionalProperties": True` silently dropped undeclared keys unless `"type": "object"` was explicitly declared.

1. **Object schema routing (`fastmcp/utilities/json_schema_type.py`):**
   - In `_convert_normalized`: Route schemas that contain `"properties"` without an explicit `"type"` through `_object_schema_to_type`.
   - In `_convert_schema`: Delegate schemas containing `"properties"` to `_object_schema_to_type` instead of calling `_create_dataclass` directly, ensuring `additionalProperties: True` correctly generates a Pydantic model with `extra="allow"`.
   - In `_merge_defaults`: Treat property schemas defining `"properties"` as objects when merging nested default values.

2. **Tests (`tests/utilities/json_schema_type/test_containers.py`):**
   - Added parameterized regression test `test_object_schema_without_type_preserves_additional_properties` covering both explicit and implicit object schemas with empty and populated `properties`, verifying that additional properties are preserved.

### Verification
- Ran `uv run pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type/test_containers.py` (70/70 passed).
- Ran `uv run pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type` (407/407 passed).
- Validated reproduction case from #6124: `{"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": True}` and `{"properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}, "additionalProperties": True}` both retain undeclared keys.
- Passed `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.

title: fix: keep additionalProperties on object schemas without a type
body:
## Problem

An object schema that has `properties` but no `"type": "object"` ignores
`additionalProperties: true`, so `json_schema_to_type` silently drops every
undeclared key. The same schema with `"type": "object"` keeps them. Fixes #6124.

```python
for schema in (
    {"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": True},
    {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": True},
):
    ta = TypeAdapter(json_schema_to_type(schema))
    print(ta.dump_python(ta.validate_python({"a": 1})))
# {}
# {'a': 1}
```

## Root cause

`_convert_schema` sends any schema with `properties` and no `type` straight to
`_create_dataclass`, which has no notion of `additionalProperties`. The object
handler `_object_schema_to_type` already implements the right matrix
(`dict[str, Any]`, dict-of-value-type, Pydantic model with `extra="allow"`, or
dataclass), but only the `"type": "object"` path reaches it.

## Fix

When an untyped schema has `properties` and truthy `additionalProperties`,
route it through `_object_schema_to_type` instead of `_create_dataclass`. The
no-`additionalProperties` and `additionalProperties: false` cases still take
the dataclass path, unchanged.

## Testing

- Two new tests in `TestAdditionalProperties`: a properties-only object keeps
  undeclared keys, and `{"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": true}`
  returns `dict[str, Any]`. Both fail on the parent commit and pass with the fix.
- `pytest tests/utilities/json_schema_type/` (advanced/containers/constraints/
  unions/core): 236 passed.
- `ruff format` applied; `ruff check` reports only the pre-existing BLE001 at
  `json_schema_type.py:1055` (untouched by this change).

title: Compare JSON const and enum values by JSON equality

## Description

title: Deliver concurrent triage reviews, draft fixes and mutation proposals
body:
Automatic triage previously serialized unrelated intake and retained useful reviews only in Prefect. Give issues renewable ownership so independent work can progress concurrently, deliver revision-specific reviews through a separate GitHub App, and take unclaimed issues through credential-isolated validation and independent review to draft publication. Native triage passes its durably retained evidence directly to review. JSON Schema version names such as `draft-07` no longer become author holds. Posted reviews remain visible and counted after later freshness stops.

The independent review also retains specific mutation proposals with target revisions, public payloads, contribution norms and unmet approval gates. Bounded canonical-PR discovery follows maintainer direction in contribution discussion, including closed proposals, so reviews can assess the selected survivor. Ownership, security routing, freshness, independent scrutiny and contributor credit remain gates. Assignments and closures remain proposals for maintainer approval; automatic merges and issue closures are disabled.

```bash
.github/agentic/scripts/agentic_stack.sh mutations <controller-run-id>
```

title: Move proxied Skills backend calls onto ProxyProvider
body:
`ProxyProvider` owns every conversation with the backend: listing and fetching tools, resources, templates and prompts all go through its methods and its client handling. Skills were the exception. The backend `skills/list` and `skills/get` calls lived in `_ProxiedSkills`, which kept its own copy of the client setup and transport-error translation and imported four private helpers from `proxy.py` to do it.

This moves both calls onto `ProxyProvider` as `_list_skills()` and `_get_skill(uri)`, beside the other component methods. The provider now makes every backend call, and `_ProxiedSkills` only decides which entries are served and visible to the caller. The duplicate client wrapper goes away, and Skills become overridable the same way every other proxied component already is:

```python
class TracedProxy(ProxyProvider):
    async def _list_skills(self) -> Sequence[MCPSkill]:
        with tracer.start_as_current_span("proxy.skills.list"):
            return await super()._list_skills()
```

title: fix(server): rebuild tool argument errors instead of echoing pydantic's
body:
Fixes #6099

When a `tools/call` fails argument validation the server re-raised the pydantic error, so `str(ValidationError)` reached the caller with the exact pydantic version URL (`https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.14/v/string_type`), the internal adapter name (`call[echo]`), and every submitted value with its inferred type. Server-side logging already avoids all of that (#5106); the response did not.

## Change

`fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/server.py`

- New `_validation_error_message(tool_name, error)` rebuilds the client-facing text from `error.errors(include_url=False, include_context=False, include_input=False)`: one line per invalid argument with its location and reason, prefixed by the tool name.
- The argument-validation branch raises `ToolError` with that message instead of re-raising the pydantic error. The warning log (`_validation_error_summary`) is unchanged.
- Raw pydantic errors raised by a tool's own validation (the separate branch) keep their previous behaviour.

Before:

```
2 validation errors for call[echo]
message
  Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=123, input_type=int]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.14/v/string_type
extra
  Unexpected keyword argument [type=unexpected_keyword_argument, input_value='x', input_type=str]
```

After:

```
Invalid arguments for tool 'echo': 2 validation errors
- message: Input should be a valid string
- extra: Unexpected keyword argument
```

## Tests

`tests/server/test_input_validation.py`

- New `test_client_error_omits_pydantic_details` drives the issue's repro and asserts the field/reason lines are present while `errors.pydantic.dev`, `call[`, `input_value`, `input_type` and `N validation errors for` are absent.
- `test_validation_logs_omit_client_data` previously asserted the client still received the raw values; it now asserts the caller learns which argument failed without the pydantic internals, while the log assertions are unchanged.

Verified: `pytest tests/server/test_input_validation.py -q` -> **54 passed**; with only `server.py` reverted, **7 failed** (the six log/client parametrizations and the new test). `ruff check` reports only the two pre-existing findings in untouched code (`PYI041` on the `set_instructions` signature and the string-concat finding at line 2046), and `ruff format` is clean on both changed files.

title: Stage skill exports before replacing installed files

## Description

A server serves `Skill` objects, but a client could only get `MCPSkill` metadata back. The only way to get a whole skill was `sync_skills()` to disk, so moving a skill from one system to another meant going through the filesystem. `read_skill()` reads every file in the manifest, checks it against its digest, and returns a `Skill`:

```python
skill = await client.read_skill("skill://review/SKILL.md")
mirror.add_provider(SkillCatalogProvider([skill]))
```

title: Verify and export skills with resource-manifest fallback
body:
`Client.read_skill()` currently needs the Skills extension even when a server already serves skill files as resources. It now falls back to FastMCP's `_manifest` resource when the extension is unavailable or does not know the skill, verifies every file's size and SHA-256 digest, and returns a `Skill`. Manifest resource URIs are read unchanged, including query parameters; server errors propagate. `ClientGroup.read_skill()` selects a server explicitly, and `Skill.to_directory()` exports the resulting value with path validation on every platform.

```python
from pathlib import Path

from fastmcp import Client

async with Client("http://localhost:8000/mcp") as client:
    skill = await client.read_skill("skill://review/SKILL.md")
    skill.to_directory(Path("skills") / skill.name)
```

`download_skill()` and `sync_skills()` use the same verification before writing. This deliberately requires valid frontmatter: older resource-only skills need a `name` matching their URI and a `description`. `overwrite=True` replaces the existing folder, removing locally added files. Legacy filesystem providers preserve CRLF so served bytes agree with their manifests. The guide documents these changes and keeps code-defined skills and discovery first.

Related: #6085 and #6087.

title: Share Prefab renderer resources across equivalent tools
body:
Prefab tools currently advertise separate renderer resources even when their pages and resource configuration match. This gives identical resources different identities and causes bundled renderers to be transferred repeatedly as users open different views. Automatically synthesized resources now share a stable URI derived from the installed Prefab version, delivery mode, MIME type, and effective resource metadata. Different CSP, permissions, domains, and border preferences stay distinct, including through tool transforms and mounted apps.

Previously advertised per-tool URIs remain readable as aliases; explicit resource URI overrides and backend tool hashes are preserved. HTML remains lazy, and sharing does not depend on host caching. These tools now advertise the same renderer URI without additional configuration:

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("Views")

@mcp.tool(app=True)
def orders() -> str:
    return "Orders"

@mcp.tool(app=True)
def customers() -> str:
    return "Customers"
```

Closes #5472.

title: fix: preserve CRLF descriptions in generated CLI parameter help
body:
`generate-cli` embeds parameter descriptions in Python source, but its hand-written escaping leaves carriage returns unescaped. Defaults, JSON argument decoding, and command behavior are unchanged.

For example, this parameter can now be used by the generated CLI without normalizing its description first:

```python
message: Annotated[str, Field(description="First line\r\nSecond line")]
```

Fixes #6074.

title: Serialize array and object OpenAPI path and cookie parameters instead of leaking Python reprs
body:
Path and cookie parameters from OpenAPI operations were serialized with `str()`, so an array path parameter went out as its Python repr (URL-encoded `['a', 'b']`) instead of the simple-style `a,b`, and array/object cookie values had the same problem. This serializes both locations in `RequestDirector.build`, next to the existing query-parameter serialization: scalars keep the true/false boolean convention, arrays join with commas, and objects serialize as key,value pairs, or key=value pairs with explode.

```python
director.build(route, {"ids": ["a", "b", "c"]})
# before: http://localhost/items/%5B%27a%27%2C%20%27b%27%2C%20%27c%27%5D
# after:  http://localhost/items/a%2Cb%2Cc  (one segment, decodes to a,b,c)
```

Fixes #6068

title: Discover skills through mounted servers
body:
## Description

Skills discovery breaks under composition. `SkillsExtension` must be registered by hand with an explicit `providers=[...]` list, so a parent that mounts a server with skills serves the files but answers `skills/list` with "server does not advertise the Skills extension".

This uses the existing provider-extension bubbling (`required_extensions` + `auto_register`). Skill providers bundle a `SkillsExtension`. When it's registered with no `providers`, it finds sources on its own server and through mounts, and it rewrites each mounted entry's URIs through the mount's namespaces. A mounted skill is listed only when the parent routes every file back to the child and passes the parent's access checks.

```python
child = FastMCP("Child", providers=[SkillCatalogProvider([review])])
parent = FastMCP("Parent")
parent.mount(child, namespace="team")
# parent's skills/list -> skill://team/review/SKILL.md
```

Decisions:
- `SkillsExtension(providers=[...])` still works. It limits discovery to those providers and doesn't include mounts.
- Providers with their own transforms, and servers with server-level transforms, are left out instead of raising, so auto-registration can never break a mount.

title: Make Skill a storage-neutral object with folders as one loader
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxks?thread=cmsg_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxksNQhfjgVek9vQzNnfU1emtj)_

## Description

FastMCP has no object for a skill itself. Skills exist only as folders on disk or as SEP-2640 wire records, so you can't define one in code or load one from a database.

This PR adds `fastmcp.skills.Skill`, an immutable bundle of exact file bytes. You can build one in code or load it with `from_directory`, `from_package` or `from_files`. `fastmcp.skills.provider.SkillCatalogProvider` serves skills as resources and as a `SkillsExtension` source. To load skills at request time, override `load_skills()`.

```python

mcp.add_extension(SkillsExtension(providers=[skills]))
```

title: fix(transforms): enforce wall-clock timeout and external callback limit in MontySandboxProvider and CodeMode
body:
### Summary
In FastMCP's experimental CodeMode, untrusted model-generated code runs in pydantic-monty sandbox while tool calls are bridged via asynchronous host callbacks. While Monty enforces instruction and feed duration limits internally, Monty's max_feed_duration_secs excludes time spent awaiting host callbacks. Consequently:
1. Long-running or hanging host callbacks are decoupled from sandbox time limits, allowing unbounded wall-clock execution.
2. Unbounded loops of external function calls can exhaust host threads or task queues if external call limits are not enforced.

This change:
1. Adds wall_clock_timeout_secs: float | None = None and max_external_calls: int | None = None to MontySandboxProvider.
2. Tracks external call invocations and raises RuntimeError if max_external_calls is exceeded, preventing host call exhaustion.
3. Enforces asyncio.wait_for around _run_monty and cleanly cancels the future and pending callback tasks when wall-clock timeout expires.
4. Adds wall_clock_timeout_secs to CodeMode, mapping sandbox timeout into a legible ToolError.
5. Adds unit tests covering max_external_calls, wall_clock_timeout_secs, and CodeMode timeout handling (100% test pass rate).

Resolves #4157

title: Serialize non-string OpenAPI header parameters instead of crashing
body:
Tools generated from OpenAPI operations with non-string header parameters crashed on every call: the input schema advertises the declared type (integer, boolean, array, ...), but request building passed the raw JSON value to httpx, which requires header values to be strings. Cookie parameters were already serialized during request building; header parameters were the gap. Fixes #6060.

`RequestDirector.build` now serializes header values before constructing the request, reusing the scalar conversion that query and cookie values already get (so booleans become `true`/`false`) and following the OpenAPI `simple` style — the default for header parameters — for arrays (comma-joined) and objects (key,value pairs, or key=value pairs with explode).

```python
# X-Count: integer, X-Flag: boolean, X-Tags: array of string
director.build(route, {"X-Count": 3, "X-Flag": True, "X-Tags": ["a", "b"]})
# headers: x-count: "3", x-flag: "true", x-tags: "a,b"
```

title: Fix resource templates with multiple query expressions
body:
Resource template query handling assumed a template contains exactly one `{?...}` expression. Parameters in any later block were dropped during matching, a `{&...}` continuation expression made the template unmatchable (it was treated as a path parameter with an invalid regex group name), and expansion emitted a second `?` instead of joining the blocks into one query string. Templates registered and listed fine in all three cases, so the failure only surfaced as missing arguments or "resource not found" at read time. Fixes #6059.

Query expressions are now scanned across the whole template: parameter extraction, path-pattern building, expansion, and proxy forwarding all treat `{?...}` and `{&...}` blocks uniformly, and expansion opens the query string once and continues it with `&`.

```python
@mcp.resource("data://{id}{?x}{&y}")
def get_data(id: str, x: str = "dx", y: str = "dy") -> str:
    return f"id={id} x={x} y={y}"

# read_resource("data://7?x=1&y=2") now returns "id=7 x=1 y=2"
```

title: fix: keep $defs referenced through escaped or sub-path pointers
body:
`compress_schema()` collects the `$defs` names a schema uses by reading each `$ref`'s last path segment. That is only the definition name for the simplest pointer, so three other legal forms pin nothing and their definitions get pruned, leaving dangling `$ref`s:

- percent-encoded names: `#/$defs/Alias%20One`
- JSON Pointer escapes: `#/$defs/a~1b` (`/`), `#/$defs/c~0d` (`~`)
- pointers that continue below a definition: `#/$defs/Container/properties/value`

## What changed

- New `_def_name_from_ref()` parses the first pointer token after `#/$defs/`, percent-decodes it and applies the RFC 6901 `~1` → `/`, `~0` → `~` unescaping. `_single_pass_optimize()` uses it instead of `ref.split("/")[-1]`.
- One regression test with all three pointer shapes plus a genuinely unused definition, asserting the four referenced names survive and `Unused` is still pruned.

## Verification

```
pytest tests/utilities/test_json_schema.py -q      # 73 passed
ruff format --check <both files>                   # 2 files already formatted
ruff check <both files>                            # All checks passed
```

- Red check with the source change stashed: `assert set(result["$defs"]) == {"Alias One", "a/b", "c~d", "Container"}` fails because every definition is pruned — the dangling-`$ref` case in the issue.
- Not run: the full suite (`uv run pytest -n auto`).

Fixes #6034

title: fix: report a missing prompt argument as invalid params
body:
Calling `prompts/get` without one of a prompt's required arguments returns JSON-RPC `-32603` (internal error), and with `mask_error_details=True` the missing argument names are stripped as well. The MCP spec lists "Missing required arguments" as `-32602` (invalid params), and tools already surface a validation error for the same mistake.

## Root cause

`FunctionPrompt.render` raised a bare `ValueError("Missing required arguments: ...")`. `FastMCP.render_prompt` catches anything that is not a `FastMCPError`/`MCPError` and wraps it in `PromptError` (masking the message when configured), and `to_mcp_error` maps `PromptError` to the default `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## What changed

- `FunctionPrompt.render` raises `ValidationError`, the class `to_mcp_error` already maps to `INVALID_PARAMS` (`fastmcp/exceptions.py`). Nothing else about the missing-argument check changes.
- Two regression tests build a prompt with a required argument and call `client.get_prompt(..., {})` with masking off and on: both assert code `-32602` and that the message names `topic`.
- One existing unit test (`test_fn_with_invalid_kwargs`) now expects `ValidationError` instead of `ValueError`, because a missing required argument is exactly the invalid-params case; it still asserts that rendering fails rather than proceeding.

## Verification

```
pytest tests/prompts/test_prompt.py -q      # 64 passed
pytest tests/test_exceptions.py -q          # 13 passed
ruff format --check <both files>            # 2 files already formatted
```

- Red check with the source change stashed: the two new tests fail with `assert -32603 == -32602`, and the masked variant reports the message as `"Error rendering prompt 'summarize'"` — the behavior from the issue.
- `ruff check` reports one finding at `fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/prompts/function_prompt.py:236` (`except Exception as e` with an unused binding); it is present on `main` too and untouched by this PR.
- Not run: the full suite (`uv run pytest -n auto`) and `prek`, which need the dev extras and pre-commit tooling this isolated install does not carry.

Fixes #6022

title: Fix generated CLIs for tools named app, console or Client
body:
Each tool becomes a module-level function named after the tool, so a tool can replace a name the generated script relies on. A tool named `app` replaced the cyclopts app, and `app()` at the bottom of the script then called the tool function, so every command, even `--help`, failed with `TypeError: app() missing 1 required keyword-only argument`. Tools named `console`, `Client`, `json` or `list` broke printing, connecting, JSON arguments or the script's own type annotations in the same way.

Tool functions are now named `tool_<name>`, so they can no longer replace the script's imports, globals or builtins. Only the Python function names in newly generated scripts change: cyclopts gets each command name from `name=`, so commands, flags and output stay the same. Renaming only on a collision would keep the old function names, but it needs a hand-kept list of every name the script template uses, which goes stale when the template changes; the prefix avoids that. Code that imports a generated script and calls a tool function directly would need the new name.

```bash
python cli.py --help
# before: TypeError: app() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'name'
# after:  the help lists the commands, and `call-tool app --name Notes` reaches the tool
```

Fixes #6055

title: Rename the resource-era list_skills helper to list_skill_summaries
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxks?thread=cmsg_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxksWVkPSipoGXPnEX8e3QmimV)_

FastMCP has two `list_skills`. `fastmcp.utilities.skills.list_skills(client)` scans `resources/list` for `skill://…/SKILL.md` and returns `SkillSummary` objects. `Client.list_skills()`, added with the Skills extension in 4.1.2, sends `skills/list` and returns full entries with manifests. Same name, different protocol, different results. On a server with discovery enabled they disagree on descriptions: the helper reports `Skill: <name>` because discovery-mode resources use generic descriptions.

The helper becomes `list_skill_summaries`, so `list_skills` means the protocol method. The old function stays as an alias that emits `FastMCPDeprecationWarning` and points at both replacements. `sync_skills` calls the new name. The Skills over MCP page (#6049) and the client page mention the new name.

```python
from fastmcp.utilities.skills import list_skill_summaries  # resources/list
skills = await client.list_skills()  # skills/list, with SkillsClientExtension
```

title: Consolidate skills docs into one Skills over MCP page
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zzstoatzz"} -->
_Requested by **nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxks?thread=cmsg_01THrtW7nMPpqRikagWCuxksWVkPSipoGXPnEX8e3QmimV)_

Skills had two pages that described one feature from opposite ends: "Skills Provider" (resources, 3.x) and "Experimental Skills Extension" (`skills/list` / `skills/get`, 4.1.2). Neither told a reader that one server does both, which client-side helper goes with which mode, or what discovery mode changes about the provider. People asking "how do skills over MCP work in FastMCP?" had no single link to send.

This replaces both with `/servers/skills`. It builds one server from a repo `skills/` folder and walks through it end to end: the folder layout and frontmatter rules, then serving the folder. From there it shows what a plain MCP client sees as resources, how to install the skills into a local agent with `sync_skills`, and how a discovery client lists entries and verifies each file against its SHA-256 manifest record. Provider options, the strict rules discovery mode applies, access control, and today's limits (no transforms, mounts or proxy forwarding for discovery) follow. Both old URLs redirect to the new page, and inbound links are updated.

```python
skills = SkillsDirectoryProvider(SKILLS_DIR, experimental_skills=True)
mcp.add_provider(skills)
mcp.add_extension(SkillsExtension(providers=[skills]))
```

Every Python block on the page was run against a live HTTP server built from the page's own example, and the output shown on the page is that run's. The page documents the API as released in 4.1.4, so it can be published now. #5788 and #5995 edit `experimental-skills.mdx`, so their docs changes should move to this page when they land.

title: Make the version-check InvalidURL regression independent of proxy parsing
body:
The upgrade checks fail with HTTPX 2.14 because the version-check regression assumes `NO_PROXY=[::1]` is invalid. The newer client accepts it, so the test reaches PyPI and can return a real version. Raise `httpx2.InvalidURL` at the mocked request boundary instead, preserving the #5638 error-handling regression without a network request or a dependency-specific proxy assumption. Production behavior is unchanged. Fixes #6040.

The version-check module passes all 27 tests with both HTTPX 2.12 and 2.14, and all static checks pass. The Linux unit run has 9,913 passes and one stdio-cancellation failure also reproduced on the unchanged base; the Windows ACL and conformance-launch failures likewise reproduce on that base. The remaining test groups hit a local 180-second limit. AI-assisted with Codex; reviewed and tested locally.
